live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:1: And now, my children, I know all things, for this is from Yahuah's (Lord’s) lips, and this my eyes have seen, from beginning to end.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:2: I know all things, and have written all things into books, the heavens and their end, and their plenitude, and all the armies and their marchings.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:3: I have measured and described the stars, the great countless multitude of them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:4: What man has seen their revolutions, and their entrances? For not even the angels see their number, while I have written all their names.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:5: And I measured the sun’s circle, and measured its rays, counted the hours, I wrote down too all things that go over the earth, I have written the things that are nourished, and all seed sown and unsown, which the earth produces and all plants, and every grass and every flower, and their sweet smells, and their names, and the dwelling-places of the clouds, and their composition, and their wings, and how they bear rain and raindrops.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:6: And I investigated all things, and wrote the road of the thunder and of the lightning, and they showed me the keys and their guardians, their rise, the way they go; it is let out gently in measure by a chain, lest by a heavy chain and violence it hurl down the angry clouds and destroy all things on earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:7: I wrote the treasure-houses of the snow, and the store-houses of the cold and the frosty airs, and I observed their season’s key-holder, he fills the clouds with them, and does not exhaust the treasure-houses.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:8: And I wrote the resting-places of the winds and observed and saw how their key-holders bear weighing-scales and measures; first, they put them in one weighing-scale, then in the other the weights and let them out according to measure cunningly over the whole earth, lest by heavy breathing they make the earth to rock.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:9: And I measured out the whole earth, its mountains, and all hills, fields, trees, stones, rivers, all existing things I wrote down, the height from earth to the seventh heaven, and downwards to the very lowest hell, and the judgment-place, and the very great, open and weeping hell.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:10: And I saw how the prisoners are in pain, expecting the limitless judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|40:11: And I wrote down all those being judged by the judge, and all their judgment and sentences and all their works.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|41:1: And I saw all forefathers from all time with Adam and Eva, and I sighed and broke into tears and said of the ruin of their dishonour:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|41:2: Woe is me for my infirmity and for that of my forefathers, and thought in my heart and said:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|41:3: Blessed is the man who has not been born or who has been born and shall not sin before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face, that he come not into this place, nor bring the yoke of this place.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|42:1: I saw the key-holders and guards of the gates of hell standing, like great serpents, and their faces like extinguishing lamps, and their eyes of fire, their sharp teeth, and I saw all Yahuah's (Lord’s) works, how they are right, while the works of man are some good, and others bad, and in their works are known those who lie evilly.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|43:1: I, my children, measured and wrote out every work and every measure and every righteous judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|43:2: As one year is more honourable than another, so is one man more honourable than another, some for great possessions, some for wisdom of heart, some for particular intellect, some for cunning, one for silence of lip, another for cleanliness, one for strength, another for comeliness, one for youth, another for sharp wit, one for shape of body, another for sensibility, let it be heard everywhere, but there is none better than he who fears Elohim (God), he shall be more glorious in time to come.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|44:1: Yahuah (Lord) with his hands having created man, in the likeness of his own face, Yahuah (Lord) made him small and great.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|44:2: Whoever reviles the ruler’s face, and abhors Yahuah's (Lord’s) face, has despised Yahuah's (Lord's) face, and he who vents anger on any man without injury, Yahuah's (Lord’s) great anger will cut him down, he who spits on the face of man reproachfully, will be cut down at Yahuah's (Lord’s) great judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|44:3: Blessed is the man who does not direct his heart with malice against any man, and helps the injured and condemned, and raises the broken down, and shall do charity to the needy, because on the day of the great judgment every weight, every measure and every makeweight will be as in the market, that is to say they are hung on scales and stand in the market, and every one shall learn his own measure, and according to his measure shall take his reward.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|45:1: Whoever hastens to make offerings before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face, Yahuah (Lord) for his part will hasten that offering by granting of his work.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|45:2: But whoever increases his lamp before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face and make not true judgment, Yahuah (Lord) will not increase his treasure in the realm of the highest.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|45:3: When Yahuah (Lord) demands bread, or candles, or the flesh of beasts, or any other sacrifice, then that is nothing; but Elohim (God) demands pure hearts, and with all that only tests the heart of man.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|46:1: Hear, my people, and take in the words of my lips.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|46:2: If any one bring any gifts to an earthly ruler, and have disloyal thoughts in his heart, and the ruler know this, will he not be angry with him, and not refuse his gifts, and not give him over to judgment?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|46:3: Or if one man make himself appear good to another by deceit of tongue, but have evil in his heart, then will not the other understand the treachery of his heart, and himself be condemned, since his untruth was plain to all?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|46:4: And when Yahuah (Lord) shall send a great light, then there will be judgment for the just and the unjust, and there no one shall escape notice.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:1: And now, my children, lay thought on your hearts, mark well the words of your father, which are all come to you from Yahuah's (Lord’s) lips.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:2: Take these books of your father’s handwriting and read them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:3: For the books are many, and in them you will learn all Yahuah's (Lord’s) works, all that has been from the beginning of creation, and will be till the end of time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:4: And if you will observe my handwriting, you will not sin against Yahuah (Lord); because there is no other except Yahuah (Lord), neither in heaven, nor in earth, nor in the very lowest places, nor in the one foundation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:5: Yahuah (Lord) has placed the foundations in the unknown, and has spread forth heavens visible and invisible; he fixed the earth on the waters, and created countless creatures, and who has counted the water and the foundation of the unfixed, or the dust of the earth, or the sand of the sea, or the drops of the rain, or the morning dew, or the wind’s breathings? Who has filled earth and sea, and the indissoluble winter?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|47:6: I cut the stars out of fire, and decorated heaven, and put it in their midst.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|55:4: Therefore I bid you do before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face all his good pleasure.
live.pseudepigrapha|4-maccabees|5:18: And you scoff at our philosophy, if under it we were living in a manner contrary to reason.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:1: That the sun go along the seven heavenly circles, which are the appointment of one hundred and eighty-two thrones, that it go down on a short day, and again one hundred and eighty-two, that it go down on a big day, and he has two thrones on which he rests, revolving hither and thither above the thrones of the months, from the seventeenth day of the month Tsivan it goes down to the month Thevan, from the seventeenth of Thevan it goes up.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:2: And thus it goes close to the earth, then the earth is glad and makes grow its fruits, and when it goes away, then the earth is sad, and trees and all fruits have no florescence.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:3: All this he measured, with good measurement of hours, and fixed a measure by his wisdom, of the visible and the invisible.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:4: From the invisible he made all things visible, himself being invisible.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:5: Thus I make known to you, my children, and distribute the books to your children, into all your generations, and amongst the nations who shall have the sense to fear Elohim (God), let them receive them, and may they come to love them more than any food or earthly sweets, and read them and apply themselves to them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:6: And those who understand not Yahuah (Lord), who fear not Elohim (God), who accept not, but reject, who do not receive the books, a terrible judgment awaits these.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|48:7: Blessed is the man who shall bear their yoke and shall drag them along, for he shall be released on the day of the great judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|49:1: I swear to you, my children, but I swear not by any oath, neither by heaven nor by earth, nor by any other creature which Elohim (God) created.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|49:2: Yahuah (Lord) said: There is no oath in me, nor injustice, but truth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|49:3: If there is no truth in men, let them swear by the words, Yea, yea, or else, Nay, nay.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|49:4: And I swear to you, yea, yea, that there has been no man in his mother’s womb, but that already before, even to each one there is a place prepared for the repose of that soul, and a measure fixed how much it is intended that a man be tried in this world.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|49:5: Yea, children, deceive not yourselves, for there has been previously prepared a place for every soul of man.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:1: I have put every man’s work in writing and none born on earth can remain hidden nor his works remain concealed.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:3: Now therefore, my children, in patience and meekness spend the number of your days, that you inherit endless life.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:4: Endure for the sake of Yahuah (Lord) every wound, every injury, every evil word and attack.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:5: If ill-requitals befall you, return them not either to neighbour or enemy, because Yahuah (Lord) will return them for you and be your avenger on the day of great judgment, that there be no avenging here among men.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:6: Whoever of you spends gold or silver for his brother’s sake, he will receive ample treasure in the world to come.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|50:7: Injure not widows nor orphans nor strangers, lest Elohim's (God’s) wrath come upon you.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:1: Stretch out your hands to the poor according to your strength.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:2: Hide not your silver in the earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:3: Help the faithful man in affliction, and affliction will not find you in the time of your trouble.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:4: And every grievous and cruel yoke that come upon you bear all for the sake of Yahuah (Lord), and thus you will find your reward in the day of judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:5: It is good to go morning, midday, and evening into Yahuah's (Lord’s) dwelling, for the glory of your creator.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|51:6: Because every breathing thing glorifies him, and every creature visible and invisible returns him praise.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:1: Blessed is the man who opens his lips in praise of Elohim (God) of Sabaoth and praises Yahuah (Lord) with his heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:2: Cursed every man who opens his lips for the bringing into contempt and calumny of his neighbour, because he brings Elohim (God) into contempt.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:3: Blessed is he who opens his lips blessing and praising Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:4: Cursed is he before Yahuah (Lord) all the days of his life, who opens his lips to curse and abuse.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:5: Blessed is he who blesses all Yahuah's (Lord’s) works.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:6: Cursed is he who brings Yahuah's (Lord’s) creation into contempt.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:7: Blessed is he who looks down and raises the fallen.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:8: Cursed is he who looks to and is eager for the destruction of what is not his.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:9: Blessed is he who keeps the foundations of his fathers made firm from the beginning.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:10: Cursed is he who perverts the decrees of his forefathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:11: Blessed is he who imparts peace and love.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:12: Cursed is he who disturbs those that love their neighbours.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:13: Blessed is he who speaks with humble tongue and heart to all.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:14: Cursed is he who speaks peace with his tongue, while in his heart there is no peace but a sword.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|52:15: For all these things will be laid bare in the weighing-scales and in the books, on the day of the great judgment.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|53:1: And now, my children, do not say: Our father is standing before Elohim (God), and is praying for our sins, for there is there no helper of any man who has sinned.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|53:2: You see how I wrote all works of every man, before his creation, all that is done amongst all men for all time, and none can tell or relate my handwriting, because Yahuah (Lord) see all imaginings of man, how they are vain, where they lie in the treasure-houses of the heart.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|53:3: And now, my children, mark well all the words of your father, that I tell you, lest you regret, saying: Why did our father not tell us?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|54:1: At that time, not understanding this let these books which I have given you be for an inheritance of your peace.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|54:2: Hand them to all who want them, and instruct them, that they may see Yahuah's (Lord’s) very great and marvellous works.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|55:1: My children, behold, the day of my term and time have approached.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|55:2: For the angels who shall go with me are standing before me and urge me to my departure from you; they are standing here on earth, awaiting what has been told them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|55:3: For to-morrow I shall go up on to heaven, to the uppermost Jerusalem to my eternal inheritance.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|56:1: Mathosalam having answered his father Enoch, said: What is agreeable to your eyes, father, that I may make before your face, that you may bless our dwellings, and your sons, and that your people may be made glorious through you, and then that you may depart thus, as Yahuah (Lord) said?
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|56:2: Enoch answered to his son Mathosalam and said: Hear, child, from the time when Yahuah (Lord) anointed me with the ointment of his glory, there has been no food in me, and my soul remembers not earthly enjoyment, neither do I want anything earthly.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|57:1: My child Methosalam, summon all your brethren and all your household and the elders of the people, that I may talk to them and depart, as is planned for me.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|57:2: And Methosalam made haste, and summoned his brethren, Regim, Riman, Uchan, Chermion, Gaidad, and all the elders of the people before the face of his father Enoch; and he blessed them, and said to them:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:1: Listen to me, my children, to-day.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:2: In those days when Yahuah (Lord) came down on to earth for Adam’s sake, and visited all his creatures, which he created himself, after all these he created Adam, and Yahuah (Lord) called all the beasts of the earth, all the reptiles, and all the birds that soar in the air, and brought them all before the face of our father Adam.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:3: And Adam gave the names to all things living on earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:4: And Yahuah (Lord) appointed him ruler over all, and subjected to him all things under his hands, and made them dumb and made them dull that they be commanded of man, and be in subjection and obedience to him.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:5: Thus also Yahuah (Lord) created every man lord over all his possessions.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:6: Yahuah (Lord) will not judge a single soul of beast for man’s sake, but adjudges the souls of men to their beasts in this world; for men have a special place.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|58:7: And as every soul of man is according to number, similarly beasts will not perish, nor all souls of beasts which Yahuah (Lord) created, till the great judgment, and they will accuse man, if he feed them ill.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:1: Whoever defiles the soul of beasts, defiles his own soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:2: For man brings clean animals to make sacrifice for sin, that he may have cure of his soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:3: And if they bring for sacrifice clean animals, and birds, man has cure, he cures his soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:4: All is given you for food, bind it by the four feet, that is to make good the cure, he cures his soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:5: But whoever kills beast without wounds, kills his own souls and defiles his own flesh.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|59:6: And he who does any beast any injury whatsoever, in secret, it is evil practice, and he defiles his own soul.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|60:1: He who works the killing of a man’s soul, kills his own soul, and kills his own body, and there is no cure for him for all time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|60:2: He who puts a man in any snare, shall stick in it himself, and there is no cure for him for all time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|60:3: He who puts a man in any vessel, his retribution will not be wanting at the great judgment for all time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|60:4: He who works crookedly or speaks evil against any soul, will not make justice for himself for all time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|61:1: And now, my children, keep your hearts from every injustice, which Yahuah (Lord) hates. Just as a man asks something for his own soul from Elohim (God), so let him do to every living soul, because I know all things, how in the great time to come there is much inheritance prepared for men, good for the good, and bad for the bad, without number many.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|61:2: Blessed are those who enter the good houses, for in the bad houses there is no peace nor return from them.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|61:3: Hear, my children, small and great! When man puts a good thought in his heart, brings gifts from his labours before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face and his hands made them not, then Yahuah (Lord) will turn away his face from the labour of his hand, and that man cannot find the labour of his hands.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|61:4: And if his hands made it, but his heart murmur, and his heart cease not making murmur incessantly, he has not any advantage.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|62:1: Blessed is the man who in his patience brings his gifts with faith before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face, because he will find forgiveness of sins.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|62:2: But if he take back his words before the time, there is no repentance for him; and if the time pass and he do not of his own will what is promised, there is no repentance after death.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|62:3: Because every work which man does before the time, is all deceit before men, and sin before Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|63:1: When man clothes the naked and fills the hungry, he will find reward from Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|63:2: But if his heart murmur, he commits a double evil; ruin of himself and of that which he gives; and for him there will be no finding of reward on account of that.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|63:3: And if his own heart is filled with his food and his own flesh, clothed with his own clothing, he commits contempt, and will forfeit all his endurance of poverty, and will not find reward of his good deeds.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|63:4: Every proud and magniloquent man is hateful to Yahuah (Lord), and every false speech, clothed in untruth; it will be cut with the blade of the sword of death, and thrown into the fire, and shall burn for all time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|64:1: When Enoch had spoken these words to his sons, all people far and near heard how Yahuah (Lord) was calling Enoch. They took counsel together:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|64:2: Let us go and kiss Enoch, and two thousand men came together and came to the place Achuzan where Enoch was, and his sons.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|64:3: And the elders of the people, the whole assembly, came and bowed down and began to kiss Enoch and said to him:
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|64:4: Our father Enoch, may you be blessed of Yahuah (Lord), the eternal ruler, and now bless your sons and all the people, that we may be glorified to-day before your face.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|64:5: For you shalt be glorified before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face for all time, since Yahuah (Lord) chose you, rather than all men on earth, and designated you writer of all his creation, visible and invisible, and redeemed of the sins of man, and helper of your household.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:1: And Enoch answered all his people saying: Hear, my children, before that all creatures were created, Yahuah (Lord) created the visible and invisible things.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:2: And as much time as there was and went past, understand that after all that he created man in the likeness of his own form, and put into him eyes to see, and ears to hear, and heart to reflect, and intellect wherewith to deliberate.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:3: And Yahuah (Lord) saw all man’s works, and created all his creatures, and divided time, from time he fixed the years, and from the years he appointed the months, and from the months he appointed the days, and of days he appointed seven.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:4: And in those he appointed the hours, measured them out exactly, that man might reflect on time and count years, months, and hours, their alternation, beginning, and end, and that he might count his own life, from the beginning until death, and reflect on his sin and write his work bad and good; because no work is hidden before Yahuah (Lord), that every man might know his works and never transgress all his commandments, and keep my handwriting from generation to generation.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:5: When all creation visible and invisible, as Yahuah (Lord) created it, shall end, then every man goes to the great judgment, and then all time shall perish, and the years, and thenceforward there will be neither months nor days nor hours, they will be adhered together and will not be counted.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:6: There will be one aeon, and all the righteous who shall escape Yahuah's (Lord’s) great judgment, shall be collected in the great aeon, for the righteous the great aeon will begin, and they will live eternally, and then too there will be amongst them neither labour, nor sickness, nor humiliation, nor anxiety, nor need, nor brutality, nor night, nor darkness, but great light.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|65:7: And they shall have a great indestructible wall, and a paradise bright and incorruptible, for all corruptible things shall pass away, and there will be eternal life.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:1: And now, my children, keep your souls from all injustice, such as Yahuah (Lord) hates.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:2: Walk before his face with terror and trembling and serve him alone.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:3: Bow down to the true Elohim (God), not to dumb idols, but bow down to his similitude, and bring all just offerings before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face. Yahuah (Lord) hates what is unjust.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:4: For Yahuah (Lord) sees all things; when man takes thought in his heart, then he counsels the intellects, and every thought is always before Yahuah (Lord), who made firm the earth and put all creatures on it.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:5: If you look to heaven, Yahuah Shammah (the Lord is there); if you take thought of the sea’s deep and all the under-earth, Yahuah Shammah (the Lord is there).
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:6: For Yahuah (Lord) created all things. Bow not down to things made by man, leaving Yahuah (Lord) of all creation, because no work can remain hidden before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:7: Walk, my children, in long-suffering, in meekness, honesty, in provocation, in grief, in faith and in truth, in reliance on promises, in illness, in abuse, in wounds, in temptation, in nakedness, in privation, loving one another, till you go out from this age of ills, that you become inheritors of endless time.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|66:8: Blessed are the just who shall escape the great judgment, for they shall shine forth more than the sun sevenfold, for in this world the seventh part is taken off from all, light, darkness, food, enjoyment, sorrow, paradise, torture, fire, frost, and other things; he put all down in writing, that you might read and understand.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|67:1: When Enoch had talked to the people, Yahuah (Lord) sent out darkness on to the earth, and there was darkness, and it covered those men standing with Enoch, and they took Enoch up on to the highest heaven, where Yahuah (Lord) is; and he received him and placed him before his face, and the darkness went off from the earth, and light came again.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|67:2: And the people saw and understood not how Enoch had been taken, and glorified Elohim (God), and found a roll in which was traced The Invisible Elohim (God); and all went to their dwelling places.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:1: Enoch was born on the sixth day of the month Tsivan, and lived three hundred and sixty-five years.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:2: He was taken up to heaven on the first day of the month Tsivan and remained in heaven sixty days.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:3: He wrote all these signs of all creation, which Yahuah (Lord) created, and wrote three hundred and sixty-six books, and handed them over to his sons and remained on earth thirty days, and was again taken up to heaven on the sixth day of the month Tsivan, on the very day and hour when he was born.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:4: As every man’s nature in this life is dark, so are also his conception, birth, and departure from this life.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:5: At what hour he was conceived, at that hour he was born, and at that hour too he died.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:6: Methosalam and his brethren, all the sons of Enoch, made haste, and erected an altar at that place called Achuzan, whence and where Enoch had been taken up to heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:7: And they took sacrificial oxen and summoned all people and sacrificed the sacrifice before Yahuah's (Lord’s) face.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:8: All people, the elders of the people and the whole assembly came to the feast and brought gifts to the sons of Enoch.
live.pseudepigrapha|2-enoch|68:9: And they made a great feast, rejoicing and making merry three days, praising Elohim (God), who had given them such a sign through Enoch, who had found favour with him, and that they should hand it on to their sons from generation to generation, from age to age.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:1: A narrative and revelation of Baruch, concerning those ineffable things which he saw by command of Elohim (God). Bless Thou, O Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:2: A revelation of Baruch, who stood upon the river Gel weeping over the captivity of Jerusalem, when also Abimelech was preserved by the hand of Elohim (God), at the farm of Agrippa. And he was sitting thus at the beautiful gates, where the Holy of holies lay.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:3: Verily I Baruch was weeping in my mind and sorrowing on account of the people, and that Nebuchadnezzar the king was permitted by Elohim (God) to destroy His city, saying: Yahuah (Lord), why didst Thou set on fire Thy vineyard, and lay it waste? Why didst Thou do this? And why, Yahuah (Lord), didst Thou not requite us with another chastisement, but didst deliver us to nations such as these, so that they reproach us and say, Where is their Elohim (God)?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:4: And behold as I was weeping and saying such things, I saw an angel of Yahuah (Lord) coming and saying to me: Understand, O man, greatly beloved, and trouble not thyself so greatly concerning the salvation of Jerusalem, for thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God), the Almighty. For He sent me before thee, to make known and to show to thee all (the things) of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:5: For thy prayer was heard before Him, and entered into the ears of Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:6: And when he had said these things to me, I was silent. And the angel said to me: Cease to provoke Elohim (God), and I will show thee other mysteries, greater than these.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:7: And I Baruch said, As Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) liveth, if thou wilt show me, and I hear a word of thine, I will not continue to speak any longer.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|1:8: Elohim (God) shall add to my judgement in the day of judgement, if I speak hereafter. And the angel of the powers said to me, Come, and I will show thee the mysteries of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:1: And he took me and led me where the firmament has been set fast, and where there was a river which no one can cross, nor any strange breeze of all those which Elohim (God) created.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:2: And he took me and led me to the first heaven, and showed me a door of great size. And he said to me, Let us enter through it, and we entered as though borne on wings, a distance of about thirty days' journey.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:3: And he showed me within the heaven a plain; and there were men dwelling thereon, with the faces of oxen, and the horns of stags, and the feet of goats, and the haunches of lambs.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:4: And I Baruch asked the angel, Make known to me, I pray thee, what is the thickness of the heaven in which we journeyed, or what is its extent, or what is the plain, in order that I may also tell the sons of men?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:5: And the angel whose name is Phamael said to me: This door which thou seest is the door of heaven, and as great as is the distance from earth to heaven, so great also is its thickness; and again as great as is the distance from North to South, so great is the length of the plain which thou didst see. And again the angel of the powers said to me, Come, and I will show thee greater mysteries.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:6: But I said, I pray thee show me what are these men.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|2:7: And he said to me, These are they who built the tower of strife against Elohim (God), and Yahuah (Lord) banished them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:1: And the angel of Yahuah (Lord) took me and led me to a second heaven. And he showed me there also a door like the first and said, Let us enter through it.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:2: And we entered, being borne on wings a distance of about sixty days' journey.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:3: And he showed me there also a plain, and it was full of men, whose appearance was like that of dogs, and whose feet were like those of stags.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:4: And I asked the angel: I pray thee, Yahuah (Lord), say to me who are these.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:5: And he said, These are they who gave counsel to build the tower, for they whom thou seest drove forth multitudes of both men and women, to make bricks; among whom, a woman making bricks was not allowed to be released in the hour of child-birth, but brought forth while she was making bricks, and carried her child in her apron, and continued to make bricks.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:6: And Yahuah (Lord) appeared to them and confused their speech, when they had built the tower to the height of four hundred and sixty-three cubits.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:7: And they took a gimlet, and sought to pierce the heaven, saying, Let us see (whether) the heaven is made of clay, or of brass, or of iron.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|3:8: When Elohim (God) saw this He did not permit them, but smote them with blindness and confusion of speech, and rendered them as thou seest.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:1: And I Baruch said, Behold, Yahuah (Lord), Thou didst show me great and wonderful things; and now show me all things for the sake of Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:2: And the angel said to me, Come, let us proceed. (And I proceeded) with the angel from that place about one hundred and eighty-five days' journey.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:3: And he showed me a plain and a serpent, which appeared to be two hundred plethra in length.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:4: And he showed me Hades, and its appearance was dark and abominable. And I said, Who is this dragon, and who is this monster around him?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:5: And the angel said, The dragon is he who eats the bodies of those who spend their life wickedly, and he is nourished by them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:6: And this is Hades, which itself also closely resembles him, in that it also drinks about a cubit from the sea, which does not sink at all.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:7: Baruch said, And how (does this happen)? And the angel said, Hearken, Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) made three hundred and sixty rivers, of which the chief of all are Alphias, Abyrus, and the Gericus; and because of these the sea does not sink. And I said, I pray thee show me which is the tree which led Adam astray.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:8: And the angel said to me, It is the vine, which the angel Sammael planted, whereat Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) was angry, and He cursed him and his plant, while also on this account He did not permit Adam to touch it, and therefore the devil being envious deceived him through his vine.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:9: And I Baruch said, Since also the vine has been the cause of such great evil, and is under judgement of the curse of Elohim (God), and was the destruction of the first created, how is it now so useful?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:10: And the angel said, Thou askest aright. When Elohim (God) caused the deluge upon earth, and destroyed all flesh, and four hundred and nine thousand giants, and the water rose fifteen cubits above the highest mountains, then the water entered into paradise and destroyed every flower; but it removed wholly without the bounds the shoot of the vine and cast it outside.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:11: And when the earth appeared out of the water, and Noah came out of the ark, he began to plant of the plants which he found.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:12: But he found also the shoot of the vine; and he took it, and was reasoning in himself, What then is it? And I came and spake to him the things concerning it.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:13: And he said, Shall I plant it, or what shall I do? Since Adam was destroyed because of it, let me not also meet with the anger of Elohim (God) because of it. And saying these things he prayed that Elohim (God) would reveal to him what he should do concerning it.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:14: And when he had completed the prayer which lasted forty days, and having besought many things and wept, he said: Yahuah (Lord), I entreat thee to reveal to me what I shall do concerning this plant.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:15: But Elohim (God) sent his angel Sarasael, and said to him, Arise, Noah, and plant the shoot of the vine, for thus saith Yahuah (Lord): Its bitterness shall be changed into sweetness, and its curse shall become a blessing, and that which is produced from it shall become the blood of Elohim (God); and as through it the human race obtained condemnation, so again through Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) the Immanuel will they receive in Him the upward calling, and the entry into paradise.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:16: Know therefore, O Baruch, that as Adam through this very tree obtained condemnation, and was divested of the glory of Elohim (God), so also the men who now drink insatiably the wine which is begotten of it, transgress worse than Adam, and are far from the glory of Elohim (God), and are surrendering themselves to the eternal fire.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|4:17: For (no) good comes through it. For those who drink it to surfeit do these things: neither does a brother pity his brother, nor a father his son, nor children their parents, but from the drinking of wine come all evils, such as murders, adulteries, fornications, perjuries, thefts, and such like. And nothing good is established by it.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|5:1: And I Baruch said to the angel, Let me ask thee one thing, Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|5:2: Since thou didst say to me that the dragon drinks one cubit out of the sea, say to me also, how great is his belly?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|5:3: And the angel said, His belly is Hades; and as far as a plummet is thrown (by) three hundred men, so great is his belly. Come, then, that I may show thee also greater works than these.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:1: And he took me and led me where the sun goes forth; and he showed me a chariot and four, under which burnt a fire, and in the chariot was sitting a man, wearing a crown of fire, (and) the chariot (was) drawn by forty angels.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:2: And behold a bird circling before the sun, about nine cubits away. And I said to the angel, What is this bird?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:3: And he said to me, This is the guardian of the earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:4: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), how is he the guardian of the earth? Teach me.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:5: And the angel said to me, This bird flies alongside of the sun, and expanding his wings receives its fiery rays.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:6: For if he were not receiving them, the human race would not be preserved, nor any other living creature. But Elohim (God) appointed this bird thereto.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:7: And he expanded his wings, and I saw on his right wing very large letters, as large as the space of a threshing-floor, the size of about four thousand modii; and the letters were of gold.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:8: And the angel said to me, Read them. And I read, and they ran thus: Neither earth nor heaven bring me forth, but wings of fire bring me forth.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:9: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), what is this bird, and what is his name? And the angel said to me, His name is called Phoenix.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:10: (And I said), And what does he eat? And he said to me, The manna of heaven and the dew of earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:11: And I said, Does the bird excrete? And he said to me, He excretes a worm, and the excrement of the worm is cinnamon, which kings and princes use. But wait and thou shalt see the glory of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:12: And while he was conversing with me, there was as a thunder-clap, and the place was shaken on which we were standing. And I asked the angel, My Lord, what is this sound? And the angel said to me, Even now the angels are opening the three hundred and sixty-five gates of heaven, and the light is being separated from the darkness.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:13: And a voice came which said, Light-giver, give to the world radiance.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:14: And when I heard the noise of the bird, I said, Yahuah (Lord), what is this noise?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:15: And he said, This is the bird who awakens from slumber the cocks upon earth. For as men do through the mouth, so also does the cock signify to those in the world, in his own speech.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|6:16: For the sun is made ready by the angels, and the cock crows.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:1: And I said, And where does the sun begin its labours, after the cock crows?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:2: And the angel said to me, Listen, Baruch: All things whatsoever I showed thee are in the first and second heaven, and in the third heaven the sun passes through and gives light to the world. But wait, and thou shalt see the glory of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:3: And while I was conversing with him, I saw the bird, and he appeared in front, and grew less and less, and at length returned to his full size.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:4: And behind him I saw the shining sun, and the angels which draw it, and a crown upon its head, the sight of which we were not able to gaze upon, and behold.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:5: And as soon as the sun shone, the Phoenix also stretched out his wings. But I, when I beheld such great glory, was brought low with great fear, and I fled and hid in the wings of the angel.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|7:6: And the angel said to me, Fear not, Baruch, but wait and thou shalt also see their setting.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:1: And he took me and led me towards the west; and when the time of the setting came, I saw again the bird coming before it, and as soon as he came I saw the angels, and they lifted the crown from its head.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:2: But the bird stood exhausted and with wings contracted.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:3: And beholding these things, I said, Yahuah (Lord), wherefore did they lift the crown from the head of the sun, and wherefore is the bird so exhausted?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:4: And the angel said to me, The crown of the sun, when it has run through the day—four angels take it, and bear it up to heaven, and renew it, because it and its rays have been defiled upon earth; moreover it is so renewed each day. And I Baruch said, Yahuah (Lord), and wherefore are its beams defiled upon earth?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:5: And the angel said to me, Because it beholds the lawlessness and unrighteousness of men, namely fornications, adulteries, thefts, extortions, idolatries, drunkenness, murders, strife, jealousies, evil-speakings, murmurings, whisperings, divinations, and such like, which are not well-pleasing to Elohim (God). On account of these things is it defiled, and therefore is it renewed.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:6: But thou askest concerning the bird, how it is exhausted. Because by restraining the rays of the sun through the fire and burning heat of the whole day, it is exhausted thereby.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|8:7: For, as we said before, unless his wings were screening the rays of the sun, no living creature would be preserved.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:1: And they having retired, the night also fell, and at the same time came the chariot of the moon, along with the stars.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:2: And I Baruch said, Yahuah (Lord), show me it also, I beseech of thee, how it goes forth, where it departs, and in what form it moves along.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:3: And the angel said, Wait and thou shalt see it also shortly. And on the morrow I also saw it in the form of a woman, and sitting on a wheeled chariot. And there were before it oxen and lambs in the chariot, and a multitude of angels in like manner.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:4: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), what are the oxen and the lambs? And he said to me, They also are angels.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:5: And again I asked, Why is it that it at one time increases, but at another time decreases?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:6: And (he said to me), Listen, O Baruch: This which thou seest had been written by Elohim (God) beautiful as no other.
live.pseudepigrapha|4-maccabees|9:4: For we esteem thy mercy, giving us our life in return for a breach of the Law, a thing harder to bear than death itself.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:7: And at the transgression of the first Adam, it was near to Sammael when he took the serpent as a garment. And it did not hide itself but increased, and Elohim (God) was angry with it, and afflicted it, and shortened its days.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|9:8: And I said, And how does it not also shine always, but only in the night? And the angel said, Listen: as in the presence of a king, the courtiers cannot speak freely, so the moon and the stars cannot shine in the presence of the sun; for the stars are always suspended, but they are screened by the sun, and the moon, although it is uninjured, is consumed by the heat of the sun.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:1: And when I had learnt all these things from the archangel, he took and led me into a fourth heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:2: And I saw a monotonous plain, and in the middle of it a pool of water. And there were in it multitudes of birds of all kinds, but not like those here on earth.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:3: But I saw a crane as great as great oxen; and all the birds were great beyond those in the world.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:4: And I asked the angel, What is the plain, and what the pool, and what the multitudes of birds around it?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:5: And the angel said, Listen, Baruch: The plain which contains in it the pool and other wonders is the place where the souls of the righteous come, when they hold converse, living together in choirs.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:6: But the water is that which the clouds receive, and rain upon the earth, and the fruits increase.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:7: And I said again to the angel of Yahuah (Lord), But (what) are these birds? And he said to me, They are those which continually sing praise to Yahuah (Lord).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:8: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), and how do men say that the water which descends in rain is from the sea?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:9: And the angel said, The water which descends in rain—this also is from the sea, and from the waters upon earth; but that which stimulates the fruits is (only) from the latter source.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|10:10: Know therefore henceforth that from this source is what is called the dew of heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:1: And the angel took me and led me thence to a fifth heaven. And the gate was closed.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:2: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), is not this gate-way open that we may enter? And the angel said to me, We cannot enter until Michael comes, who holds the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven; but wait and thou shalt see the glory of Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:3: And there was a great sound, as thunder. And I said, Yahuah (Lord), what is this sound?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:4: And he said to me, Even now Michael, the commander of the angels, comes down to receive the prayers of men.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:5: And behold a voice came, Let the gates be opened. And they opened them, and there was a roar as of thunder.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:6: And Michael came, and the angel who was with me came face to face with him and said, Hail, my commander, and that of all our order.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:7: And the commander Michael said, Hail thou also, our brother, and the interpreter of the revelations to those who pass through life virtuously.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:8: And having saluted one another thus, they stood still. And I saw the commander Michael, holding an exceedingly great vessel; its depth was as great as the distance from heaven to earth, and its breadth as great as the distance from north to south.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|11:9: And I said, Yahuah (Lord), what is that which Michael the archangel is holding? And he said to me, This is where the merits of the righteous enter, and such good works as they do, which are escorted before the heavenly Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:1: And as I was conversing with them, behold angels came bearing baskets full of flowers. And they gave them to Michael.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:2: And I asked the angel, Yahuah (Lord), who are these, and what are the things brought hither from beside them?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:3: And he said to me, These are angels (who) are over the righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:4: And the archangel took the baskets, and cast them into the vessel.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:5: And the angel said to me, These flowers are the merits of the righteous.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:6: And I saw other angels bearing baskets which were (neither) empty nor full. And they began to lament, and did not venture to draw near, because they had not the prizes complete.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:7: And Michael cried and said, Come hither, also, ye angels, bring what ye have brought.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|12:8: And Michael was exceedingly grieved, and the angel who was with me, because they did not fill the vessel.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|13:1: And then came in like manner other angels weeping and bewailing, and saying with fear, Behold how we are overclouded, O Yahuah (Lord), for we were delivered to evil men, and we wish to depart from them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|13:2: And Michael said, Ye cannot depart from them, in order that the enemy may not prevail to the end; but say to me what ye ask.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|13:3: And they said, We pray thee, Michael our commander, transfer us from them, for we cannot abide with wicked and foolish men, for there is nothing good in them, but every kind of unrighteousness and greed.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|13:4: For we do not behold them entering [into Church at all, nor among spiritual fathers, nor] into any good work. But where there is murder, there also are they in the midst, and where are fornications, adulteries, thefts, slanders, perjuries, jealousies, drunkenness, strife, envy, murmurings, whispering, idolatry, divination, and such like, then are they workers of such works, and of others worse.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|13:5: Wherefore we entreat that we may depart from them. And Michael said to the angels, Wait till I learn from Yahuah (Lord) what shall come to pass.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|14:1: And in that very hour Michael departed, and the doors were closed. And there was a sound as thunder.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|14:2: And I asked the angel, What is the sound? And he said to me, Michael is even now presenting the merits of men to Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|15:1: And in that very hour Michael descended, and the gate was opened; and he brought oil.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|15:2: And as for the angels which brought the baskets which were full, he filled them with oil, saying, Take it away, reward our friends an hundredfold, and those who have laboriously wrought good works.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|15:3: For those who sowed virtuously, also reap virtuously. And he said also to those bringing the half-empty baskets, Come hither ye also; take away the reward according as ye brought, and deliver it to the sons of men.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|15:4: [Then he said also to those who brought the full and to those who brought the half-empty baskets: Go and bless our friends, and say to them that thus saith Yahuah (Lord), Ye are faithful over a few things, I will set you over many things; enter into the joy of your Lord.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|16:1: And turning he said also to those who brought nothing: Thus saith Yahuah (Lord), Be not sad of countenance, and weep not, nor let the sons of men alone.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|16:2: But since they angered me in their works, go and make them envious and angry and provoked against a people that is no people, a people that has no understanding.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|16:3: Further, besides these, send forth the caterpillar and the unwinged locust, and the mildew, and the common locust (and) hail with lightnings and anger, and punish them severely with the sword and with death, and their children with demons.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|16:4: For they did not hearken to my voice, nor did they observe my commandments, nor do them, but were despisers of my commandments, and insolent towards the priests who proclaimed my words to them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|17:1: And while he yet spake, the door was closed, and we withdrew.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|17:2: And the angel took me and restored me to the place where I was at the beginning.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|17:3: And having come to myself, I gave glory to Elohim (God), who counted me worthy of such honour.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-baruch|17:4: Wherefore do ye also, brethren, who obtained such a revelation, yourselves also glorify Elohim (God), so that He also may glorify you, now and ever, and to all eternity. Amen.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:1: Now Philopater, on learning from those who came back that Antiochus had made himself master of the places which belonged to himself, sent orders to all his footmen and horsemen, took with him his sister Arsinoe, and marched out as far as the parts of Raphia, where Antiochus and his forces encamped.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:2: And one Theodotus, intending to carry out his design, took with him the bravest of the armed men who had been before committed to his trust by Ptolemy, and got through at night to the tent of Ptolemy, to kill him on his own responsibility, and so to end the war.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:3: But Dositheus, called the son of Drimulus, by birth a Yahudi (Jew), afterward a renegade from the laws and observances of his country, conveyed Ptolemy away, and made an obscure person lie down in his stead in the tent. It befel this man to receive the fate which was meant for the other.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:4: A fierce battle then took place; and the men of Antiochus prevailing, Arsinoe continually went up and down the ranks, and with dishevelled hair, with tears and entreaties, begged the soldiers to fight manfully for themselves, their children, and wives; and promised that if they proved conquerors, she would give them two minæ of gold apiece.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:5: It thus fell out that their enemies were defeated in hand-to-hand encounter, and that many of them were taken prisoners.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:6: Having vanquished this attempt, the king then decided to proceed to the neighbouring cities, and encourage them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:7: By doing this, and by making donations to their temples, he inspired his subjects with confidence.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:8: The Yahudim (Jews) also sent some of their council and of their elders to him. The greetings, guest-gifts, and congratulations on the past, bestowed by them, filled him with the greater eagerness to visit their city.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:9: Having arrived at Jerusalem, sacrificed, and offered thank-offerings to the Greatest Elohim (God), and done whatever else was suitable to the sanctity of the place, and entered the inner court,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:10: he was so struck with the exact magnificence of the place, and so wondered at the orderly arrangements of the temple, that he conceived the purpose of entering the sanctuary itself.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:11: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:12: Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying, Be it that they were deprived of this honour, I ought not to be.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:13: And he put the question, Why, when he entered all temples, none of the priests who were present forbad him?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:14: He was thoughtlessly answered by some one, That he did wrong to boast of this.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:15: Well; since I have done this, said he, be the cause what it may, shall I not enter with or without your consent?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:16: And when the priests fell down in their sacred vestments imploring the Greatest Elohim (God) to come and help in time of need, and to avert the violence of the fierce aggressor, and when they filled the temple with lamentations and tears,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:17: then those who had been left behind in the city were scared, and rushed forth, uncertain of the event.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:18: Virgins, who had been shut up within their chambers, came out with their mothers, scattering dust and ashes on their heads, and filling the streets with outcries.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:19: Women, but recently separated off, left their bridal chambers, left the reserve that befitted them, and ran about the city in a disorderly manner.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:20: Newborn babes were deserted by the mothers or nurses who waited upon them; some here, some there, in houses, or in fields; these now, with an ardour which could not be checked, swarmed into the El Elyon (Most High) temple.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:21: Various were the prayers offered up by those who assembled in this place, on account of the unholy attempt of the king.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:22: Along with these there were some of the citizens who took courage, and would not submit to his obstinacy, and his intention of carrying out his purpose.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:23: Calling out to arms, and to die bravely in defence of the law of their fathers, they created a great uproar in the place, and were with difficulty brought back by the aged and the elders to the station of prayer which they had occupied before.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:24: During this time the multitude kept on praying.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:25: The elders who surrounded the king strove in many ways to divert his haughty mind from the design which he had formed.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:26: He, in his hardened mood, insensible to all persuasion, was going onwards, with the view of carrying out this design.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:27: Yet even his own officers, when they saw this, joined the Yahudim (Jews) in an appeal to Him who has all power, to aid in the present crisis, and not wink at such overweening lawlessness.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:28: Such was the frequency and the vehemence of the cry of the assembled crowd, that an indescribable noise ensued.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|1:29: Not the men only, the very walls and floor seemed to sound forth; all things preferring dissolution rather than to see the place defiled.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:1: Now was it that the high priest Simon bowed his knees over against the holy place, and spread out his hands in reverent form, and uttered the following supplication:
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:2: O Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord), King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exulteth in his confidence and strength.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:3: It is thou, the Creator of all, Yahuah (Lord) of the universe, who art a righteous Governor, and judgest all who act with pride and insolence.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:4: It was thou who didst destroy the former workers of unrighteousness, among whom were the giants, who trusted in their strength and hardihood, by covering them with a measureless flood.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:5: It was thou who didst make the Sodomites, those workers of exceeding iniquity, men notorious for their vices, an example to after generations, when thou didst consume them with fire and brimstone.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:6: Thou didst make known thy power when thou causedst the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of thy people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:7: And thou rolledst the depths of the sea over him, when he made pursuit with chariots, and with a multitude of followers, and gavest a safe passage to those who put their trust in thee, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:8: These saw and felt the works of thine hands, and praised thee the Almighty.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:9: Thou, O King, when thou createdst the illimitable and measureless earth, didst choose out this city: thou didst make this place sacred to thy name, albeit thou needest nothing: thou didst glorify it with thy illustrious presence, after constructing it to the glory of thy great and honourable name.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:10: And thou didst promise, out of love to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that should we fall away from thee, and become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, thou wouldest hear our prayer.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:11: Verily thou art faithful and true.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:12: And whereas thou didst often aid our fathers when hard pressed, and in low estate, and deliveredst them out of great dangers,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:13: see now, holy King, how through our many and great sins we are borne down, and made subject to our enemies, and are become weak and powerless.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:14: We being in this low condition, this bold and profane man seeks to dishonour this thy holy place, consecrated out of the earth to the name of thy Majesty.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:15: Thy dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:16: But since it seemed good to thee to exhibit thy glory among thy people Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst sanctify this place.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:17: Punish us not by means of the uncleanness of their men, nor chastise us by means of their profanity; lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:18: We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:19: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and shew forth thy compassion in this hour.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:20: Let thy mercies quickly go before us. Grant us peace, that the cast down and broken hearted may praise thee with their mouth.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:21: At that time Elohim (God), who seeth all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable; and scourged the man greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:22: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:23: His friends and body-guards, beholding the swift recompense which had suddenly overtaken him, struck with exceeding terror, and fearing that he would die, speedily removed him.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:24: When in course of time he had come to himself, this severe check caused no repentance within him, but he departed with bitter threatenings.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:25: He proceeded to Egypt, grew worse in wickedness through his beforementioned companions in wine, who were lost to all goodness;
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:26: and not satisfied with countless acts of impiety, his audacity so increased that he raised evil reports there, and many of his friends, watching his purpose attentively, joined in furthering his will.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:27: His purpose was to inflict a public stigma upon our race; wherefore he erected a pillar at the tower-porch, and caused the following inscription to be engraven upon it:
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:28: That entrance to their own temple was to be refused to all those who would not sacrifice; that all the Yahudim (Jews) were to be registered among the common people; that those who resisted were to be forcibly seized and put to death;
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:29: that those who were thus registered, were to be marked on their persons by the ivy-leaf symbol of Dionysus, and to be set apart with these limited rights.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:30: To do away with the appearance of hating them all, he had it written underneath, that if any of them should elect to enter the community of those initiated in the rites, these should have equal rights with the Alexandrians.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:31: Some of those who were over the city, therefore, abhorring any approach to the city of piety, unhesitatingly gave in to the king, and expected to derive some great honour from a future connection with him.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:32: A nobler spirit, however, prompted the majority to cling to their religious observances, and by paying money that they might live unmolested, these sought to escape the registration:
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|2:33: cheerfully looking forward to future aid, they abhorred their own apostates, considering them to be national foes, and debarring them from the common usages of social intercourse.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:1: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:2: While this was going on, an invidious rumour was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi (Jewish) race. The purport of their charge was, that the Yahudim (Jews) kept them away from the ordinances of the law.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:3: Now, while the Yahudim (Jews) always maintained a feeling of unswerving loyalty towards the kings,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:4: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:5: although, as they adorned their conversation with works of righteousness, they had established themselves in the good opinion of the world.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:6: What all the rest of mankind said, was, however, made of no account by the foreigners;
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:7: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:8: Nor was this unexpected uproar and sudden conflux of people unobserved by the Greeks who lived in the city, concerning men who had never harmed them: yet to aid them was not in their power, since all was oppression around; but they encouraged the Yahudim (Jews) by sympathizing with them in their troubles, and expected a favourable turn of affairs:
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:9: He who knoweth all things, will not, said they , disregard so great a people.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:10: Some of the neighbours, friends, and fellow dealers of the Yahudim (Jews), even called them secretly to an interview, pledged them their assistance, and promised to do their very utmost for them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:11: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:12: King Ptolemy Philopater, to the commanders and soldiers in Egypt, and in all places, health and happiness!
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:13: I am right well; and so, too, are my affairs.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:14: Since our Asiatic campaign, the particulars of which ye know, and which by the aid of the gods, not lightly given, and by our own vigour, has been brought to a successful issue according to our expectation,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:15: we resolved, not with strength of spear, but with gentleness and much humanity, as it were to nurse the inhabitants of Cœle-Syria and Phœnicia, and to be their willing benefactors.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:16: So, having bestowed considerable sums of money upon the temples of the several cities, we proceeded even as far as Jerusalem; and went up to honour the temple of these wretched beings who never cease from their folly.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:17: To outward appearance they received us willingly; but belied that appearance by their deeds. When we were eager to enter their temple, and to honour it with the most beautiful and exquisite gifts,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:18: they were so carried away by their old arrogance, as to forbid us the entrance; while we, out of our forbearance toward all men, refrained from exercising our power upon them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:19: And thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any thing reasonable.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:20: We then, having endeavoured to make allowance for the madness of these persons, and on our victorious return treating all people in Egypt courteously, acted in a manner which was befitting.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:21: Accordingly, bearing no ill-will against their kinsmen [at Jerusalem], but rather remembering our connection with them, and the numerous matters with sincere heart from a remote period entrusted to them, we wished to venture a total alteration of their state, by bestowing upon them the rights of citizens of Alexandria, and to admit them to the everlasting rites of our solemnities.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:22: All this, however, they have taken in a very different spirit. With their innate malignity, they have spurned the fair offer; and constantly inclining to evil,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:23: have rejected the inestimable rights. Not only so, but by using speech, and by refraining from speech, they abhor the few among them who are heartily disposed towards us; ever deeming that their ignoble course of procedure will force us to do away with our reform.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:24: Having then, received certain proofs that these Yahudim (Jews) bear us every sort of ill-will, we must look forward to the possibility of some sudden tumult among ourselves, when these impious men may turn traitors and barbarous enemies.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:25: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:26: For by the punishment of them in one body we perceive that we have found the only means of establishing our affairs for the future on a firm and satisfactory basis.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:27: Whoever shall shield a Yahudi (Jew), whether it be old man, child, or suckling, shall with his whole house be tortured to death.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:28: Whoever shall inform against the Yahudim (Jews) , besides receiving the property of the person charged, shall be presented with two thousand drachmæ from the royal treasury, shall be made free, and shall be crowned.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:29: Whatever place shall shelter a Yahudi (Jew), shall, when he is hunted forth, be put under the ban of fire, and be for ever rendered useless to every living being for all time to come.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|3:30: Such was the purport of the king's letter.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:1: Wherever this decree was received, the people kept up a revelry of joy and shouting; as if their long-pent-up, hardened hatred, were now to shew itself openly.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:2: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:3: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:4: They were sent out unanimously by the generals in the several cities, with such stern and pitiless feeling, that the exceptional nature of the infliction moved even some of their enemies. These, influenced by sentiments of common humanity, and reflecting upon the uncertain issue of life, shed tears at this their miserable expulsion.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:5: A multitude of aged hoary-haired men, were driven along with halting bending feet, urged onward by the impulse of a violent, shameless force to quick speed.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:6: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:7: Bound, and exposed to public gaze, they were hurried violently on board ship.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:8: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.
live.pseudepigrapha|4-maccabees|9:5: Thou wouldst terrify us with thy threats of death under torture, as if a little while ago thou hadst learned nothing from Eleazar.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:9: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:10: The planks of the deck above them barred out the light, and shut out the day on every side, so that they might be treated like traitors during the whole voyage.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:11: They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:12: When this was done, the king, hearing that their brethren in the city often went out and lamented the melancholy distress of these victims,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:13: was full of rage, and commanded that they should be carefully subjected to the same (and not one whit milder) treatment.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:14: The whole nation was now to be registered. Every individual was to be specified by name; not for that hard servitude of labour which we have a little before mentioned, but that he might expose them to the before-mentioned tortures; and finally, in the short space of a day, might extirpate them by his cruelties.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:15: The registering of these men was carried on cruelly, zealously, assiduously, from the rising of the sun to its going down, and was not brought to an end in forty days.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:16: The king was filled with great and constant joy, and celebrated banquets before the temple idols. His erring heart, far from the truth, and his profane mouth, gave glory to idols, deaf and incapable of speaking or aiding, and uttered unworthy speech against the Greatest Elohim (God).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:17: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) was too great for registration,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:18: inasmuch as there were many still left in the land, of whom some were in inhabited houses, and others were scattered about in various places; so that all the commanders in Egypt were insufficient for the work.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:19: The king threatened them, and charged them with taking bribes, in order to contrive the escape of the Yahudim (Jews) : but was clearly convinced of the truth of what had been said.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:20: They said, and proved, that paper and pens had failed them for the carrying out of their purpose.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|4:21: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|5:1: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|5:2: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Yahudim (Jews).
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|5:3: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim (Jews) the most.
live.pseudepigrapha|3-maccabees|5:4: The master of the elephants, Hermon, fulfilled his commission punctually.
