live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|127:5: And after the death of Jacob my father I loved them 'more abundantly', and all things whatsoever he commanded I did 'very abundantly' for them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|127:6: And I suffered them not to be afflicted even in the smallest matter; and all that was in my hand I gave unto them.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|127:7: 'And' their children were my children, and my children as their servants; and their life was my life, and all their suffering was my suffering, 'and all their sickness was my infirmity'. My land was their land, and their counsel my counsel.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|127:8: And I exalted not myself among them 'in arrogance' because of my 'worldly' glory, but I was among them as one of the least.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|128:1: If ye also, therefore, walk in the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), my children, He will exalt you there, and will bless you with good things for ever and ever.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|128:2: 'And if any one seeketh to do evil unto you, do well unto him, and pray for him, and ye shall be redeemed of Yahuah (Lord) from all evil'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|128:3: 'For', behold, ye see that 'out of my humility and long-suffering' I took unto wife the daughter of the priest of Heliopolis. And a hundred talents of gold were given me with her, and Yahuah (Lord) made them to serve me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|128:4: And He gave me also beauty as a flower beyond the beautiful ones of Yashar'el (Israel); and He preserved me 'unto old age in strength and' in beauty, because I was like in all things to Jacob.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:1: And hear ye, my children, also the vision which I saw.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:2: There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:3: And I saw that the three harts became three lambs, and they cried to Yahuah (Lord), and He brought them forth into a flourishing and well-watered place, yea He brought them out of darkness into light.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:4: And there they cried unto Yahuah (Lord) until there gathered together to them the nine harts, and they became as twelve sheep, and after a little time they increased and became many flocks.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:5: And after these things I saw and behold, twelve bulls were sucking one cow, which produced a sea of milk, and there drank thereof the twelve flocks and innumerable herds.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:6: And the horns of the fourth bull went up unto heaven and became as a wall for the flocks, and in the midst of the [two] horns there grew another horn.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:7: And I saw a bull calf which surrounded them twelve times, and it became a help to the bulls wholly.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:8: And I saw that [from Yahudah (Judah) was born] a virgin [wearing a linen garment, and from her] was born a lamb, [without spot]; and on his left hand there was as it were a lion; and all the beasts rushed against him, and the lamb overcame them, and destroyed them and trod them under foot.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:9: And because of him the angels and men rejoiced, and all the land.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:10: And these things shall come to pass in their season, in the last days.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:11: Do ye therefore, my children, observe the commandments of Yahuah (Lord), and honour Levi and Yahudah (Judah); for from them shall arise 'unto you' [the Lamb of Elohim (God), who taketh away the sin of the world] one who saveth [all the Gentiles and] Yashar'el (Israel).
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|129:12: For his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, which shall not pass away; but my kingdom among you shall come to an end as a watcher's hammock, which after the summer disappeareth.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:1: 'For' I know that after my death the Egyptians will afflict you, but Elohim (God) will avenge you, and will bring you into that which He promised to your fathers.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:2: But ye shall carry up my bones with you; 'for when my bones are being taken up thither, Yahuah (Lord) shall be with you in light, and Beliar shall be in darkness with the Egyptians'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:3: And carry ye up Asenath your mother [to the Hippodrome], and near Rachel your mother bury her.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:4: And when he had said these things he stretched out his feet, and died at a good old age.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:5: And all Yashar'el (Israel) mourned for him, and all Egypt, with a great mourning.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|130:6: And when the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went out of Egypt, they took with them the bones of Joseph, and they buried him in Hebron with his fathers, and the years of his life were one hundred and ten years.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:1: The copy of the words of Benjamin, which he commanded his sons to observe, after he had lived a hundred and twenty-five years.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:2: And he kissed them, and said: As Isaac was born to Abraham in his old age, so also was I to Jacob.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:3: And since Rachel my mother died in giving me birth, I had no milk; therefore I was suckled by Bilhah her handmaid.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:4: For Rachel remained barren for twelve years 'after she had borne Joseph'; and she prayed Yahuah (Lord) with fasting twelve days, and she conceived and bare me.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:5: For 'my father' loved Rachel dearly, 'and prayed that he might see two sons born from her'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|131:6: Therefore was I called Benjamin, that is, a son of days.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|132:1: And when I went into Egypt, 'to Joseph, and my brother recognised me, he said' unto me: What did they tell my father when they sold me?
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|132:2: And I said 'unto him', They dabbled thy coat with blood and sent it, and said: Know whether this be thy son's coat.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|132:3: And he said unto me: Even so, brother, when they had stripped me of my coat they gave me to the Ishmaelites, and they gave me a loin cloth, and scourged me, and bade me run.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|132:4: And as for one of them that had beaten me with a rod, a lion met him and slew him.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|132:5: And so his associates were affrighted.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|133:1: Do ye also, therefore, my children, love Yahuah Elohim (the Lord God) of heaven and earth, and keep His commandments, following the example of the good and holy man 'Joseph'.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|133:2: And let your mind be unto good, even as ye know me; for he that hath his mind right, seeth all things rightly.
live.pseudepigrapha|testaments-xii|133:3: Fear ye Yahuah (Lord), and love your neighbour; and even though the spirits of Beliar claim you to afflict you with every evil, yet shall they not have dominion over you, even as they had not over Joseph my brother.

cards.note: *On the third day, Elohim (God) planted the garden in the east of the earth.* The first Book of Adam and Eve opens at the Genesis garden — the Adamic origin Matthew's *book of the generation* echoes. The Hebrew library's extended Adamic narrative sets the stage for the second-Adam genealogy at Matt 1:1.
cards.s_text: The book of the generation of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the son of David, the son of Abraham.
cards.t_text: On the third day, Elohim (God) planted the garden in the east of the earth, on the border of the world eastward, beyond which, towards the sun-rising, one finds nothing but water, that encompasses the whole world, and reaches to the borders of heaven.

cards.note: *Now Er was wicked, and he was in need concerning Tamar.* The Testament of Yahudah (Judah) — chapters 24-39 of the Testaments XII — narrates the Tamar episode in Yahudah's own voice, his deathbed testament to his sons. The patriarch himself, in the Hebrew library's pseudepigraphal voice, walks the same narrative Matt 1:3 names with the words *Yahudah (Judah) begat Phares and Zara of Thamar.*
cards.s_text: And Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar; and Phares begat Esrom; and Esrom begat Aram;
cards.t_text: Now Er was wicked, and he 'was in need' concerning Tamar, because she was not of the land of Canaan. And on the third night an angel of Yahuah (Lord) smote him.

cards.note: The Testament of Yoseph (Joseph) — Testaments XII chapters 72-87 — opens the patriarchal-Yoseph's deathbed words to his sons. The Matthean Yoseph at Matt 1:18-25 carries the patriarchal-Yoseph's role: the dreamer (Genesis 37), the Egypt-carrier (Genesis 46), the preserver of the covenant line. Matthew echoes the patriarchal pattern by name.
cards.s_text: Now the birth of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).
cards.t_text: The copy of the testament of Joseph. When he was about to die he called his sons and his brethren together, and said to them:

cards.note: *For Yahuah (Lord) shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah (Judah) as it were a King, Elohim (God) and man.* Simeon Chapter 5 (Testaments XII ch 11) names the Levitical-priest + Yahudite-king Messiah explicitly — *Elohim (God) and man.* Matthew's genealogy at Matt 1:1 names David (the kingship promise) and Avraham (Abraham) (the seed-promise); the priestly side comes through the same line. The Hebrew library knew the doubled identity before the gospel announced it.
cards.s_text: The book of the generation of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the son of David, the son of Abraham.
cards.t_text: For Yahuah (Lord) shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah (Judah) as it were a King [Elohim (God) and man], He shall save all [the Gentiles and] the race of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *In the second jubilee, he that is anointed shall be conceived in the sorrow of beloved ones.* Levi Chapter 9 (Testaments XII ch 20) names the conception of the anointed one in advance — the same conception narrative Matt 1:18-25 walks. The Hebrew library's pseudepigraphal witness to the Messianic conception prepares the apostolic apposition *they shall call his name Immanuel — Elohim (God) with us* at Matt 1:23.
cards.s_text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.
cards.t_text: In the second jubilee, he that is anointed shall be conceived in the sorrow of beloved ones; and his priesthood shall be honoured and shall be glorified by all.

cards.note: *And there shall arise in the latter days one beloved of Yahuah (Lord), of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) and Levi.* Benjamin Chapter 9 (Testaments XII ch 96) — the closing testament of the youngest tribe — names the Beloved who shall arise in the latter days from the doubled-tribal lineage. Matthew 1:1's genealogical opening lands on the Beloved Benjamin named.
cards.s_text: The book of the generation of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the son of David, the son of Abraham.
cards.t_text: And there shall arise in the latter days] one beloved of Yahuah (Lord), [of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) and Levi], a doer of His good pleasure in his mouth, [with new knowledge enlightening the Gentiles].

cards.note: *And I indeed saw a woman of the family of David the prophet, named Mary, and Virgin, and she was espoused to a man named Joseph, a carpenter, and he also was of the seed and family of the righteous David.* The Ascension of Isaiah's extracanonical witness to the virgin-conception narrative — Mary and Joseph both of David's line, the virgin-conception named, the Davidic descent affirmed. The Hebrew library's seventh-heaven vision lands the same narrative Matt 1:18-25 walks in earthly time.
cards.s_text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.
cards.t_text: And I indeed saw a woman of the family of David the prophet, named Mary, and Virgin, and she was espoused to a man named Joseph, a carpenter, and he also was of the seed and family of the righteous David of Bethlehem Yahudah (Judah).

cards.note: *Go forth and descend through all the heavens, and thou wilt descend to the firmament and that world.* The Father commissioning the Beloved to descend through the heavens — the Hebrew library's framing of the incarnation as the Formed's descent from the seventh heaven into flesh. The Formless-Formed framework reads this passage as the apocalyptic-witness to the same Immanuel narrative Matt 1:23 announces.
cards.s_text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.
cards.t_text: "Go forth and descend through all the heavens, and thou wilt descend to the firmament and that world: to the angel in Sheol thou wilt descend, but to Haguel thou wilt not go.

cards.note: *till the Beloved will descend in the form in which you will see Him descend will descend, I say into the world in the last days Yahuah (Lord), who will be called Messiah (Christ).* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:12). The pre-incarnation announcement of the Beloved's descent in human form — the prophetic-Christology that lands at Matt 1:23's *Immanuel — Elohim (God) with us.*
cards.s_text: Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.
cards.t_text: And he said unto me: "Crowns and thrones of glory they do not receive, till the Beloved will descend in the form in which you will see Him descend will descend, I say into the world in the last days Yahuah (Lord), who will be called Messiah (Christ).

cards.note: *As the number of the stars and their power, so will I make thy seed a nation and a people, set apart for me in my heritage.* The Apocalypse of Abraham extends the seed-promise of Genesis 22:17 / 15:5 — the same seed-promise the Matt 1:1 genealogy traces forward to the Messiah. The Hebrew library's apocalyptic vision affirms the seed-line architecture Matthew opens his gospel with.
cards.s_text: The book of the generation of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), the son of David, the son of Abraham.
cards.t_text: And He said to me: "As the number of the stars and their power, so will I make thy seed a nation and a people, set apart for me in my heritage with Azazel."

cards.note: *And behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.* Levi, telling his sons of his vision (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 18:6), names the heavens-opening at the priestly investiture — the same heavens-opening Matt 3:16 narrates over Yahusha (Jesus) at the Yarden (Jordan). The Hebrew library knew the heavens open at the moment a covenant-bearing figure is invested for service; the gospel's opening of the heavens follows the same architecture.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:
cards.t_text: And behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.

cards.note: *Crowns and thrones of glory they do not receive, till the Beloved will descend in the form in which you will see Him descend will descend, I say into the world in the last days Yahuah (Lord), who will be called Messiah.* Ascension of Isaiah 9:12 names the Beloved's descent in human form — the same Beloved Father-voice names at Matt 3:17. The Ascension preserves the architecture: the Father commissions the Beloved's descent; the Formed takes on flesh; the public investiture at the water is the manifestation of the prior heavenly designation.
cards.s_text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
cards.t_text: And he said unto me: "Crowns and thrones of glory they do not receive, till the Beloved will descend in the form in which you will see Him descend will descend, I say into the world in the last days Yahuah (Lord), who will be called Messiah (Christ).

cards.note: *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* The Ascension of Isaiah's closing vision shows the Beloved seated at the right hand of the Great Glory after the descent-and-ascent journey. Matt 3:17's public naming-as-Son at the water is the inflection between the descent (already completed at Matt 1:23's Immanuel) and the ascent the Ascension shows in completion. The Hebrew library's framework holds the whole arc.
cards.s_text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
cards.t_text: And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.

cards.note: *Again, the devil taketh him up into an exceeding high mountain, and sheweth him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;* (Matthew 4:8). *After it is consummated, Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being; yea, he will descent from his firmament in the likeness of a man, a lawless king, the slayer of his mother: who himself (even) this king.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:2). The Ascension of Isaiah says that Beliar is the king of this world and has ruled it since it came into being. When the devil takes Yahusha (Jesus) up the mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, he is showing what he holds for the present age, so the offer that follows was no empty boast. But the same passage speaks of the completion of the world, and a rule that was given for a season is a rule with an end.
cards.s_text: Again, the devil takes him up into an exceeding high mountain, and shows him all the kingdoms of the world, and the glory of them;
cards.t_text: After it is consummated, Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being; yea, he will descent from his firmament in the likeness of a man, a lawless king, the slayer of his mother: who himself (even) this king.

cards.note: *And saith unto him, All these things will I give thee, if thou wilt fall down and worship me.* (Matthew 4:9). *And they will sacrifice to him and they will serve him saying: "This is Elohim (God) and beside him there is no other." And they greater number of those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:8–9). Satan asks Yahusha (Jesus) for worship, and Yahusha (Jesus) refuses. The Ascension of Isaiah shows what the same ruler gets from the world in the days of the end: sacrifice and service, and the cry that there is no other god beside him, and then the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved turned aside after him. It is the same grab for worship, once refused by the Son in the wilderness, and then carried out on the many who do not hold fast.
cards.s_text: And says unto him, All these things will I give you, if you will fall down and worship me.
cards.t_text: And they greater number of those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.

cards.note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shalt thou serve.* (Matthew 4:10). *For Beliar was in great wrath against Isaiah by reason of the vision, and because of the exposure wherewith he had exposed Sammael, and because through him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known, and His transformation and His descent and the likeness into which He should be transformed (that is) the likeness of man, and the persecution wherewith he should be persecuted, and the torturers wherewith the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should torture Him, and the coming of His twelve disciples, and the teaching, and that He should before the sabbath be crucified upon the tree, and should be crucified together with wicked men, and that He should be buried in the sepulchre,* (Ascension of Isaiah 3:13). Beliar's rage against Isaiah is over one thing: the prophet had made known the Beloved's going forth from the seventh heaven and his descent in the likeness of man. In the wilderness the same adversary meets the Beloved now come down in that likeness, and is sent away with the commandment of Torah: worship Yahuah (the Lord) and serve him only. The one Beliar tried to keep hidden dismisses him with the Word.
cards.s_text: Then says Yahusha (Jesus) unto him, Get you hence, Satan: for it is written, You shall worship Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God), and him only shall you serve.
cards.t_text: For Beliar was in great wrath against Isaiah by reason of the vision, and because of the exposure wherewith he had exposed Sammael, and because through him the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known, and His transformation and His descent and the likeness into which He should be transformed (that is) the likeness of man, and the persecution wherewith he should be persecuted, and the torturers wherewith the children of Yashar'el (Israel) should torture Him, and the coming of His twelve disciples, and the teaching, and that He should before the sabbath be crucified upon the tree, and should be crucified together with wicked men, and that He should be buried in the sepulchre,

cards.note: *But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.* (Matthew 5:22). *For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2). Gad is speaking to his sons about what he did to Joseph. In front of their father he spoke peaceably, and the moment he had gone out hatred darkened his mind and drove his soul toward killing his brother. That is the road Yahusha (Jesus) is describing: the commandment against murder was never only about the hand, because anger at a brother is where the killing begins. He is not setting the Torah aside but reading the commandment down to its root, the same root Gad learned the hard way and warned his children about.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, You fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.
cards.t_text: For in the presence of my father I spake peaceably to Joseph; and when I had gone out, the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.

cards.note: *With these spirits are mingled the spirits of error. First, the spirit of fornication is seated in the nature and in the senses.* Testament of Reuben 3:1 (DB ch 3) names the *spirit of fornication* as a heart-seated reality preceding the bodily act — the heart-architecture the Torah's tenth commandment also named. Matt 5:28's *whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart* walks the same heart-stake-architecture: the act follows the heart-spirit; the antithesis restores what the Torah and the testaments carried.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever looks on a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.
cards.t_text: Besides all these there is an eighth spirit of sleep, with which is brought about the trance of nature and the image of death.

cards.note: *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;* (Matthew 5:44). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Gad does not stop at loving the brother who treats you well. If a man sins against you, speak peaceably to him, keep no guile in your soul, and forgive him when he repents. Yahusha (Jesus) reaches the same place from the other side, telling us to bless those who curse us, do good to those who hate us, and pray for those who persecute us. This is not a teaching set against Moses; the fathers were already handing it to their sons, and Gad hands it down out of what hatred did to Joseph.
cards.s_text: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
cards.t_text: Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.

cards.note: *Elohim (God) aided my singleness. For on all the poor and oppressed I bestowed the good things of the earth in the singleness of my heart.* Testament of Issachar (DB ch 41 v.8) names the singleness-of-heart architecture in the patriarch's own testimony to his sons — singleness as the open-handed bestowal of the good things of the earth on the poor and oppressed. Matt 6:22's *if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light* walks the same Hebrew library architecture at the antithesis-restoration level. The single eye is the open hand; the singleness of the patriarch's testimony is the heart-pattern the gospel names.
cards.s_text: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore your eye be single, your whole body shall be full of light.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (Lord) increased ten thousandfold His benefits in my hands; and also Jacob, my father, knew that Elohim (God) aided my singleness.

cards.note: *Then saith he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;* (Matthew 9:37). *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2). Baruch looks ahead to the time when the age has ripened and the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, and the Mighty One brings bewilderment on the earth and its rulers. Yahusha (Jesus), looking at the crowds, says the harvest truly is plenteous, and the labourers are few. What Baruch placed at the end of the age, Yahusha (Jesus) says is already at hand. Both speak of a harvest of two kinds of seed, which is why the sorting matters and why labourers are wanted.
cards.s_text: Then says he unto his disciples, The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few;
cards.t_text: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.

cards.note: *Pray ye therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.* (Matthew 9:38) *Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.* (2 Baruch 70:2) Yahusha (Jesus) sees the crowds and tells his disciples to ask Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest for labourers, because the harvest is standing ready. Baruch had already been told what that harvest is: the time of the age ripens, and what was sown in it, evil seed and good seed alike, has come up. The one Baruch calls the Mighty One is the owner of that field, so the prayer in Matthew is a prayer prayed inside that ripening time, and the next chapter sends the twelve out as the answer.
cards.s_text: Pray you therefore Yahuah (Lord) of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
cards.t_text: Behold! the days come, and it shall be when the time of the age has ripened, And the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come, That the Mighty One will bring upon the earth and its inhabitants and upon its rulers Perturbation of spirit and stupor of heart.

cards.note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* (2 Baruch 78:3) Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the multitudes and finds them scattered and without a shepherd, which is a picture of a people and not of a crowd of strangers. Baruch writes to the brethren in captivity and says who that people is: the twelve tribes, bound by one bond because they are born from one father. However far they have been carried, they are one flock by birth, and that is what moves Yahusha (Jesus) to compassion.
cards.s_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.t_text: And truly I know that behold all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.

cards.note: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36) *For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* (2 Baruch 78:7) Yahusha (Jesus) is moved with compassion at sheep scattered abroad with no shepherd. Baruch closes his letter to the scattered tribes with the promise that answers it: Yahuah (Lord) will never forget or forsake them, and with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed. The compassion in Matthew and the mercy in Baruch are one mercy, and its work is the gathering.
cards.s_text: But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.
cards.t_text: For if ye so do these things, He will continually remember you, He who always promised on our behalf to those who were more excellent than we, that He will never forget or forsake us, but with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.

cards.note: *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28) *And when he had bravely met his glorious death, the third son was brought forward and was earnestly entreated by many to taste and so to save himself. But he answered in a loud voice, ‘Are ye ignorant that the same father begat me and my brothers that are dead, and the same mother gave us birth, and in the same doctrines was I brought up? I do not forswear the noble bond of brotherhood. Therefore if ye have any engine of torment, apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.’ But they were greatly angered at the bold speech of the man, and they dislocated his hands and his feet with their dislocating engines, and wrenched his limbs out of their sockets, and unstrung them; and they twisted round his fingers, and his arms, and his legs, and his elbow-joints. And in no wise being able to strangle his spirit they stripped off his skin, taking the points of the fingers with it, and tore in Scythian fashion the scalp from his head, and straightway brought him to the wheel. And on this they twisted his spine till he saw his own flesh hanging in strips and great gouts of blood pouring down from his entrails. And at the point of death he said, ‘We, O most abominable tyrant, suffer thus for our upbringing and our virtue that are of Elohim (God); but thou for thy impiety and thy cruelty shalt endure torments without end.’* (4 Maccabees 10:1) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own that those who kill the body cannot kill the soul, and that the fear belongs to the One who holds both. The third of the seven brothers says the same thing to Antiochus on the wheel: apply every engine to this body, for my soul you cannot reach. He is of the seed of Yahudah (Judah), dying for keeping the Law of his fathers, and he tells the tyrant that his own cruelty will meet torments without end. The persecutor's power stops at the body, and the soul is held in another hand.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: And when he had bravely met his glorious death, the third son was brought forward and was earnestly entreated by many to taste and so to save himself. But he answered in a loud voice, ‘Are ye ignorant that the same father begat me and my brothers that are dead, and the same mother gave us birth, and in the same doctrines was I brought up? I do not forswear the noble bond of brotherhood. Therefore if ye have any engine of torment, apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.’ But they were greatly angered at the bold speech of the man, and they dislocated his hands and his feet with their dislocating engines, and wrenched his limbs out of their sockets, and unstrung them; and they twisted round his fingers, and his arms, and his legs, and his elbow-joints. And in no wise being able to strangle his spirit they stripped off his skin, taking the points of the fingers with it, and tore in Scythian fashion the scalp from his head, and straightway brought him to the wheel. And on this they twisted his spine till he saw his own flesh hanging in strips and great gouts of blood pouring down from his entrails. And at the point of death he said, ‘We, O most abominable tyrant, suffer thus for our upbringing and our virtue that are of Elohim (God); but thou for thy impiety and thy cruelty shalt endure torments without end.’

cards.note: *And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.* (Matthew 10:28) *O Reason of the sons, lord over the passions! O religion, that wast dearer to the mother than her children! The mother, having two choices before her, religion and the present saving alive of her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). O how may I express the passionate love of parents for children? We stamp a marvellous likeness of our soul and of our shape on the tender nature of the child, and most of all through the mother's sympathy with her children being deeper than the father's. For women are softer of soul than men, and the more children they bear the more do they abound in love for them.* (4 Maccabees 15:1) The Messiah (Christ) sets the order of fear plainly: do not fear those who can only reach the body, but the One who has power over soul and body. The mother of the seven brothers had that choice laid before her in the flesh, her sons' lives saved for the present on the tyrant's word, or religion which saves unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). She loved religion more, and she and her sons kept the Law of Yahuah (God) unto death. It is the same priority the Messiah (Christ) gives his own when he sends them out to be hated.
cards.s_text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
cards.t_text: O Reason of the sons, lord over the passions! O religion, that wast dearer to the mother than her children! The mother, having two choices before her, religion and the present saving alive of her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). O how may I express the passionate love of parents for children? We stamp a marvellous likeness of our soul and of our shape on the tender nature of the child, and most of all through the mother's sympathy with her children being deeper than the father's. For women are softer of soul than men, and the more children they bear the more do they abound in love for them.

cards.note: *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22) *For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* (4 Maccabees 17:12) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own they will be hated of all men for his name, and that salvation belongs to the one who endures to the end. The book says of the seven brothers, Eleazar and their mother that on the day of trial virtue proved them through endurance and set before them the prize of victory in incorruption and everlasting life. Both put endurance first and the prize after it. These were the seed of Yahudah (Judah) holding to the Law unto death, and the life held out to them is life that does not decay, which the faithful asleep await with us at the resurrection.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.

cards.note: *And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.* (Matthew 10:22) *The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* (4 Maccabees 17:17) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own they will be hated of all men and that the one who endures to the end shall be saved. The book gives the seven brothers as the picture of that endurance: even the tyrant and his council admired it, and the book says it has brought them to stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age. Endurance in the Law of their fathers did not end in the grave. The faithful who have fallen asleep wait with us for the first resurrection and are not made perfect without us, so what the verse holds out is the end promised to the one who endures.
cards.s_text: And you shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endures to the end shall be saved.
cards.t_text: The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.

cards.note: *For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.* (Matthew 10:20) *But he said, ‘Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* (4 Maccabees 10:4) The Messiah (Christ) tells his own not to take thought how or what they shall speak when they are brought before rulers, because the Spirit of their Father speaks in them. The fourth of the seven brothers faces the same hour when Antiochus orders his tongue cut out, and he answers that Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless. What matters in the hour of trial does not depend on a prepared speech or even on the tongue, since the Father hears and is present with the one who stands for his Law.
cards.s_text: For it is not you that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaks in you.
cards.t_text: But he said, ‘Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.

cards.note: *Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.* (Matthew 10:4). *Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:3). Before the Twelve are ever named, the Ascension of Isaiah says that the ruler of this world will persecute what they plant and that one of the Twelve will fall into his hands. Matthew's list of the apostles closes on exactly that note, with the last name carrying the word betrayed. Nothing in the account takes the Beloved by surprise. The persecution of the plant and the loss of one from the inner circle were spoken of ahead of time, and Matthew's commissioning of the Twelve goes on to warn them of what is coming.
cards.s_text: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
cards.t_text: Will persecute the plant which the Twelve Apostles of the Beloved have planted. Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.

cards.note: *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* (Matthew 18:35). *Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3). Yahusha (Jesus) closes His warning with the words from your hearts: the Father will deal with us as we deal with a brother we will not forgive. Gad gives his sons the same measure. Love one another from the heart, speak peaceably to a brother who sins against you, and when he repents and confesses, forgive him. Both put the whole matter in the heart, where a brother is either forgiven or kept in the ledger.
cards.s_text: So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if you from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
cards.t_text: Love ye one another from the heart; and if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile; and if he repent and confess, forgive him.

cards.note: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.* (Matthew 19:21) *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5) Yahusha (Jesus) tells the rich young man that if he wants to be perfect he should go, sell what he has, give to the poor, and have treasure in heaven, and then come and follow. Levi tells his sons the same thing in other words: work righteousness on the earth, and it is kept as a treasure in heaven. Just before this, Yahusha (Jesus) had told the man that the way into life is to keep the commandments, so the treasure in heaven is what righteousness done on the earth is laid up as.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, If you will be perfect, go and sell that you have, and give to the poor, and you shall have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
cards.t_text: Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.

cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28). *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2). Joseph sees twelve harts feeding together, and all twelve end up dispersed over the earth, the nine first and the three likewise. The twelve harts read as the twelve tribes, scattered. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks of those same tribes as a whole people sitting under judgment when the Son of Adam takes His throne, with twelve thrones set for judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). A people who are to be judged as twelve tribes must first be gathered as twelve, and Joseph's vision is the scattering that the gathering answers.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That you which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, you also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth, and likewise also the three.

cards.note: *Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.* (Matthew 20:28). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Yahusha (Jesus) says of Himself that the Son of Adam came not to be served but to serve, and to give His life a ransom for many. Benjamin, looking ahead, says he knows how lowly He will be upon the earth and how glorious in heaven. The lowliness and the glory belong to one person: the one who takes the servant's place on earth is the one who ascends from Hades into heaven.
cards.s_text: Even as the Son of Adam came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
cards.t_text: And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]

cards.note: *And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:30). *And after these things shall a star arise to you from Jacob in peace, And a man shall arise [from my seed], like the sun of righteousness, Walking with the sons of men in meekness and righteousness; And no sin shall be found in him.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:1). Yahudah (Judah) tells his sons that a star will rise to them out of Jacob, a man from his own seed who walks among the sons of men in meekness and without sin. Two blind men by the Jericho road, who cannot see him, cry out to him by that very title, Son of David, the seed of Yahudah (Judah). The testament named the man; the blind men recognized him by his line before they could see his face.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you Son of David.
cards.t_text: And after these things shall a star arise to you from Jacob in peace, And a man shall arise [from my seed], like the sun of righteousness, Walking with the sons of men in meekness and righteousness; And no sin shall be found in him.

cards.note: *And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:30) *[This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), And this Fountain giving life unto all.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:4) The two blind men call Yahusha (Jesus) the Son of David. The verse before this one has Yahudah (Judah) saying his sons will be sons in truth and will walk in His commandments first and last, and then he names the Branch of Elohim (God) that comes from his line and the Fountain giving life to all. The Son of David the blind men name is that Branch, and men who cannot see are the ones who know him by hearing his voice as he passes.
cards.s_text: And, behold, two blind men sitting by the way side, when they heard that Yahusha (Jesus) passed by, cried out, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you Son of David.
cards.t_text: [This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), And this Fountain giving life unto all.]

cards.note: *And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Adonai (Lord), thou Son of David.* (Matthew 20:31) *Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5) The multitude tells the blind men to hold their peace, and they cry out all the more, Son of David. Yahudah (Judah) says the sceptre of his kingdom will shine forth and a stem will rise from the root of his sons. The two men have no sight, yet they name the stem from the root of Yahudah (Judah) while the crowd, which can see, tries to silence them. They show what Yahusha (Jesus) said of his own sheep, that they hear his voice.
cards.s_text: And the multitude rebuked them, because they should hold their peace: but they cried the more, saying, Have mercy on us, O Lord, you Son of David.
cards.t_text: Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;

cards.note: *Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.* (Matthew 21:5) *Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5) Matthew shows the King coming to the daughter of Zion, meek and sitting on an ass, as the prophet had said. Yahudah (Judah) told his sons that the sceptre of his kingdom would shine forth and a stem rise from their root. The sceptre promised to the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) arrives not in a chariot but on a colt, and the daughter of Zion is told to look.
cards.s_text: Tell you the daughter of Sion, Behold, your King comes unto you, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.
cards.t_text: Then shall the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem;

cards.note: *Tell ye the daughter of Sion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.* (Matthew 21:5) *And from it shall grow a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:6) Matthew shows the King coming to the daughter of Zion, meek, on a colt. Yahudah (Judah) says a rod of righteousness will grow from the stem that comes from his root, to judge and to save all who call upon Yahuah (Lord). The Gentiles here are best read as the scattered seed of Yashar'el (Israel) living among the nations, the ones the King is coming to gather and who call out to him, as the crowds of the entry will do. This is not a new people set in the place of the twelve tribes.
cards.s_text: Tell you the daughter of Sion, Behold, your King comes unto you, meek, and sitting upon an ass, and a colt the foal of an ass.
cards.t_text: And from it shall grow a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).

cards.note: *But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.* (Matthew 23:13) *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3) Yahusha (Jesus) charges the scribes and Pharisees with shutting up the kingdom of heaven against men, going in neither themselves nor letting others enter. Levi foresaw leaders of his own line dealing lawlessly with Yashar'el (Israel), and the veil of the temple being rent so that it would no longer cover their shame. In both the failing is a leadership that holds the door and breaks the commandments, and the people kept out are its victims. When the veil of the temple is torn at his death, the lawlessness of the keepers is laid bare.
cards.s_text: But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for you neither go in yourselves, neither suffer you them that are entering to go in.
cards.t_text: And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.

cards.note: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.* (Matthew 23:15) *And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:11) Yahusha (Jesus) says the scribes and Pharisees cross sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made they make him twofold more the child of hell than themselves. Levi's vision of the weeks names the priests who come in the seventh week as idolaters, lovers of money, proud and lawless. A convert made by leaders like that is made into what they are, which is why the measure is whether a teacher keeps the commandments. The fault is in the system that made the proselyte, and the one it made is its victim.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, you make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.
cards.t_text: And in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless, lascivious, abusers of children and beasts.

cards.note: *Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.* (Matthew 23:28). *But do not ye, my children, wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness; but cleave unto goodness only, for Elohim (God) hath His habitation therein, and men desire it.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 105:1). Yahusha (Jesus) names the double face plainly: outwardly righteous before men, inwardly full of hypocrisy and iniquity. Asher warns his sons against exactly that, to wear one face and not two, and to cleave to goodness only because Elohim (God) makes His habitation there. What Yahusha (Jesus) exposes in the hypocrite, Asher tells his children to refuse before it ever takes root.
cards.s_text: Even so you also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within you are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
cards.t_text: But do not ye, my children, wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness; but cleave unto goodness only, for Elohim (God) hath His habitation therein, and men desire it.

cards.note: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.* (Matthew 23:27). *For they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin; 'for they both do the evil thing and they have pleasure in them that do it', following the example of the spirits of deceit, and striving against mankind.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 108:2). Yahusha (Jesus) calls the hypocrites whited sepulchres, beautiful on the outside and full of death within. Asher gives the same condition its weight: the double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin, because they do the evil thing and also take pleasure in those who do it. The tomb is the picture of the sin Asher counts twice, a clean outside covering what is in fact within.
cards.s_text: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for you are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness.
cards.t_text: For they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin; 'for they both do the evil thing and they have pleasure in them that do it', following the example of the spirits of deceit, and striving against mankind.

cards.note: *And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?* (Matthew 24:3) *For in the fortieth year of my life, I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem, that the sun and the moon were standing still.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 90:1) The disciples sit on the mount of Olives and ask Yahusha (Jesus) the sign of his coming and of the end of the world. Naphtali, in the fortieth year of his life, saw a vision on that same mountain, east of Jerusalem. It is a place where what is coming is shown and asked about, and the two come together there.
cards.s_text: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives, the disciples came unto him privately, saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of your coming, and of the end of the world?
cards.t_text: For in the fortieth year of my life, I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem, that the sun and the moon were standing still.

cards.note: *And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.* (Matthew 24:14) *For through their tribes shall Elohim (God) appear [dwelling among men] on earth, To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 93:3) Yahusha (Jesus) says the gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world as a witness to all nations, and then the end comes. Naphtali's last words say what the news is: Elohim (God) appears through the tribes to save the race of Yashar'el (Israel) and to gather the righteous from among the Gentiles. The Gentiles here are best read as the scattered seed of the twelve tribes living among the nations, which is why the news goes out broadly: the sheep are scattered everywhere, are not known by sight, and hear when they are called.
cards.s_text: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.
cards.t_text: For through their tribes shall Elohim (God) appear [dwelling among men] on earth, To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.

cards.note: *And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30). *Until the El Elyon (Most High) shall visit the earth, coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water. He shall save Yashar'el (Israel) and all the Gentiles [Elohim (God) speaking in the person of man].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:3). Asher has just told his sons that they will sin, be handed to their enemies, and be scattered to the four corners of the earth. Then he says the Most High will visit the earth, coming Himself as man, and will save Yashar'el (Israel) and the Gentiles, who stand right beside the scattered of the verse before. Matthew shows the same one at the end of that road, the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven, all the tribes of the earth mourning, and the Son of Adam coming in the clouds with power and great glory. The one who comes in the person of man is Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom Elohim (God) took form, who walked with Adam's line from the beginning and came in flesh, and the tribes that mourn are the tribes Asher says were scattered.
cards.s_text: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
cards.t_text: Until the El Elyon (Most High) shall visit the earth, coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water. He shall save Yashar'el (Israel) and all the Gentiles [Elohim (God) speaking in the person of man].

cards.note: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). *But Yahuah (Lord) will gather you together in faith through His tender mercy, 'and' for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:7). The sons of Asher are told they will be scattered until they do not know their own lands, tribe, and tongue. Yet Yahuah (the Lord) will gather them, and the reason given is Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: the gathering rests on the fathers and on the blood that carries their promise. Matthew has the same gathering in view, with the elect called in from the four winds. The elect there are the scattered seed of the fathers being brought home, and not a company assembled out of any people by confession.
cards.s_text: And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
cards.t_text: But Yahuah (Lord) will gather you together in faith through His tender mercy, 'and' for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.]

cards.note: *And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt.* (Matthew 26:39) *'Why dost thou delay, O tyrant? We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.* (4 Maccabees 9:1) Both stand before a death they could avoid and choose the will of Elohim (God) over their own preservation. The seven brothers, the seed of Yahudah (Judah), tell the tyrant they are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of their fathers, so they witness that Torah stands to the death. The Messiah (Christ) in the garden prays that the cup pass from him and then gives himself to the Father's will, nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. The brothers' endurance foreshadows his laying down of his life, though the cup he takes is far greater than their pain, for he drinks it as the Pesach (Passover) lamb in obedience to the Father.
cards.s_text: And he went a little further, and fell on his face, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as you will.
cards.t_text: 'Why dost thou delay, O tyrant? We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.

cards.note: *He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done.* (Matthew 26:42) *And righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.* (4 Maccabees 17:15) The Messiah (Christ) prays a second time that if the cup cannot pass he will drink it, and he ends with thy will be done, the Son's willing submission to the Father who sent him. The book says of the seven brothers that righteousness won the victory and gave the crown to her athletes, because they would not turn from the Law even to save their lives. Their crown is the foreshadow, and his drinking of the cup leads to the resurrection on the third day. Obedience to the Father's will through death is the road to the prize in both.
cards.s_text: He went away again the second time, and prayed, saying, O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, your will be done.
cards.t_text: And righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.

cards.note: *Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.* (Matthew 26:46) *And these men, therefore, having sanctified themselves for Elohim's (God’s) sake, not only have received this honour, but also the honour that through them the enemy had no more power over our people, and the tyrant suffered punishment, and our country was purified, they having as it were become a ransom for our nation’s sin; and through the blood of these righteous men and the propitiation of their death, the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel) that before was evil entreated.* (4 Maccabees 17:19) The Messiah (Christ) rises from his prayer and walks toward the one who betrays him, not away from him, because the hour of his laying down his life is at hand. The book, in its own voice, says of the seven brothers that they became as it were a ransom for the nation's sin, and that through their death the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel). That is the book's witness, and it foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) laying down of his life rather than replacing it, for the brothers show that Torah stands to the death. The cross is the door home to the commandments, and the Messiah (Christ) goes to it willingly as the Pesach (Passover) lamb.
cards.s_text: Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that does betray me.
cards.t_text: And these men, therefore, having sanctified themselves for Elohim's (God’s) sake, not only have received this honour, but also the honour that through them the enemy had no more power over our people, and the tyrant suffered punishment, and our country was purified, they having as it were become a ransom for our nation’s sin; and through the blood of these righteous men and the propitiation of their death, the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel) that before was evil entreated.

cards.note: *Then saith Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.* (Matthew 26:31) *And behold, I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages [against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly], deceiving Yashar'el (Israel), and stirring up against it great evils from Yahuah (Lord).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:2) On the night of his arrest Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples they will all be offended because of him, and says it is written that the shepherd will be smitten and the sheep scattered. Long before, Levi told his sons that at the end of the ages they would act ungodly against the Saviour of the world, deceiving Yashar'el (Israel) and leaving it open to great evils. Both describe leadership failing and the flock scattered as a result. The one who is smitten was himself born of Yahudah (Judah) and came for his people, so what is named here is a corrupt leadership, not the people.
cards.s_text: Then says Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, All you shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad.
cards.t_text: And behold, I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages [against the Saviour of the world, Messiah (Christ), acting godlessly], deceiving Yashar'el (Israel), and stirring up against it great evils from Yahuah (Lord).

cards.note: *Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.* (Matthew 26:65) *And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3) The high priest tears his own clothes and calls the truth blasphemy, though the Torah forbids the high priest to rend his clothes. Levi had said that when the lawlessness of the leaders of his line was full, it would be the veil of the temple that was rent, so as not to cover their shame. One rending is a man's, done in anger to silence a witness; the other is Yahuah's (God's), and it uncovers. The charge is against the office as it was being used, not against the people under it.
cards.s_text: Then the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He has spoken blasphemy; what further need have we of witnesses? behold, now you have heard his blasphemy.
cards.t_text: And ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness; but the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.

cards.note: *For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.* (Matthew 26:28). *In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8). Jacob, embracing Joseph, tells him that in him the prophecy of heaven will be fulfilled: a blameless one delivered up for lawless men, a sinless one dying for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant. Yahusha (Jesus) at the table gives that blood its name, shed for many for the remission of sins. The Testament says the salvation is for the Gentiles and for the house of Yashar'el (Israel), and the Gentiles named beside Yashar'el (Israel) are the scattered seed of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) living among the nations, which is why the news goes out broadly: the sheep are scattered everywhere, and the ones who hear are the ones it was always for.
cards.s_text: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
cards.t_text: In thee shall be fulfilled the prophecy of heaven [concerning the Lamb of Elohim (God), and Saviour of the world], that a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men [in the blood of the covenant, for the salvation of the Gentiles and 'of Israel', and shall destroy Beliar and his servants].

cards.note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). *And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.* (2 Baruch 6:7). The veil is torn from the top to the bottom, which is a tearing from above. In 2 Baruch the hand from above also acts upon the veil: the angel descends into the Holy of Holies and takes from there the veil, the ark, the mercy seat and every holy vessel, and the next verse in the book says he charges the earth to guard them until the last times so that strangers may not get possession of them. In neither is the house of Yahuah (God) simply done away with. In Baruch its holy things are kept to be restored, and in Matthew the veil is opened from above, and the way back into the holiest is the way home.
cards.s_text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;
cards.t_text: And I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark, and the mercy-seat, and the two tables, and the holy raiment of the priests, and the altar of incense, and the forty-eight precious stones, wherewith the priest was adorned and all the holy vessels of the tabernacle.

cards.note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51). *And thereupon the angel opened to me the gates of heaven, and I saw the holy temple, and upon a throne of glory the El Elyon (Most High).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:1). Levi is shown the gates of heaven opened and the holy temple with the throne of glory inside it. At the death of Yahusha (Jesus) the veil that closed the earthly holy of holies is torn from the top down, opened from heaven's side and not from ours. What Levi saw opened in vision is opened in fact at the cross, and the way into the holiest is laid bare.
cards.s_text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;
cards.t_text: And thereupon the angel opened to me the gates of heaven, and I saw the holy temple, and upon a throne of glory the El Elyon (Most High).

cards.note: *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;* (Matthew 27:51) *And He said to me: Levi, I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:2) Levi is told that the blessings of the priesthood are his until Yahuah (Lord) comes and sojourns in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel). Matthew shows what the end of that until looks like: when Yahusha (Jesus) has come and given his life, the veil of the temple is torn from the top to the bottom, and the way into the holy place stands open. Nothing of Torah is thrown out in this; the way to the Father is opened from above by the one who came to sojourn among his people.
cards.s_text: And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent;
cards.t_text: And He said to me: Levi, I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52) *And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 24:17) Levi is told that some of his seed will be high priests, judges and scribes, and that the holy place will be guarded by what they say. Matthew shows the saints who slept rising out of opened graves when Yahusha (Jesus) dies, which can be read as a foretaste of the resurrection of the faithful that is still ahead. The two meet on the same ground: the holy place and the faithful who served Yahuah (God) in it are not left to the grave.
cards.s_text: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,
cards.t_text: And some of them shall be high priests, and judges, and scribes; For by their mouth shall the holy place be guarded.

cards.note: *He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.* (Matthew 27:42) *O Reason of the sons, lord over the passions! O religion, that wast dearer to the mother than her children! The mother, having two choices before her, religion and the present saving alive of her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). O how may I express the passionate love of parents for children? We stamp a marvellous likeness of our soul and of our shape on the tender nature of the child, and most of all through the mother's sympathy with her children being deeper than the father's. For women are softer of soul than men, and the more children they bear the more do they abound in love for them.* (4 Maccabees 15:1) The mockers at the cross offer the choice of a present deliverance: come down and we will believe. It is the choice the mother of the seven brothers had before her, the saving alive of her sons for the present or religion which saves unto eternal life according to Elohim (God), and she loved religion more. The Messiah (Christ) could have saved himself and did not, for his life was not taken from him; he laid it down of himself. He chooses the Father's purpose over present safety, as she chose the Law of Yahuah (God) over the tyrant's promise.
cards.s_text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.
cards.t_text: O Reason of the sons, lord over the passions! O religion, that wast dearer to the mother than her children! The mother, having two choices before her, religion and the present saving alive of her seven sons according to the tyrant's promise, loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God). O how may I express the passionate love of parents for children? We stamp a marvellous likeness of our soul and of our shape on the tender nature of the child, and most of all through the mother's sympathy with her children being deeper than the father's. For women are softer of soul than men, and the more children they bear the more do they abound in love for them.

cards.note: *He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:43) *But as many as with their whole heart make righteousness their first thought, these alone are able to master the weakness of the flesh, believing that unto Elohim (God) they die not, as our patriarchs, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, died not, but that they live unto Elohim (God).* (4 Maccabees 7:12) The mockers say that since he trusted in Elohim (God), let him deliver him now. The book answers from the other side: those who make righteousness their first thought believe that they die not unto Elohim (God), as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob died and yet live unto him. Deliverance for the one who trusts is not measured by whether he comes down from the cross. The fathers sleep and await the first resurrection with us, and Yahusha's (Jesus's) deliverance came on the third day.
cards.s_text: He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: But as many as with their whole heart make righteousness their first thought, these alone are able to master the weakness of the flesh, believing that unto Elohim (God) they die not, as our patriarchs, Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, died not, but that they live unto Elohim (God).

cards.note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50) *For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* (4 Maccabees 17:12) Yahusha (Jesus) cries with a loud voice and yields up the ghost, laying down his life of his own will, as he had said no one takes it from him. The book says that on the day of trial virtue proved the seven brothers through endurance and set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.
