The brothers endured in the Law unto death, and their endurance foreshadows his. The prize set before him is the resurrection on the third day and the first resurrection at his coming.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.
cards.t_text: For on that day virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.

cards.note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50) *The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* (4 Maccabees 17:17) *And these men, therefore, having sanctified themselves for Elohim's (God’s) sake, not only have received this honour, but also the honour that through them the enemy had no more power over our people, and the tyrant suffered punishment, and our country was purified, they having as it were become a ransom for our nation’s sin; and through the blood of these righteous men and the propitiation of their death, the divine Providence delivered Yashar'el (Israel) that before was evil entreated.* (4 Maccabees 17:19) Yahusha (Jesus) yields up the ghost, laying down his life of his own will. The book shows the seven brothers admired even by the tyrant and now standing beside the throne of Elohim (God), and in its own voice says their death was as it were a ransom for the nation's sin. That is the book's witness, and it foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) laying down of his life rather than standing in its place, for what the brothers prove is that Torah stands to the death. The cross is the door home to the commandments, and he gives his life once, as the Pesach (Passover) lamb.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.
cards.t_text: The tyrant himself and his whole council admired their endurance, whereby they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.

cards.note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time. For they shall behold the world which is now invisible to them, And they shall behold the time which is now hidden from them:* (2 Baruch 51:7–8). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. Baruch speaks of people for whom the law was a hope, an understanding and a confidence, and says wonders will appear in their time and they will behold the world that is now invisible to them. These are people whose whole life was the Torah, and nothing here sets their works against the promise. It describes the covenant walk of those who kept the commandments, and the opened graves at the cross are the first glimpse of the seeing that is promised to them.
cards.s_text: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,
cards.t_text: But those who have been saved by their works, And to whom the law has been now a hope, And understanding an expectation, And wisdom a confidence, Shall wonders appear in their time.

cards.note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:14). The Ascension of Isaiah puts the weight where it belongs. The one who stretches out his hand against the Son is the god of that world, the adversary behind the deed, and those who carry it out do so not knowing who He is. Matthew then tells it as it happened, that they crucified him and divided his garments, in keeping with what the prophet had said. The tree is the place of the curse that falls on a people for breaking the covenant, and the Son took that curse on himself, so that the scattered might come home to the Torah, not away from it.
cards.s_text: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.
cards.t_text: And the god of that world will stretch forth his hand against the Son, and they will crucify Him on a tree, and will slay Him not knowing who He is.

cards.note: *Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.* (Matthew 27:50). *And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:16). Matthew tells that Yahusha (Jesus) cried out and yielded up the ghost, and the verb is his own: he gave himself up. The Ascension of Isaiah says what that death was for. He goes down and plunders the angel of death, and on the third day he ascends. The death at the cross is the doorway of the descent, and the descent ends in the rising.
cards.s_text: Yahusha (Jesus), when he had cried again with a loud voice, yielded up the ghost.
cards.t_text: And when He hath plundered the angel of death, He will ascend on the third day, and he will remain in that world five hundred and forty-five days.

cards.note: *And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,* (Matthew 27:52). *And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:17). Matthew says the graves were opened and many bodies of the saints which slept arose. The Ascension of Isaiah says why the righteous waited as they did: their spirits do not receive their garments until the Messiah ascends, and then many of them ascend with him. Those who walked the covenant faithfully and slept are the first to be brought out when the way is opened, and the opened graves at the cross are a foretaste of the larger rising still to come.
cards.s_text: And the graves were opened; and many bodies of the saints which slept arose,
cards.t_text: And then many of the righteous will ascend with Him, whose spirits do not receive their garments till Yahuah (Lord) Messiah (Christ) ascend and they ascend with Him.

cards.note: *And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.* (Matthew 27:35). *In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree:* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:20). Matthew tells of the crucifixion in a few plain lines and says it came to pass according to what was spoken by the prophet. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah himself seeing it first, and naming the place: in Jerusalem, on a tree. What Matthew sets down as history, the prophet was shown beforehand.
cards.s_text: And they crucified him, and parted his garments, casting lots: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots.
cards.t_text: In Jerusalem indeed I saw Him being crucified on a tree:

cards.note: *And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.* (Matthew 27:60). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew closes the day with the body laid in a new tomb cut in the rock and a great stone rolled to the door. The Ascension of Isaiah tells where the Beloved was while the body lay there: after they crucified Him, He descended to the angel of Sheol. The same verse says the adversary envied him and stirred up the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The charge lies with the adversary who envied and stirred, and a people who did not know who they were handing over are the lost sheep, not enemies.
cards.s_text: And laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn out in the rock: and he rolled a great stone to the door of the sepulchre, and departed.
cards.t_text: And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.

cards.note: *He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where Yahusha (Lord) lay.* (Matthew 28:6). *And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:21). At the empty tomb the angel says that he is not here, for he is risen, as he said. The Ascension of Isaiah has Isaiah told the same in vision, that He will rise after the third day and remain days. The rising was not an afterthought, it was said before by Yahusha (Jesus) himself and seen before by the prophet, and the days he remained with his own after rising are the days the vision speaks of.
cards.s_text: He is not here: for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
cards.t_text: And likewise after the third day rise again and remain days.

cards.note: *Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.* (Matthew 28:11). *And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:19). Matthew tells that some of the watch came into the city and showed the chief priests all that had been done, and the verses that follow tell of money given to the soldiers to carry a false story. The Ascension of Isaiah gives the order of it: the adversary envied him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against him, not knowing who He was. The line runs from the adversary through those who held the seat of leadership, and the many who were roused did not know, and are deceived sheep. It is a system that lied, and no verse here makes a whole people the enemy.
cards.s_text: Now when they were going, behold, some of the watch came into the city, and shewed unto the chief priests all the things that were done.
cards.t_text: And after this the adversary envied Him and roused the children of Yashar'el (Israel) against Him, not knowing who He was, and they delivered Him to the king, and crucified Him, and He descended to the angel of Sheol.

cards.note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:22). Isaiah sees Him send out the Twelve Apostles and then ascend, and Matthew has the sending in his own words: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations. Twelve are sent because the twelve tribes are the ones being sought, and the nations are where the scattered of those tribes now live. We do not know the sheep by sight, so the word goes out broadly, and the sheep hear his voice.
cards.s_text: Go you therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):
cards.t_text: And the angel who conducted me said: "Understand, Isaiah": and I saw when He sent out the Twelve Apostles and ascended.

cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). The Ascension of Isaiah says He sat down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory the prophet could not behold. The Great Glory is the Father, the formless one, and the Son who took form sits at his right hand. When Yahusha (Jesus) says in Matthew that all power is given unto him in heaven and in earth, the word given tells the same story: the Son receives the power from the Father who gives it, and takes his seat beside him.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
cards.t_text: And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.

cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5). Benjamin says the one who comes will ascend from Hades and pass from earth into heaven, lowly on the earth and glorious in heaven. After the cross and the tomb, Yahusha (Jesus) comes to His disciples and says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth. The word Benjamin gave his sons is the road that ends in that sentence.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
cards.t_text: And He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven. And I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.]

cards.note: *Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):* (Matthew 28:19). *For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:5). The fathers left their sons the commandments of Elohim (God) as their inheritance, to be kept while they waited for Yahuah (the Lord) to reveal His salvation to all the Gentiles. The until marks the length of the waiting, not an end to the keeping. When Yahusha (Jesus) says to go and teach all nations, the message goes out broadly because those it is for are scattered among them and are not known by sight. Benjamin's word has the order right: the commandments stay in the hands of the sons, and the salvation goes out to be heard.
cards.s_text: Go you therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit):
cards.t_text: For all these things they gave us for an inheritance, saying: Keep the commandments of Elohim (God), until Yahuah (Lord) shall reveal His salvation to all Gentiles.

cards.note: *Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.* (Matthew 28:10). *Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, [who appeared upon earth in the form of a man in humility. And as many as believe on Him on the earth shall rejoice with Him].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:7). After His resurrection Yahusha (Jesus) tells the women to carry word to His brethren, and the brethren He means are sons of Yashar'el (Israel). Benjamin pictures that same people rising from the dead, each patriarch over his own tribe, worshipping the King of heaven who appeared on earth in the form of a man. The Testament keeps the tribes by name and by order, and the Messiah (Christ) still calls them brethren.
cards.s_text: Then said Yahusha (Jesus) unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.
cards.t_text: Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven, [who appeared upon earth in the form of a man in humility. And as many as believe on Him on the earth shall rejoice with Him].

cards.note: *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18). *Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:8). Benjamin says all men shall rise, some to glory and some to shame, and that Yahuah (the Lord) will judge Yashar'el (Israel) first because they did not believe Him when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh. Yahusha (Jesus) says all power is given to Him in heaven and in earth, and a judge needs that power. Judgment beginning with the house of the fathers is the order the Testament lays out, and Yahusha (Jesus) is the one who holds the authority to carry it through.
cards.s_text: And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
cards.t_text: Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].

cards.note: thread:the-formless-father-and-the-formed-son-witnessed-in-ascension-of-isaiah | The Lukan Transfiguration parallel — Mosheh (Moses) and Eliyahu (Elijah) appearing in glory, the Father-voice naming *This is my beloved Son: hear him* (Luke 9:35). The Formless-Father / Formed-Son architecture witnessed in the Ascension of Isaiah 9-10 seventh-heaven framing.

cards.note: thread:the-faithful-righteous-suffering-unto-death-and-the-atoning-blood-architecture-in-4-maccabees | Luke carries the substitutionary-atoning-blood architecture with synoptic substance — the King silent before his accusers, the mockery from those who pass by, the *if thou be the King of the Yahudim (Jews), save thyself* (v.37), and the death-as-faithful-unto-death the 4 Maccabees prefiguring names.
cards.s_text: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
cards.t_text: He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him.

cards.note: thread:the-day-of-the-most-high-cosmic-darkness-and-the-resurrection-of-the-righteous-in-2-esdras-and-2-baruch | Luke carries the cosmic-darkness-over-the-land from the sixth to the ninth hour with the synoptic substance, uniquely naming *the sun was darkened* (v.45) — the day-of-the-Most-High substance the 2 Esdras / 2 Baruch witness frames around the cross.
cards.s_text: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
cards.t_text: Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over all the land unto the ninth hour.

cards.note: *These things, therefore, I say to you from experience, my children, that ye may drive forth hatred, which is of the devil, and cleave to the love of Elohim (God).* The Testament of Gad (DB ch 61 v.2) names hatred outright as *of the devil* — the very poison Gad repented of, set against the love of Elohim (God) the new commandment presses. John 15:23's *He that hateth me hateth my Father also* lands the same architecture at its root: the hatred of the world for the Formed one is hatred of the Father who sent him, because hatred is of the devil and cannot abide the Light. The patriarch traced the hatred to its source; the gospel names the One it strikes.
cards.s_text: He that hates me hates my Father also.
cards.t_text: These things, 'therefore', I say to you from experience, my children, that ye may drive forth hatred, which is of the devil, and cleave to the love of Elohim (God).

cards.note: *Hatred, therefore, is evil, for it constantly mateth with lying, speaking against the truth; and it maketh small things to be great, and causeth the light to be darkness, and calleth the sweet bitter, and teacheth slander, and kindleth wrath, and stirreth up war, and violence and all covetousness; it filleth the heart with evils and devilish poison.* The Testament of Gad (DB ch 61 v.1) names hatred as the inversion-engine that speaks against the truth, calls light darkness, and fills the heart with devilish poison. John 15:18's *If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you* names the same hatred turned against the Formed one and his own: the world's hatred is not reasoned offence but the devil's poison the patriarch warned against, the hatred that calls the Light of the world darkness.
cards.s_text: If the world hate you, you know that it hated me before it hated you.
cards.t_text: 'Hatred, therefore, is evil,' for it constantly mateth with lying, speaking against the truth; and it maketh small things to be great, and causeth the light to be darkness, and calleth the sweet bitter, and teacheth slander, and 'kindleth' wrath, and 'stirreth' up war, and violence and all covetousness; it filleth the heart with evils and devilish poison.

cards.note: *Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.* (John 15:13). *And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 134:5). Yahusha (Jesus) names the greatest love as laying down one's life for his friends. Benjamin teaches his sons the same love at its starting measure: the man with the grace of a good spirit loves his brother as his own soul. A man who loves another as his own soul has already begun to hold his own life loosely, and the Messiah (Christ) carries that love to its furthest end.
cards.s_text: Greater love has no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
cards.t_text: And him that hath the grace of a good spirit he loveth as his own soul.

cards.note: *Put away, therefore, jealousy from your souls, and love one another with uprightness of heart.* The Testament of Gad (DB ch 63 v.7) closes the patriarch's exhortation with the same love-one-another command, named with *uprightness of heart* — the inward singleness from which the love must come. John 15:12's *This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you* walks the same architecture: the love is not sentiment but the uprightness of heart the fathers commanded, now measured by the love of the One who calls the disciples friends and lays down his life for them.
cards.s_text: This is my commandment, That you love one another, as I have loved you.
cards.t_text: Put away, therefore, jealousy from your souls, and love one another with uprightness of heart.

cards.note: *love one another in deed, and in word, and in the inclination of the soul.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:1). Gad carries the love-one-another command in his own testimony to his sons, and he names it out of his own repentance for the hatred he bore against Joseph his brother. Yahusha's (Jesus') *a new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another* (John 13:34) is *new* not because the Hebrew library never named brotherly love, but because he loves *as I have loved you* — the patriarch's heart-command brought to its measure in the Formed one's own laying-down of his life. The wisdom of the fathers already pressed the command on the twelve sons of Yashar'el (Israel); the gospel binds it to the cross.
cards.s_text: A new commandment I give unto you, That you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another.
cards.t_text: And now, my children, 'I exhort you,' love ye each one his brother, and put away hatred from your hearts, love one another in deed, and in word, and in the inclination of the soul.

cards.note: *And there is no time at which the works of men can be hid; for on the heart itself have they been written down before the Lord.* The Testament of Judah (DB ch 35 v.4) names the spirit-of-truth's inward work — the works of men written on the heart itself, hidden from no time before Yahuah (the Lord). John 14:17's *Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you* walks the same architecture: the Spirit of truth is the inward witness, dwelling within and writing on the heart, whom the world cannot receive because it knows him not. The wisdom of the fathers named the spirit of truth's inward writing; the gospel names the indwelling the disciples receive.
cards.s_text: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it sees him not, neither knows him: but you know him; for he dwells with you, and shall be in you.
cards.t_text: And there is no time at which the works of men can be hid; for on the heart itself have they been written down 'before the Lord'.

cards.note: *And the spirit of truth testifieth all things, and accuseth all; and the sinner is burnt up by his own heart, and cannot raise his face to the judge.* The Testament of Judah (DB ch 35 v.5) names *the spirit of truth* by the very title Yahusha (Jesus) uses — the Spirit who testifies all things and accuses, before whom the sinner is burnt up by his own heart. John 16:8's *And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment* walks the same architecture: the Comforter, the Spirit of truth, does the reproving / accusing work the Hebrew library already named the spirit of truth doing. The convicting work is not a new office; it is the spirit of truth the patriarch named, now sent from the Father by the Son.
cards.s_text: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
cards.t_text: And the spirit of truth testifieth all things, and accuseth all; and the sinner is burnt up 'by his own heart', and cannot raise his face 'to the judge'.

cards.note: *And thereupon the princes and powers of that world will worship Thee.* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:15). The enthronement and the worship come as one motion — exactly the order of Hebrews 1, where the firstbegotten brought into the world is worshipped by all the angels (Hebrews 1:6) and seated at the right hand above them (Hebrews 1:13). The princes and powers bow to the Son; the worship belongs to him because he is Elohim enthroned, not a creature elevated.
cards.s_text: And again, when he brings in the firstbegotten into the world, he says, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.
cards.t_text: And thereupon the princes and powers of that world will worship Thee."

cards.note: *And afterwards from the angels of death Thou wilt ascend to Thy place. And Thou wilt not be transformed in each heaven, but in glory wilt Thou ascend and sit on My right hand.* (Ascension of Isaiah 10:14). The Father's own word to the Son in the vision sets the whole shape of Hebrews 1: the Son descends, conquers death, and *in glory* ascends to *sit on My right hand* — the very session Hebrews names, *sat down on the right hand of the Majesty on high* (Hebrews 1:3) and *Sit on my right hand* (Hebrews 1:13). The Formed who took flesh remains who he was; the Father seats him at the right hand and the powers are made to worship.
cards.s_text: And again, when he brings in the firstbegotten into the world, he says, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.
cards.t_text: And afterwards from the angels of death Thou wilt ascend to Thy place. And Thou wilt not be transformed in each heaven, but in glory wilt Thou ascend and sit on My right hand.

cards.note: *And then all the angels drew nigh and worshipped and gave praise.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:29). The angels themselves — not ranked beside the Son but bowed before him — *drew nigh and worshipped.* This is the answer Hebrews presses: *unto which of the angels said he at any time...* (Hebrews 1:5,13). To no angel is worship rendered; the angels are the ones who render it. The firstbegotten receives what belongs to Elohim alone.
cards.s_text: And again, when he brings in the firstbegotten into the world, he says, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.
cards.t_text: And then all the angels drew nigh and worshipped and gave praise.

cards.note: *And after I had seen Him, all the righteous whom I had seen and also the angels whom I had seen came to Him. And Adam and Abel and Seth and all the righteous first drew near and worshipped Him, and they all praised Him with one voice, and I myself also gave praise with them, and my giving of praise was as theirs.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:28). The seer is shown the very scene Hebrews announces — *let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him* (Hebrews 1:6). The Glorious One whose glory surpassed all is worshipped by Adam and the righteous and by the angelic host together; the worship Hebrews commands for the firstbegotten is the worship the seer beheld in the seventh heaven, given to the Son alone.
cards.s_text: And again, when he brings in the firstbegotten into the world, he says, And let all the angels of Elohim (God) worship him.
cards.t_text: And after I had seen Him, all the righteous whom I had seen and also the angels whom I had seen came to Him. And Adam and Abel and Seth and all the righteous first drew near and worshipped Him, and they all praised Him with one voice, and I myself also gave praise with them, and my giving of praise was as theirs.

cards.note: *And as I stood alone and looked, I saw behind the living creatures a chariot with fiery wheels, each wheel full of eyes round about; and over the wheels was a throne, which I saw, and this was covered with fire, and fire encircled it round about, and lo, an indescribable fire environed a fiery host.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:9). Abraham too was carried up and saw the throne-chariot — *a chariot with fiery wheels, each wheel full of eyes round about; and over the wheels was a throne... covered with fire.* It is the throne John sees set in heaven, *and one sat on the throne* (Revelation 4:2), with the lightnings proceeding out of it (Revelation 4:5). The same fiery throne-chariot of Ezekiel runs through the restored library: the seers of Yashar'el (Israel) beheld one throne, the throne of the living Elohim (God).
cards.s_text: And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne.
cards.t_text: And as I stood alone and looked, I saw behind the living creatures a chariot with fiery wheels, each wheel full of eyes round about; and over the wheels was a throne, which I saw, and this was covered with fire, and fire encircled it round about, and lo, an indescribable fire environed a fiery host.

cards.note: *And as the fire raised itself up, ascending into the height, I saw under the fire a throne of fire, and, round about it, all-seeing ones, reciting the song; and under the throne four fiery living creatures singing, and their appearance was one, each one of them with four faces.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:3). The restored library sets the same four beneath the same throne: *under the throne four fiery living creatures singing... each one of them with four faces,* surrounded by *all-seeing ones.* So John sees *in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne... four beasts full of eyes before and behind* (Revelation 4:6). The all-seeing throne-bearers of Abraham's vision are John's eye-filled living creatures, the cherubim of the one throne.
cards.s_text: And before the throne there was a sea of glass like unto crystal: and in the midst of the throne, and round about the throne, were four beasts full of eyes before and behind.
cards.t_text: And as the fire raised itself up, ascending into the height, I saw under the fire a throne of fire, and, round about it, all-seeing ones, reciting the song; and under the throne four fiery living creatures singing, and their appearance was one, each one of them with four faces.

cards.note: *And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.* (Revelation 4:8). *And such was the appearance of their countenances, of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies, so that the four creatures had sixteen faces; and each had six wings from their shoulders, and their sides, and their loins.* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:4). John sees four beasts with six wings each, full of eyes, who rest not day and night as they say Holy, holy, holy. The verse before gives their four faces: *And the first beast was like a lion, and the second beast like a calf, and the third beast had a face as a man, and the fourth beast was like a flying eagle.* (Revelation 4:7). Abraham is shown the same creatures under the throne: a lion, a man, an ox and an eagle, with six wings each. Two witnesses see the same four faces and the same six wings around the throne.
cards.s_text: And the four beasts had each of them six wings about him; and they were full of eyes within: and they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which was, and is, and is to come.
cards.t_text: And such was the appearance of their countenances, of a lion, of a man, of an ox, of an eagle: four heads were upon their bodies, so that the four creatures had sixteen faces; and each had six wings from their shoulders, and their sides, and their loins.

cards.note: *And I fell on my face to worship him, but the angel who conducted me did not permit me, but said unto me: "Worship neither throne nor angel..."* (Ascension of Isaiah 7:21). John's very gesture — *I fell at his feet to worship him* (Revelation 19:10) — is Isaiah's in his ascent, and the angel's refusal is the same: he will not permit the worship, for *I am not thy lord, but thy fellow servant* (Ascension of Isaiah 8:5). Throughout the apocalyptic seers the rule holds unbroken: the conducting angel forbids the worship and turns it back to the One.
cards.s_text: And I fell at his feet to worship him. And he said unto me, See you do it not: I am your fellowservant, and of your brethren that have the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus): worship Elohim (God): for the testimony of Yahusha (Jesus) is the spirit of prophecy.
cards.t_text: And I fell on my face to worship him, but the angel who conducted me did not permit me, but said unto me: "Worship neither throne nor angel which belongs to the six heavens—for for this cause I was sent to conduct thee—until I tell thee in the seventh heaven.

cards.note: Genesis 1:27 — *So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.* The making of Adam and Eve that Tobit 8:6 recalls as the pattern of his own marriage.
cards.s_text: You madest Adam, and gavest him Eve his wife for an helper and stay: of them came mankind: you have said, It is not good that man should be alone; let us make to him an aid like to himself.
cards.t_text: So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.

cards.note: Titus 3:5 - *Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit);* The cleansing sea Adam may not reach by his own going in 1 Adam and Eve 1:5 answers to the washing of regeneration granted not by works but by mercy.
cards.s_text: But when Elohim (God) made Adam go out of the garden, He did not place him on the border of it northward. This was so that he and Eve would not be able to go near to the sea of water where they could wash themselves in it, be cleansed from their sins, erase the transgression they had committed, and be no longer reminded of it in the thought of their punishment.
cards.t_text: Not by works of righteousness which we have done, but according to his mercy he saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit);

cards.note: Lamentations 3:22 - *It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.* That Adam is preserved and provided a dwelling rather than destroyed in 1 Adam and Eve 1:8 is the unfailing mercy that keeps the fallen from being consumed.
cards.s_text: Again, also, because Elohim (God) is merciful and of great pity, and governs all things in a way that He alone knows--He made our father Adam live in the western border of the garden, because on that side the earth is very broad.
cards.t_text: It is of the LORD’S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.

cards.note: Psalm 103:14 - *For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.* The Elohim who governs Adam's dwelling in pity in 1 Adam and Eve 1:8 is the Father who knows the frame of the man He made of dust.
cards.s_text: Again, also, because Elohim (God) is merciful and of great pity, and governs all things in a way that He alone knows--He made our father Adam live in the western border of the garden, because on that side the earth is very broad.
cards.t_text: For he knows our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.

cards.note: 1 Peter 3:21 - *The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward Elohim (God),) by the resurrection of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):* The saving, repentance-bearing water of 1 Adam and Eve 1:4 is the figure Peter names baptism, joined to the resurrection.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) created that sea of his own good pleasure, for He knew what would come of the man He would make; so that after he had left the garden, on account of his transgression, men should be born in the earth. Among them are righteous ones who will die, whose souls Elohim (God) would raise at the last day; when all of them will return to their flesh, bathe in the water of that sea, and repent of their sins.
cards.t_text: The like figure whereunto even baptism does also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward Elohim (God),) by the resurrection of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ):

cards.note: John 6:39 - *And this is the Father's will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.* The very last-day raising promised over Adam's sea in 1 Adam and Eve 1:4 is the Father's will the Messiah declares He came to do.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) created that sea of his own good pleasure, for He knew what would come of the man He would make; so that after he had left the garden, on account of his transgression, men should be born in the earth. Among them are righteous ones who will die, whose souls Elohim (God) would raise at the last day; when all of them will return to their flesh, bathe in the water of that sea, and repent of their sins.
cards.t_text: And this is the Father’s will which has sent me, that of all which he has given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.

cards.note: Daniel 12:2 - *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* The souls Elohim would raise at the last day to return to their flesh in 1 Adam and Eve 1:4 are the sleepers in the dust whom Daniel sees awake.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) created that sea of his own good pleasure, for He knew what would come of the man He would make; so that after he had left the garden, on account of his transgression, men should be born in the earth. Among them are righteous ones who will die, whose souls Elohim (God) would raise at the last day; when all of them will return to their flesh, bathe in the water of that sea, and repent of their sins.
cards.t_text: And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.

cards.note: Ezekiel 36:25 - *Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.* The pure sea that washes the righteous clean of their sins in 1 Adam and Eve 1:4 is the clean water Yahuah promises to sprinkle for cleansing.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) created that sea of his own good pleasure, for He knew what would come of the man He would make; so that after he had left the garden, on account of his transgression, men should be born in the earth. Among them are righteous ones who will die, whose souls Elohim (God) would raise at the last day; when all of them will return to their flesh, bathe in the water of that sea, and repent of their sins.
cards.t_text: Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you.

cards.note: Genesis 4:16 - *And Cain went out from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.* The geography Adam is given in 1 Adam and Eve 1:8 is the very stage of the two seed-lines, the field east of Eden where Cain would later wander.
cards.s_text: Again, also, because Elohim (God) is merciful and of great pity, and governs all things in a way that He alone knows--He made our father Adam live in the western border of the garden, because on that side the earth is very broad.
cards.t_text: And Cain went out from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

cards.note: Jubilees 3:9 - *And after Adam had completed forty days in the land where he had been created, we brought him into the Garden of Eden to till and keep it, but his wife they brought in on the eightieth day, and after this she entered into the Garden of Eden.* Jubilees keeps the same memory of the holy garden into which Adam was set, the ground from which 1 Adam and Eve 1:1 measures the world eastward.
cards.s_text: On the third day, Elohim (God) planted the garden in the east of the earth, on the border of the world eastward, beyond which, towards the sun-rising, one finds nothing but water, that encompasses the whole world, and reaches to the borders of heaven.
cards.t_text: And after Adam had completed forty days in the land where he had been created, we brought him into the Garden of Eden to till and keep it, but his wife they brought in on the eightieth day, and after this she entered into the Garden of Eden.

cards.note: Genesis 3:24 - *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* Adam's appointed cave in the rock below the garden in 1 Adam and Eve 1:9 sits outside the flaming sword that now keeps the way back.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) commanded him to live there in a cave in a rock--the Cave of Treasures below the garden.
cards.t_text: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

cards.note: Genesis 2:8 - *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.* The Conflict's garden planted in the east is the very garden of Eden Moses set eastward in 1 Adam and Eve 1:1.
cards.s_text: On the third day, Elohim (God) planted the garden in the east of the earth, on the border of the world eastward, beyond which, towards the sun-rising, one finds nothing but water, that encompasses the whole world, and reaches to the borders of heaven.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.

cards.note: Psalm 103:8 — *Yahuah (LORD) is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.* The pity that sends the Word to raise the fallen pair in 1 Adam and Eve 2:5 is this plenteous covenant mercy.
cards.s_text: Therefore Elohim (God) had pity on them; and when He saw them fallen before the gate of the garden, He sent His Word to our father, Adam and Eve, and raised them from their fallen state.
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) is merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and plenteous in mercy.

cards.note: Hebrews 1:1 — *Elohim (God), who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets.* The Word sent to Adam in 1 Adam and Eve 2:5 begins that long speaking of Elohim to the fathers.
cards.s_text: Therefore Elohim (God) had pity on them; and when He saw them fallen before the gate of the garden, He sent His Word to our father, Adam and Eve, and raised them from their fallen state.
cards.t_text: Elohim (God), who at sundry times and in divers manners spake in time past unto the fathers by the prophets,

cards.note: John 1:3 — *All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.* The Word that comes to the gate in 1 Adam and Eve 2:5 is the one by whom the broad earth they fear was itself made.
cards.s_text: Therefore Elohim (God) had pity on them; and when He saw them fallen before the gate of the garden, He sent His Word to our father, Adam and Eve, and raised them from their fallen state.
cards.t_text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word Elohim sends to raise Adam and Eve in 1 Adam and Eve 2:5 is the eternal Logos, Elohim Himself.
cards.s_text: Therefore Elohim (God) had pity on them; and when He saw them fallen before the gate of the garden, He sent His Word to our father, Adam and Eve, and raised them from their fallen state.
cards.t_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The grace and bright nature lost in 1 Adam and Eve 2:4 is the very glory the Word restores when He is made flesh.
cards.s_text: And because, when they were in the garden they were filled with the grace of a bright nature, and they had not hearts turned toward earthly things.
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: Psalm 103:14 — *For he knoweth our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.* Even as the bright nature fades in 1 Adam and Eve 2:4, Yahuah's pity reckons with the frame He formed.
cards.s_text: And because, when they were in the garden they were filled with the grace of a bright nature, and they had not hearts turned toward earthly things.
cards.t_text: For he knows our frame; he remembereth that we are dust.

cards.note: Genesis 3:19 — *In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.* The grace of a bright nature is exchanged for hearts now bound to the earthly things of 1 Adam and Eve 2:4, the dust to which man returns.
cards.s_text: And because, when they were in the garden they were filled with the grace of a bright nature, and they had not hearts turned toward earthly things.
cards.t_text: In the sweat of your face shall you eat bread, till you return unto the ground; for out of it were you taken: for dust you are, and unto dust shall you return.

cards.note: Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* The bright nature of 1 Adam and Eve 2:4 is the glory of the first-formed man, dust quickened by the breath of Elohim.
cards.s_text: And because, when they were in the garden they were filled with the grace of a bright nature, and they had not hearts turned toward earthly things.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.

cards.note: Genesis 3:18 — *Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to thee; and thou shalt eat the herb of the field.* The earth of stones large and small that terrifies them in 1 Adam and Eve 2:2 is the thorn-bearing ground of the curse.
cards.s_text: And when they came to the opening of the gate of the garden, and saw the broad earth spread before them, covered with stones large and small, and with sand, they feared and trembled, and fell on their faces, from the fear that came over them; and they were as dead.
cards.t_text: Thorns also and thistles shall it bring forth to you; and you shall eat the herb of the field;

cards.note: Genesis 3:17 — *And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.* The strange land Adam never saw (1 Adam and Eve 2:3) is the cursed ground he must now till.
cards.s_text: Because--whereas until this time they had been in the garden land, beautifully planted with all manner of trees--they now saw themselves, in a strange land, which they knew not, and had never seen.
cards.t_text: And unto Adam he said, Because you have hearkened unto the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree, of which I commanded you, saying, You shall not eat of it: cursed is the ground for your sake; in sorrow shall you eat of it all the days of your life;

cards.note: Genesis 3:24 — *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* The fear that lays Adam and Eve as dead before the gate (1 Adam and Eve 2:2) is the dread of the barred way home.
cards.s_text: And when they came to the opening of the gate of the garden, and saw the broad earth spread before them, covered with stones large and small, and with sand, they feared and trembled, and fell on their faces, from the fear that came over them; and they were as dead.
cards.t_text: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

cards.note: Genesis 3:23 — *Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.* The walking onto the unknown ground in 1 Adam and Eve 2:1 is this sending-forth lived out step by step.
cards.s_text: But when our father Adam, and Eve, went out of the garden, they walked the ground on their feet, not knowing they were walking.
cards.t_text: Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

cards.note: Jubilees 3:29 — *And He sent out of the Garden of Eden all flesh that was in the Garden of Eden, and all flesh was scattered according to its kinds, and according to its types to the places which had been created for them.* The same primeval record of the expulsion that frames the gate-scene of 1 Adam and Eve 3:10 — one history of the driven-out, kept in both books.
cards.s_text: And again, when Adam was by the gate of the garden, and saw the cherub with a sword of flashing fire in his hand, and the cherub grew angry and frowned at him, both Adam and Eve became afraid of him, and thought he meant to put them to death. So they fell on their faces, trembled with fear.
cards.t_text: And He sent out of the Garden of Eden all flesh that was in the Garden of Eden, and all flesh was scattered according to its kinds, and according to its types to the places which had been created for them.

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The "Word of Yahuah" who comes to Adam and Eve and raises them up (1 Adam and Eve 3:15) is the Word who would be made flesh and dwell among men.
cards.s_text: And the Word of Yahuah (Lord) came to Adam and Eve, and raised them up.
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: Psalms 91:11 — *For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.* The Angel Elohim sends "to keep the garden" (1 Adam and Eve 3:14) is the same mercy that gives His angels charge to keep His own.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) had pity on them, and showed them mercy, and sent His Angel to keep the garden.
cards.t_text: For he shall give his angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways.

cards.note: Genesis 3:24 — *So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* The cherub "with a sword of flashing fire" at the gate (1 Adam and Eve 3:10) is the very cherub and flaming sword Yahuah set to keep the way of the tree of life.
cards.s_text: And again, when Adam was by the gate of the garden, and saw the cherub with a sword of flashing fire in his hand, and the cherub grew angry and frowned at him, both Adam and Eve became afraid of him, and thought he meant to put them to death. So they fell on their faces, trembled with fear.
cards.t_text: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.

cards.note: 1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* The covenant Elohim makes with the lifted-up Adam (1 Adam and Eve 3:9) is fulfilled when the Son is manifested to destroy the devil's works.
cards.s_text: And as Adam went to it he feared, trembled and fell down; but Elohim (God) in His mercy lifted him up, and then made this covenant with him.
cards.t_text: Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* The mercy that lifts the fallen Adam and seals a covenant (1 Adam and Eve 3:9) carries the same promise — Satan bruised under foot shortly.
cards.s_text: And as Adam went to it he feared, trembled and fell down; but Elohim (God) in His mercy lifted him up, and then made this covenant with him.
cards.t_text: And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The covenant made "by the tree where Eve took of the fruit" (1 Adam and Eve 3:7) is the seed-promise spoken over the serpent at that same fall.
cards.s_text: But before that, Elohim (God) had made this covenant with our father, Adam, in the same terms, before he came out of the garden, when he was by the tree where Eve took of the fruit and gave it to him to eat.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Hebrews 1:2 — *Hath in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he hath appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;* The Word promised to save "when the five and a half days are fulfilled" (1 Adam and Eve 3:2) is the Son who in the last days speaks and by whom the worlds were made.
cards.s_text: Yes, the Word that will again save you when the five and a half days are fulfilled."
cards.t_text: Has in these last days spoken unto us by his Son, whom he has appointed heir of all things, by whom also he made the worlds;

cards.note: 1 Peter 1:20 — *Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you,* The Saviour appointed to a fixed term in 1 Adam and Eve 3:6 is the Lamb foreordained before the foundation of the world.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) in his mercy for Adam who was made after His own image and likeness, explained to him, that these were 5,000 and 500 years; and how One would then come and save him and his descendants.
cards.t_text: Who verily was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but was manifest in these last times for you,

cards.note: Galatians 4:4 — *But when the fulness of the time was come, Elohim (God) sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,* The "5,000 and 500 years" until One comes to save (1 Adam and Eve 3:6) is the fulness of time at which the Son was sent forth.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) in his mercy for Adam who was made after His own image and likeness, explained to him, that these were 5,000 and 500 years; and how One would then come and save him and his descendants.
cards.t_text: But when the fulness of the time was come, Elohim (God) sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

cards.note: Colossians 1:16 — *For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:* The Word "that created you" in 1 Adam and Eve 3:1 is the One by whom all things were made.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) said to Adam, "I have ordained on this earth days and years, and you and your descendants shall live and walk in them, until the days and years are fulfilled; when I shall send the Word that created you, and against which you have transgressed, the Word that made you come out of the garden, and that raised you when you were fallen.
cards.t_text: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:

cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The Word who "will again save you" (1 Adam and Eve 3:2) is the Word made flesh to come and save what was fallen.
cards.s_text: Yes, the Word that will again save you when the five and a half days are fulfilled."
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: John 1:3 — *All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.* This is exactly the Word "that created you" of 1 Adam and Eve 3:1 — the Maker of Adam is the Saviour of Adam.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) said to Adam, "I have ordained on this earth days and years, and you and your descendants shall live and walk in them, until the days and years are fulfilled; when I shall send the Word that created you, and against which you have transgressed, the Word that made you come out of the garden, and that raised you when you were fallen.
cards.t_text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word Elohim promises to send Adam is the One who was with Elohim from the beginning, naming the Logos at the very first day outside Eden in 1 Adam and Eve 3:1.
cards.s_text: Elohim (God) said to Adam, "I have ordained on this earth days and years, and you and your descendants shall live and walk in them, until the days and years are fulfilled; when I shall send the Word that created you, and against which you have transgressed, the Word that made you come out of the garden, and that raised you when you were fallen.
cards.t_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* Adam's refusal to be again a transgressor in 1 Adam & Eve 4:12 is mercy keeping the seed-line through which the head-bruising Seed will come.
cards.s_text: But he bowed to Elohim's (God's) orders; and said to himself, "Unless I enter the cave, I shall again be a transgressor."
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Philippians 2:8 — *And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.* The humbled obedience Adam shows in 1 Adam & Eve 4:12 is perfected by the Seed who is obedient unto death.
cards.s_text: But he bowed to Elohim's (God's) orders; and said to himself, "Unless I enter the cave, I shall again be a transgressor."
cards.t_text: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.

cards.note: Hebrews 5:8 — *Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;* Adam's bowing to Elohim's order rather than transgress in 1 Adam & Eve 4:12 foreshadows the obedience the Son learns through suffering.
cards.s_text: But he bowed to Elohim's (God's) orders; and said to himself, "Unless I enter the cave, I shall again be a transgressor."
cards.t_text: Though he were a Son, yet learned he obedience by the things which he suffered;

cards.note: Genesis 3:19 — *In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.* The place of punishment in 1 Adam & Eve 4:3 is the dust-bound mortality Genesis pronounces over Adam.
cards.s_text: And as they came to it, Adam cried over himself and said to Eve, "Look at this cave that is to be our prison in this world, and a place of punishment!
cards.t_text: In the sweat of your face shall you eat bread, till you return unto the ground; for out of it were you taken: for dust you are, and unto dust shall you return.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 5:4 — *For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.* The gloom Adam groans under in 1 Adam & Eve 4:5 is the burdened tabernacle Paul says shall be swallowed up of life.
cards.s_text: What is this rock, by the side of those groves? What is the gloom of this cavern, compared with the light of the garden?
cards.t_text: For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:16 — *But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore Elohim (God) is not ashamed to be called their Elohim (God): for he hath prepared for them a city.* The exile of 1 Adam & Eve 4:3 sets the whole line longing for the city Yahuah has prepared.
cards.s_text: And as they came to it, Adam cried over himself and said to Eve, "Look at this cave that is to be our prison in this world, and a place of punishment!
cards.t_text: But now they desire a better country, that is, an heavenly: wherefore Elohim (God) is not ashamed to be called their Elohim (God): for he has prepared for them a city.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:13 — *These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.* The cave-prison of 1 Adam & Eve 4:3 makes Adam the first stranger and pilgrim on the earth.
cards.s_text: And as they came to it, Adam cried over himself and said to Eve, "Look at this cave that is to be our prison in this world, and a place of punishment!
cards.t_text: These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off, and were persuaded of them, and embraced them, and confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* Even as Adam grieves the altered flesh, the seed-promise already runs through the woman's line he and Eve carry in 1 Adam & Eve 4:2.
cards.s_text: And indeed, when Adam looked at his flesh, that was altered, he cried bitterly, he and Eve, over what they had done. And they walked and went gently down into the Cave of Treasures.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 4:7 — *But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of Elohim (God), and not of us.* The altered flesh Adam weeps over in 1 Adam & Eve 4:2 becomes the earthen vessel mercy fills.
cards.s_text: And indeed, when Adam looked at his flesh, that was altered, he cried bitterly, he and Eve, over what they had done. And they walked and went gently down into the Cave of Treasures.
cards.t_text: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of Elohim (God), and not of us.

cards.note: Romans 3:23 — *For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);* The flesh-darkened eyes of 1 Adam & Eve 4:9 are the falling-short of glory Paul declares over all.
cards.s_text: But now we do not see as we did; our eyes have become of flesh; they cannot see like they used to see before."
cards.t_text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of Elohim (God);

cards.note: Psalm 8:5 — *For thou hast made him a little lower than the angels, and hast crowned him with glory and honour.* The eyes that once *beheld angels praising in heaven* (1 Adam & Eve 4:8) were the crown of glory man has now dimmed.
cards.s_text: And Adam said to Eve, "Look at your eyes, and at mine, which before beheld angels praising in heaven; and they too, without ceasing.
cards.t_text: For you have made him a little lower than the angels, and have crowned him with glory and honour.

cards.note: Jubilees 3:32 — *And on the new moon of the fourth month, Adam and his wife went forth from the Garden of Eden, and they dwelt in the land of ’Eldâ, in the land of their creation.* Jubilees records the same going-forth from the garden that 1 Adam & Eve 4:1 mourns.
cards.s_text: But Adam and Eve cried for having come out of the garden, their first home.
cards.t_text: And on the new moon of the fourth month, Adam and his wife went forth from the Garden of Eden, and they dwelt in the land of ’Eldâ, in the land of their creation.

cards.note: Romans 8:22 — *For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.* The first cry of the first pair in 1 Adam & Eve 4:1 is the opening note of the creation-wide groan Paul still hears.
cards.s_text: But Adam and Eve cried for having come out of the garden, their first home.
cards.t_text: For we know that the whole creation groaneth and travaileth in pain together until now.

cards.note: Genesis 3:17 — *And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life;* The stony cursed soil Adam laments in 1 Adam & Eve 4:7 is the ground Yahuah cursed for his sake.
cards.s_text: What is the soil of this cave compared with the garden land? This earth, strewed with stones; and that, planted with delicious fruit trees?"
cards.t_text: And unto Adam he said, Because you have hearkened unto the voice of your wife, and have eaten of the tree, of which I commanded you, saying, You shall not eat of it: cursed is the ground for your sake; in sorrow shall you eat of it all the days of your life;

cards.note: Genesis 3:23 — *Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.* The driving-out that Genesis states is the wound Adam and Eve weep over in 1 Adam & Eve 4:1.
cards.s_text: But Adam and Eve cried for having come out of the garden, their first home.
cards.t_text: Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.

cards.note: 1 Timothy 2:15 — *Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.* As Eve fears to stand *one and alone* in 1 Adam and Eve 5:8, Sha'ul holds out the woman's saving hope through the seed and the faith she keeps.
cards.s_text: But if You do not bring him back to life, then, O Elohim (God), take away my own soul, that I be like him, and leave me not in this dungeon, one and alone; for I could not stand alone in this world, but with him only.
cards.t_text: Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.

cards.note: Genesis 2:24 — *Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.* Eve's plea that she and Adam *die the same day* in 1 Adam and Eve 5:13 is the one-flesh bond of Eden refusing to be sundered even by death.
cards.s_text: But if You will not give him life, then take me, even me, like him; that we both may die the same day."
cards.t_text: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.

cards.note: Romans 5:17 — *For if by one man's offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).* The life and standing Eve begs for Adam in 1 Adam and Eve 5:7 is the reign-in-life that grace secures over the fall.
cards.s_text: Don't take away his soul right now; but let him live that he may stand after the measure of his repentance, and do Your will, as before his death.
cards.t_text: For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ).)

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 7:10 — *For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.* Eve's prayer that Adam be raised *that he may cry and repent* in 1 Adam and Eve 5:6 is exactly the sorrow-unto-life Sha'ul distinguishes from the world's sorrow-unto-death.
cards.s_text: O Elohim (God), look at this Your servant fallen in this manner, and bring him back to life, that he may cry and repent of his transgression which he committed through me.
cards.t_text: For godly sorrow works repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world works death.

cards.note: Jubilees 3:5 — *And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and He took for the woman one rib from amongst his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from amongst his ribs, and He built up the flesh in its stead, and built the woman.* The restored books keep one primeval history: Jubilees tells the same making of woman that Eve recites in 1 Adam and Eve 5:9-10.
cards.s_text: For You, O Elohim (God), caused him to fall asleep, and took a bone from his side, and restored the flesh in the place of it, by Your divine power.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah our Elohim (the LORD our God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon him, and he slept, and He took for the woman one rib from amongst his ribs, and this rib was the origin of the woman from amongst his ribs, and He built up the flesh in its stead, and built the woman.

cards.note: Genesis 2:23 — *And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.* Eve's cry that *I and he are one* in 1 Adam and Eve 5:11 echoes Adam's first word over her in Eden.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (Lord), I and he are one, and You, O Elohim (God), are our Creator, You are He who made us both in one day.
cards.t_text: And Adam said, This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man.

cards.note: Genesis 2:21 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof.* This is the very act Eve recounts to Yahuah in 1 Adam and Eve 5:9, the bone taken from Adam's side and the flesh restored.
cards.s_text: For You, O Elohim (God), caused him to fall asleep, and took a bone from his side, and restored the flesh in the place of it, by Your divine power.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof;

cards.note: Romans 5:12 — *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.* The fall from light into darkness Eve laments in 1 Adam and Eve 5:5 is the entrance of sin and death that Sha'ul traces back to Eden.
cards.s_text: For I alone caused Your servant to fall from the garden into this condemned land; from light into this darkness; and from the house of joy into this prison.
cards.t_text: Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

cards.note: 1 Timothy 2:14 — *And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.* Sha'ul's verdict matches Eve's own self-judgment in 1 Adam and Eve 5:5 that she alone brought Adam down.
cards.s_text: For I alone caused Your servant to fall from the garden into this condemned land; from light into this darkness; and from the house of joy into this prison.
cards.t_text: And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.

cards.note: Genesis 3:13 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.* Eve's plea that Yahuah forgive and not remember her sin in 1 Adam and Eve 5:4 unfolds the confession first wrung from her at the tree.
cards.s_text: Then she got up, spread her hands toward Elohim (God), appealing to Him for mercy and pity, and said, "O Elohim (God), forgive me my sin, the sin which I committed, and don't remember it against me.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) said unto the woman, What is this that you have done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.

cards.note: Genesis 3:6 — *And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.* This is the very deed Eve confesses in 1 Adam and Eve 5:5 when she says she alone caused Adam to fall from the garden.
cards.s_text: For I alone caused Your servant to fall from the garden into this condemned land; from light into this darkness; and from the house of joy into this prison.
cards.t_text: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.

cards.note: 1 John 3:8 — *Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.* Against the curse held over the hardened in 1 Adam and Eve 6:10 stands the Son manifested to destroy the works of the devil.
cards.s_text: But, if on the contrary, they still continue hardened in their transgression, they shall be under a curse forever."
cards.t_text: Whoever goes on sinning belongs to the devil, for the devil has been sinning from the very beginning. This is why the Son of Elohim (God) was revealed: to undo the works of the devil.

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* The mercy that punishes unto repentance in 1 Adam and Eve 6:9 looks to the day the Elohim of peace bruises Satan under His people's feet.
cards.s_text: For I am Elohim (God) the Creator, who, when I created My creatures, did not intend to destroy them. But after they had sorely roused My anger, I punished them with grievous plagues, until they repent.
cards.t_text: And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The Creator who *did not intend to destroy them* in 1 Adam and Eve 6:9 is the One who set the seed-promise that crushes the serpent's head.
cards.s_text: For I am Elohim (God) the Creator, who, when I created My creatures, did not intend to destroy them. But after they had sorely roused My anger, I punished them with grievous plagues, until they repent.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* The Satan who deceived them *by believing his words* in 1 Adam and Eve 6:7 is the liar and father of lies, a murderer from the beginning.
cards.s_text: But the wicked Satan did not keep his faith and had no good intent towards Me, that although I had created him, he considered Me to be useless, and sought the Godhead for himself; for this I hurled him down from heaven so that he could not remain in his first estate--it was he who made the tree appear pleasant in your eyes, until you ate of it, by believing his words.
