cards.note: John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* The same Word who counsels Adam in 73:2 would in the fulness of time take flesh to save the seed He had promised.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) approved Adam in what he had thought concerning this, and in the prayer he had offered in His presence; and the Word of Elohim (God) came to Adam and said to him, "O Adam, if only you had had this caution at first, before you came out of the garden into this land!"
cards.t_text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word of Elohim who comes and speaks to Adam in 1 Adam & Eve 73:2 is the eternal Logos, with Elohim from the beginning.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) approved Adam in what he had thought concerning this, and in the prayer he had offered in His presence; and the Word of Elohim (God) came to Adam and said to him, "O Adam, if only you had had this caution at first, before you came out of the garden into this land!"
cards.t_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).

cards.note: *Then Adam and Eve waited until Cain and his sister were forty days old, when Adam said to Eve, "We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children."* (1 Adam and Eve 74:9). *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 4:26). Adam and Eve wait until their children are forty days old and then say they will make an offering on the children's behalf. Genesis records that in the days of Enos men began to call upon the name of Yahuah (the LORD). Offering for the newborn is part of that calling: the first family brings its children before Elohim (God) at the start of their lives, and Genesis names the line in which the practice becomes known.
cards.s_text: Then Adam and Eve waited until Cain and his sister were forty days old, when Adam said to Eve, "We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children."
cards.t_text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Jubilees 3:27 — *And on that day on which Adam went forth from the garden, he offered as a sweet savour an offering, frankincense, galbanum, and stacte, and spices in the morning with the rising of the sun from the day when he covered his shame.* The parallel record shows Adam already an offerer from the day he left Eden, the same priestly hand that offers for the children at 1 Adam and Eve 74:9.
cards.s_text: Then Adam and Eve waited until Cain and his sister were forty days old, when Adam said to Eve, "We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children."
cards.t_text: And on that day on which Adam went forth from the garden, he offered as a sweet savour an offering, frankincense, galbanum, and stacte, and spices in the morning with the rising of the sun from the day when he covered his shame.

cards.note: Genesis 4:3 — *And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto Yahuah (LORD).* The offering Adam makes for his children at 1 Adam and Eve 74:9 is the same altar-practice his children will keep, the way kept before Sinai.
cards.s_text: Then Adam and Eve waited until Cain and his sister were forty days old, when Adam said to Eve, "We will make an offering and offer it up in behalf of the children."
cards.t_text: And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Hebrews 11:4 — *By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.* Against Cain the hater stands the righteous offerer, the parting of the two lines latent in the children of 1 Adam and Eve 74:6-8.
cards.s_text: But Luluwa means "beautiful," because she was more beautiful than her mother.
cards.t_text: By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaks.

cards.note: Jude 1:11 — *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.* Jude makes Cain a whole "way" — a lineage of works — which the womb-hatred named at 1 Adam and Eve 74:7 begins.
cards.s_text: The meaning of Cain is "hater," because he hated his sister in their mother's womb; before they came out of it. Therefore Adam named him Cain.
cards.t_text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:1 — *And in the third week in the second jubilee she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel, and in the fifth she gave birth to her daughter 'Âwân.* The parallel primeval record keeps the same sequence — Cain first, then a daughter — matching the first-born son and daughter of 1 Adam and Eve 74:5.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) looked at His maid-servant Eve, and delivered her, and she gave birth to her first-born son, and with him a daughter.
cards.t_text: And in the third week in the second jubilee she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel, and in the fifth she gave birth to her daughter ’Âwân.

cards.note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* John names the line Cain belongs to, confirming the hatred that 1 Adam and Eve 74:7 traces back to the womb.
cards.s_text: The meaning of Cain is "hater," because he hated his sister in their mother's womb; before they came out of it. Therefore Adam named him Cain.
cards.t_text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The enmity decreed at Eden's gate already burns in the womb when Cain hates his sister before birth at 1 Adam and Eve 74:7.
cards.s_text: The meaning of Cain is "hater," because he hated his sister in their mother's womb; before they came out of it. Therefore Adam named him Cain.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Genesis 4:1 — *And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from Yahuah (LORD).* The brief Genesis notice of the first conception is unfolded here into Adam's prayer and Eve's deliverance at 1 Adam and Eve 74:4-5.
cards.s_text: But when Adam saw the distress in which Eve was, he got up and prayed to Elohim (God), and said, "O Yahuah (Lord), look at me with the eye of Your mercy, and bring her out of her distress."
cards.t_text: And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Genesis 3:16 — *Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.* The narrator names this very sentence as the word being fulfilled in Eve's hard labour at 1 Adam and Eve 74:3.
cards.s_text: Adam then took Eve to that cave. When the time came for her to give birth, she strained a lot. Adam felt sorry, and he was very worried about her because she was close to death and the words of Elohim (God) to her were being fulfilled: "In suffering shall you bear a child, and in sorrow shall you bring forth a child."
cards.t_text: Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; in sorrow you shall bring forth children; and your desire shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you.

cards.note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The constant offerings and blessings of Adam's house in 1 Adam & Eve 75:10 are the same calling on the Name of Yahuah kept from the first generations.
cards.s_text: Adam and Eve did this until the children had been weaned. After they were weaned, Adam made an offering for the souls of his children in addition to the three times every week he made an offering for them.
cards.t_text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Matthew 2:11 — *And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.* The gold, incense, and myrrh of the Cave of Treasures whose tokens bless the children in 1 Adam & Eve 75:6 are the very gifts kept for the promised Saviour.
cards.s_text: But they returned not to the cave in which they were born; but came to the Cave of Treasures, in order that the children should go around in it, and be blessed with the tokens brought from the garden.
cards.t_text: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.

cards.note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* After the children of 1 Adam & Eve 75:13, the kept seed of the woman runs not through Abel but through the appointed Seth.
cards.s_text: He brought them to the Cave of Treasures, where they received a blessing, and then returned to the cave where they were born. After these children were born, Eve stopped having children.
cards.t_text: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:1 — *And in the third week in the second jubilee she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel, and in the fifth she gave birth to her daughter 'Âwân.* Jubilees, like 1 Adam & Eve 75:11, counts the daughters with the sons in this same primeval household.
cards.s_text: When the children were weaned, Eve again conceived, and when her pregnancy came to term, she gave birth to another son and daughter. They named the son Abel and the daughter Aklia.
cards.t_text: And in the third week in the second jubilee she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel, and in the fifth she gave birth to her daughter ’Âwân.

cards.note: Genesis 4:2 — *And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.* The birth of Abel named in 1 Adam & Eve 75:11 is the same second son Eve bears in Genesis.
cards.s_text: When the children were weaned, Eve again conceived, and when her pregnancy came to term, she gave birth to another son and daughter. They named the son Abel and the daughter Aklia.

They went to the altar, where Adam offered it up, as he was accustomed, asking Yahuah (Lord) to accept his offering.

cards.t_text: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, You fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.

cards.note: 1 Peter 5:8 — *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.* Cain striking and cursing his own mother in 78:12 is the adversary already devouring the household through the son he has lured.
cards.s_text: And he did not remain in the field, but he went to Eve, his mother, and beat her, and cursed her, and said to her, "Why are you planning to take my sister to wed her to my brother? Am I dead?"
cards.t_text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walks about, seeking whom he may devour:

cards.note: John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* When Cain opens his ears to Satan's speech in 78:11 he is leaning toward the father of lies, who will make him the first murderer.
cards.s_text: At these words of Satan Cain opened his ears, and leaned towards his speech.
cards.t_text: You are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father you will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 11:14 — *And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.* The disguise of a beautiful man of the field bearing gold and a garden in 78:6-9 is the deceiver's signature transformation.
cards.s_text: Meanwhile Satan came to Cain in the figure of a man of the field, and said to him, "Behold Adam and Eve have taken counsel together about the marriage of you two; and they have agreed to marry Abel's sister to you, and your sister to him.
cards.t_text: And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* Satan coming to Cain in 78:6 is the serpent's enmity carried into the second generation, striking now at the seed through the elder brother.
cards.s_text: Meanwhile Satan came to Cain in the figure of a man of the field, and said to him, "Behold Adam and Eve have taken counsel together about the marriage of you two; and they have agreed to marry Abel's sister to you, and your sister to him.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Jasher 1:22 — *And Abel answered Cain, saying, Surely Elohim who has made us in the earth, he will avenge my cause, and he will require my blood from you should you slay me, for Yahuah (the Lord) is the judge and arbiter...* Jasher gives righteous Abel's own confession of the avenging Judge, the same righteousness for which the ground would not receive him in 1 Adam & Eve 79:14.
cards.s_text: The muddy ground threw him up the first time, because he was not the first creation; and it threw him up the second time and would not receive him, because he was righteous and good, and was killed without a cause; and the ground threw him up the third time and would not receive him, that there might remain before his brother a witness against him.
cards.t_text: And Abel answered Cain, saying, Surely Elohim who has made us in the earth, he will avenge my cause, and he will require my blood from you should you slay me, for Yahuah (the Lord) is the judge and arbiter, and it is he who will requite man according to his evil, and the wicked man according to the wickedness that he may do upon earth.

cards.note: 1 John 3:10 — *In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of Elohim (God), neither he that loveth not his brother.* John sets the two brothers as the two seed-lines, the righteous-and-good Abel of 1 Adam & Eve 79:14 against the children of the devil.
cards.s_text: The muddy ground threw him up the first time, because he was not the first creation; and it threw him up the second time and would not receive him, because he was righteous and good, and was killed without a cause; and the ground threw him up the third time and would not receive him, that there might remain before his brother a witness against him.
cards.t_text: In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever does not righteousness is not of Elohim (God), neither he that loves not his brother.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:4 — *By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.* The witness the ground preserves in 1 Adam & Eve 79:14 is the very witness of faith that the New Testament says yet speaks though Abel is dead.
cards.s_text: The muddy ground threw him up the first time, because he was not the first creation; and it threw him up the second time and would not receive him, because he was righteous and good, and was killed without a cause; and the ground threw him up the third time and would not receive him, that there might remain before his brother a witness against him.
cards.t_text: By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaks.

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* Behind Cain's restraint in 1 Adam & Eve 79:26 stands the seed-promise of Genesis 3:15 — the serpent who struck through Cain will himself be crushed.
cards.s_text: And in the word of Elohim (God) that said, "I will put seven punishments on anyone who kills Cain," Elohim (God) was not seeking to kill Cain with the sword, but He sought to make him die of fasting, and praying and crying by hard rule, until the time that he was delivered from his sin.
cards.t_text: And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.

cards.note: Jude 1:11 — *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.* The cursed and trembling Cain of 1 Adam & Eve 79:18 becomes the New Testament's name for the way of the apostate seed.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) said to Cain, "Cursed be the earth that has drunk the blood of Abel your brother; and as for you, you will always be trembling and shaking; and this will be a mark on you so that whoever finds you, will kill you."
cards.t_text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

cards.note: Genesis 4:11 — *And now art thou cursed from the earth, which hath opened her mouth to receive thy brother’s blood from thy hand;* the curse on the ground that 1 Adam & Eve 79:22 hears as mercy — Elohim cursing the soil, not the murderer himself.
cards.s_text: And as to Elohim (God) saying to Cain, "Cursed be the ground that has drunk the blood of your brother." That also, was Elohim's (God's) mercy on Cain. For Elohim (God) did not curse him, but He cursed the ground; although it was not the ground that had killed Abel, and committed a wicked sin.
cards.t_text: And now are you cursed from the earth, which has opened her mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand;

cards.note: Genesis 4:15 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And Yahuah (LORD) set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.* The Torah's sevenfold word and protecting mark that 1 Adam & Eve 79:26 reads as Yahuah's mercy holding back the sword to call Cain to repentance.
cards.s_text: And in the word of Elohim (God) that said, "I will put seven punishments on anyone who kills Cain," Elohim (God) was not seeking to kill Cain with the sword, but He sought to make him die of fasting, and praying and crying by hard rule, until the time that he was delivered from his sin.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And Yahuah (LORD) set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:4 — *And Yahuah (God) reproved Cain because of Abel, because he had slain him, and he made him a fugitive on the earth because of the blood of his brother, and he cursed him upon the earth...* The older witness's reproof matching the Word's coming to question Cain in 1 Adam & Eve 79:16.
cards.s_text: Then was Elohim (God) angry, and much displeased at Abel's death; and He thundered from heaven, and lightnings went before Him, and the Word of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) came from heaven to Cain, and said to him, "Where is Abel your brother?"
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (God) reproved Cain because of Abel, because he had slain him, and he made him a fugitive on the earth because of the blood of his brother, and he cursed him upon the earth.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word of Yahuah who comes from heaven to Cain in 1 Adam & Eve 79:16 is the same Logos who was in the beginning, by whom all things were made.
cards.s_text: Then was Elohim (God) angry, and much displeased at Abel's death; and He thundered from heaven, and lightnings went before Him, and the Word of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) came from heaven to Cain, and said to him, "Where is Abel your brother?"
cards.t_text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).

cards.note: Genesis 4:9 — *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Cain, Where is Abel thy brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?* The Torah's exact exchange that 1 Adam & Eve 79:16-17 expands, the proud keeper's answer unchanged.
cards.s_text: Then Cain answered with a proud heart and a gruff voice, "How, O Elohim (God)? Am I my brother's keeper?"
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Cain, Where is Abel your brother? And he said, I know not: Am I my brother’s keeper?

cards.note: Jubilees 4:3 — *And he slew him in the field: and his blood cried from the ground to heaven, complaining because he had slain him.* The older witness keeps the crying blood that 1 Adam & Eve 79:9 shows the trembling earth refusing to swallow.
cards.s_text: But the earth, when the blood of righteous Abel fell on it, trembled, as it drank his blood, and would have destroyed Cain because of it.
cards.t_text: And he slew him in the field: and his blood cried from the ground to heaven, complaining because he had slain him.

cards.note: Revelation 6:10 — *And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Yahuah (Lord), holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?* The souls under the altar take up Abel's same plea for vengeance heard in 1 Adam & Eve 79:10 — the righteous seed still crying.
cards.s_text: And the blood of Abel cried mysteriously to Elohim (God), to avenge him of his murderer.
cards.t_text: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Yahuah (Lord), holy and true, do you not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?

cards.note: Matthew 23:35 — *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.* Yahusha names Abel's blood as the head of all the martyred righteous, the crying of 1 Adam & Eve 79:10 reaching to His own generation.
cards.s_text: And the blood of Abel cried mysteriously to Elohim (God), to avenge him of his murderer.
cards.t_text: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom you slew between the temple and the altar.

cards.note: Genesis 4:10 — *And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.* The Torah's word for the crying blood that 1 Adam & Eve 79:10 says cried mysteriously to Elohim to avenge the murder.
cards.s_text: And the blood of Abel cried mysteriously to Elohim (God), to avenge him of his murderer.
cards.t_text: And he said, What have you done? the voice of your brother’s blood cries unto me from the ground.

cards.note: Jasher 1:25 — *And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth...* Jasher keeps the weapon and the spilt blood that 1 Adam & Eve 79:7 shows oozing before Cain.
cards.s_text: Then Cain, the hard-hearted, and cruel murderer, took a large stone, and beat his brother's head with it, until his brains oozed out, and he wallowed in his blood, before him.
cards.t_text: And Cain hastened and rose up, and took the iron part of his ploughing instrument, with which he suddenly smote his brother and he slew him, and Cain spilt the blood of his brother Abel upon the earth, and the blood of Abel streamed upon the earth before the flock.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:2 — *And in the first (year) of the third jubilee, Cain slew Abel because Elohim (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel, and did not accept the offering of Cain.* The same murder dated in the older witness, naming the rejected offering that drove Cain's hand in 1 Adam & Eve 79:7.
cards.s_text: Then Cain, the hard-hearted, and cruel murderer, took a large stone, and beat his brother's head with it, until his brains oozed out, and he wallowed in his blood, before him.
cards.t_text: And in the first (year) of the third jubilee, Cain slew Abel because Elohim (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel, and did not accept the offering of Cain.

cards.note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.* John names the seed behind the staff of 1 Adam & Eve 79:7 — Cain was of the wicked one, the serpent striking at the righteous seed.
cards.s_text: Then Cain, the hard-hearted, and cruel murderer, took a large stone, and beat his brother's head with it, until his brains oozed out, and he wallowed in his blood, before him.
cards.t_text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

cards.note: Genesis 4:8 — *And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* The Torah's bare record of the murder that 1 Adam & Eve 79:5-7 retells in full, blow by blow, with the stone.
cards.s_text: Then Cain, the hard-hearted, and cruel murderer, took a large stone, and beat his brother's head with it, until his brains oozed out, and he wallowed in his blood, before him.
cards.t_text: And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:7 — *And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said "Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him."* Jubilees gives the same comfort-after-mourning that Adam prays toward in 2 Adam and Eve 1:9.
cards.s_text: But as for Adam and Eve, they came not together after Abel's funeral, for seven years. After this, however, Eve conceived; and while she was with child, Adam said to her, "Come, let us take an offering and offer it up unto Elohim (God), and ask Him to give us a fair child, in whom we may find comfort, and whom we may join in marriage to Abel's sister."
cards.t_text: And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said “Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.”

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* The offering Elohim accepts in 2 Adam and Eve 1:11 keeps the seed-line whose end is Satan bruised underfoot.
cards.s_text: And Elohim (God) heard Adam and accepted his offering. Then, they worshipped, Adam, Eve, and their daughter, and came down to the Cave of Treasures and placed a lamp in it, to burn by night and by day, before the body of Abel.
cards.t_text: And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The seed Adam prays for in 2 Adam and Eve 1:9 is the woman's seed of the first promise, kept alive after Cain's blow.
cards.s_text: But as for Adam and Eve, they came not together after Abel's funeral, for seven years. After this, however, Eve conceived; and while she was with child, Adam said to her, "Come, let us take an offering and offer it up unto Elohim (God), and ask Him to give us a fair child, in whom we may find comfort, and whom we may join in marriage to Abel's sister."
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The calling upon the Name begun in Seth's line is the very entreaty Adam makes at the altar in 2 Adam and Eve 1:10.
cards.s_text: Then they prepared an offering and brought it up to the altar, and offered it before Yahuah (Lord), and began to entreat Him to accept their offering, and to give them a good offspring.
cards.t_text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* The fair child Adam asks Yahuah to give in 2 Adam and Eve 1:9 is Seth, the appointed second seed.
cards.s_text: But as for Adam and Eve, they came not together after Abel's funeral, for seven years. After this, however, Eve conceived; and while she was with child, Adam said to her, "Come, let us take an offering and offer it up unto Elohim (God), and ask Him to give us a fair child, in whom we may find comfort, and whom we may join in marriage to Abel's sister."
cards.t_text: And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, has appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:9 — *And Cain took 'Âwân his sister to be his wife and she bare him Enoch at the close of the fourth jubilee. And in the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee, houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city, and called its name after the name of his son Enoch.* Jubilees records the same sister-marriage and multiplying line that fills Cain's place in 2 Adam and Eve 1:8.
cards.s_text: And in that place were many fruit trees and forest trees. His sister bare him children, who in their turn began to multiply by degrees until they filled that place.
cards.t_text: And Cain took ’Âwân his sister to be his wife and she bare him Enoch at the close of the fourth jubilee. And in the first year of the first week of the fifth jubilee, houses were built on the earth, and Cain built a city, and called its name after the name of his son Enoch.

cards.note: Jude 1:11 — *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.* The downward way Cain takes off the mountain in 2 Adam and Eve 1:7 becomes the very name of apostasy, 'the way of Cain.'
cards.s_text: He then went down to the bottom of the mountain, away from the garden, near to the place where he had killed his brother.
cards.t_text: Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core.

cards.note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The Cain who marries and departs without leave in 2 Adam and Eve 1:6 is named here as of the wicked one — the serpent's seed of Genesis 3:15.
cards.s_text: As for Cain, when the mourning for his brother was ended, he took his sister Luluwa and married her, without leave from his father and mother; for they could not keep him from her, by reason of their heavy heart.
cards.t_text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

cards.note: Genesis 4:17 — *And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.* The children who multiply and fill Cain's place in 2 Adam and Eve 1:8 are the line that builds the first city of the wicked seed.
cards.s_text: And in that place were many fruit trees and forest trees. His sister bare him children, who in their turn began to multiply by degrees until they filled that place.
cards.t_text: And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.

cards.note: Genesis 4:16 — *And Cain went out from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.* Cain's descent to the bottom of the mountain away from the garden in 2 Adam and Eve 1:7 is his going out from the presence of Yahuah.
cards.s_text: He then went down to the bottom of the mountain, away from the garden, near to the place where he had killed his brother.
cards.t_text: And Cain went out from the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.

cards.note: Hebrews 12:24 — *And to Yahusha (Jesus) the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaketh better things than that of Abel.* The blood Adam buries in myrrh in 2 Adam and Eve 1:4 still speaks, but the better blood it points to is the Mediator's own.
cards.s_text: And Adam carried him, his tears streaming down his face; and went to the Cave of Treasures, where he laid him, and wound him up with sweet spices and myrrh.
cards.t_text: And to Yahusha (Jesus) the mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, that speaks better things than that of Abel.

cards.note: John 19:40 — *Then took they the body of Yahusha (Jesus), and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Yahudim (Jews) is to bury.* The Saviour's body is wound in spices exactly as Adam wound up Abel with sweet spices and myrrh in 2 Adam and Eve 1:4.
cards.s_text: And Adam carried him, his tears streaming down his face; and went to the Cave of Treasures, where he laid him, and wound him up with sweet spices and myrrh.
cards.t_text: Then took they the body of Yahusha (Jesus), and wound it in linen clothes with the spices, as the manner of the Yahudim (Jews) is to bury.

cards.note: John 19:39 — *And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Yahusha (Jesus) by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.* The myrrh Adam winds about righteous Abel in 2 Adam and Eve 1:4 is brought again for the burial of the righteous One.
cards.s_text: And Adam carried him, his tears streaming down his face; and went to the Cave of Treasures, where he laid him, and wound him up with sweet spices and myrrh.
cards.t_text: And there came also Nicodemus, which at the first came to Yahusha (Jesus) by night, and brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about an hundred pound weight.

cards.note: Matthew 2:11 — *And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.* The gold, incense, and myrrh of the Cave of Treasures where Adam buries Abel in 2 Adam and Eve 1:4 are the very gifts opened before the Messiah.
cards.s_text: And Adam carried him, his tears streaming down his face; and went to the Cave of Treasures, where he laid him, and wound him up with sweet spices and myrrh.
cards.t_text: And when they were come into the house, they saw the young child with Mary his mother, and fell down, and worshipped him: and when they had opened their treasures, they presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.

cards.s_text: And they found him lying on the earth, killed, and beasts around him; while they wept and cried because of this just one. From his body, by reason of its purity, went forth a smell of sweet spices.

cards.s_text: And they found him lying on the earth, killed, and beasts around him; while they wept and cried because of this just one. From his body, by reason of its purity, went forth a smell of sweet spices.

cards.s_text: And they found him lying on the earth, killed, and beasts around him; while they wept and cried because of this just one. From his body, by reason of its purity, went forth a smell of sweet spices.

cards.note: Genesis 4:10 — *And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground.* The body Adam and Eve weep over in 2 Adam and Eve 1:3 is the blood whose cry has already reached heaven.

cards.t_text: And he said, What have you done? the voice of your brother’s blood cries unto me from the ground.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:12–13 — *He began to call on the name of Yahuah (God) on the earth. And in the seventh jubilee in the third week Enos took Nôâm his sister to be his wife, and she bare him a son in the third year of the fifth week, and he called his name Kenan.* Jubilees keeps the same memory — the calling on the Name begun in Seth's line — the worship the Conflict shows in Adam's accepted offering for Seth.
cards.s_text: Then they returned, and took an offering, and went to the mountain and offered it up, for the babe; and Elohim (God) accepted their offering, and sent His blessing upon them, and upon their son Seth; and they came back to the Cave of Treasures.

cards.note: Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* The washing for purification and the offering in the line of Seth open the way that becomes the calling on the Name of Yahuah in Seth's own house.
cards.s_text: And they came to a river of water, where Adam and his daughter washed themselves, b~ cause of their sorrow for Abel; but Eve and the babe washed for purification.
cards.t_text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* Seth fasting and praying fervently is the kept seed pressing toward the promised bruising of Satan's head, the seed-war begun in Genesis 3:15 finished in the Messiah.
cards.s_text: But Seth waxed in stature and in strength; and began to fast and pray, fervently.
cards.t_text: And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.

cards.note: Genesis 3:15 — *And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.* The two lines that remain of Adam's children are the very enmity of seed against seed, the serpent's offspring against the woman's kept seed.
cards.s_text: As for Adam, he knew not again his wife Eve, all the days of his life; neither was any more offspring born of them; but only those five, Cain, Luluwa, Abel, Aklia, and Seth alone.
cards.t_text: And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and between your seed and her seed; it shall bruise your head, and you shall bruise his heel.

cards.note: 1 John 3:10 — *In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever doeth not righteousness is not of Elohim (God), neither he that loveth not his brother.* Seth waxing in strength to fast and pray is the child of Elohim made manifest, the holy seed distinguished from the line of Cain.
cards.s_text: But Seth waxed in stature and in strength; and began to fast and pray, fervently.
cards.t_text: In this the children of Elohim (God) are manifest, and the children of the devil: whosoever does not righteousness is not of Elohim (God), neither he that loves not his brother.

cards.note: 1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The Conflict names Cain among the five but keeps Seth holy alone — the two seed-lines John divides, Cain of the wicked one against the righteous seed.
cards.s_text: As for Adam, he knew not again his wife Eve, all the days of his life; neither was any more offspring born of them; but only those five, Cain, Luluwa, Abel, Aklia, and Seth alone.
cards.t_text: Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.

cards.note: Jubilees 4:2 — *And in the first (year) of the third jubilee, Cain slew Abel because Elohim (God) accepted the sacrifice of Abel, and did not accept the offering of Cain.* The Elohim who accepts the offering over Seth is the same who weighed Abel's and Cain's, the holy line distinguished by the accepted sacrifice.
cards.s_text: Then they returned, and took an offering, and went to the mountain and offered it up, for the babe; and Elohim (God) accepted their offering, and sent His blessing upon them, and upon their son Seth; and they came back to the Cave of Treasures.

cards.note: Hebrews 11:4 — *By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.* The accepted offering for the babe Seth is the faith-offering Hebrews names, Elohim testifying over the righteous seed.
cards.s_text: Then they returned, and took an offering, and went to the mountain and offered it up, for the babe; and Elohim (God) accepted their offering, and sent His blessing upon them, and upon their son Seth; and they came back to the Cave of Treasures.

And Yahuah (LORD) had respect unto Abel and to his offering:* The offering Elohim accepts and blesses over Seth is the same respected sacrifice of the holy line, the altar kept before the Law.

cards.note: Luke 3:38 — *Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* The child Adam names in his affliction stands at the head of the genealogy that runs down to the Messiah, the kept seed of the woman.
cards.s_text: But when Adam came and saw the child's good looks, his beauty, and his perfect figure, he rejoiced over him, and was comforted for Abel. Then he named the child Seth, that means, "that Elohim (God) has heard my prayer, and has delivered me out of my affliction." But it means also "power and strength."
cards.t_text: Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Jubilees 4:7 — *And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said "Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him."* Jubilees carries the identical word over Seth's name — the raised-up second seed — confirming the Conflict's account.

cards.note: Genesis 5:3 — *And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth:* The beautiful son who is "like that of his father Adam" in 2:1 is the Seth begotten in Adam's own likeness who heads the book of the generations.

cards.note: Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* The Conflict's naming of Seth in comfort for Abel is the same scene Moses records, the appointed seed kept after the murder.
cards.s_text: But when Adam came and saw the child's good looks, his beauty, and his perfect figure, he rejoiced over him, and was comforted for Abel. cards.note: Psalm 34:7 — *The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.* Yahuah's delivering Adam many a time from the deceiver's hands in 2 Adam & Eve 3:16 is the same encamping mercy that guards all who fear Him.
cards.s_text: "Now, therefore, 0 Adam, understanding thy heart, I have delivered thee many a time from his hands; in order to show thee that I am a merciful Elohim (God); and that I wish thy good, and that I do not wish thy ruin."
cards.t_text: The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivers them.

cards.note: 1 Enoch 19:1 — *And Uriel said to me: ‘Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.* The many forms Satan takes to destroy Adam's soul in 2 Adam & Eve 3:15 are the same shape-shifting by which the fallen spirits defile mankind and are worshipped as gods.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) sent His Word unto Adam, saying, "0 Adam, that figure is the one that promised thee the Godhead, and majesty; he is not favourably disposed towards thee; but shows himself to thee at one time in the form of a woman; another moment, in the likeness if an angel; on another occasions, in the similitude of a serpent; and at another time, in the semblance of a god; but he does all that only to destroy thy soul.

cards.note: Genesis 3:1 — *Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath Elohim (God) said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?* The serpent-form among the deceiver's many guises in 2 Adam & Eve 3:15 is the very beast that beguiled Eve in the garden.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) sent His Word unto Adam, saying, "0 Adam, that figure is the one that promised thee the Godhead, and majesty; he is not favourably disposed towards thee; but shows himself to thee at one time in the form of a woman; another moment, in the likeness if an angel; on another occasions, in the similitude of a serpent; and at another time, in the semblance of a god; but he does all that only to destroy thy soul.

cards.note: Genesis 3:5 — *For Elohim (God) doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.* The Word names the woman-figure as the one that promised Adam the Godhead in 2 Adam & Eve 3:15 — the serpent's identical first lie, that man should be as gods.

cards.t_text: For Elohim (God) does know that in the day you eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and you shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.

cards.note: John 1:1 — *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* The Word that Elohim sends to Adam in 2 Adam & Eve 3:15 is the eternal Logos, with Elohim and Elohim from the beginning.
cards.s_text: Then Elohim (God) sent His Word unto Adam, saying, "0 Adam, that figure is the one that promised thee the Godhead, and majesty; he is not favourably disposed towards thee; but shows himself to thee at one time in the form of a woman; another moment, in the likeness if an angel; on another occasions, in the similitude of a serpent; and at another time, in the semblance of a god; but he does all that only to destroy thy soul.

cards.note: 1 Peter 5:8 — *Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour:* The flattering counsel to spend the days of youth in mirth and pleasure in 2 Adam & Eve 3:12 is the adversary stalking to devour his prey.

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 11:3 — *But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Messiah (Christ).* The false wedding-promise pressed on Adam in 2 Adam & Eve 3:11 is the same subtilty that beguiled Eve, now turned on her husband.
cards.s_text: "And now, lo! Elohim's (God's) promise to me is fulfilled; for it is He who has sent me to thee for the wedding; because if thou wed me, I shall bear thee finer and better children than those of Eve.
cards.t_text: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Messiah (Christ).

cards.note: 2 Corinthians 11:14 — *And no marvel; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.* Satan's appearing to Adam in the form of a beautiful woman in 2 Adam & Eve 3:4 is the very transforming Paul names — the deceiver in a borrowed, comely shape.

cards.s_text: "Spend thy youth in mirth and pleasure." (12) The different forms which Satan takes (15). When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* The murder of righteous Abel that Satan feigns to mourn in 2 Adam & Eve 3:8 was his own work, for he was a murderer from the beginning.

cards.note: Romans 16:20 — *And the Elohim (God) of peace shall bruise Satan under your feet shortly. The grace of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ) be with you. Amen.* The envying adversary of 2 Adam & Eve 3:1 meets the verdict already sworn against him: the bruising of his head.

cards.t_text: And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Isaiah 41:10 — *Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy Elohim (God): I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.* Yahuah's strengthening of Adam after the assault is the same covenant assurance He gives His people not to fear.

cards.note: John 14:18 — *I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.* The Word who *strengthened* Adam and *comforted* his heart is the same Logos who promises His own He will not leave comfortless.

cards.note: *THEN Elohim (God) ordered Satan to show himself to Adam plainly, in his own hideous form.* (2 Adam and Eve 4:1). *Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* (John 8:44). Elohim (God) orders Satan to appear to Adam plainly, in his own hideous form, so that Adam sees him as he is. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same enemy in the same way: a murderer from the beginning, with no truth in him, a liar and the father of lying. Adam is shown the face of the liar, and Yahusha (Jesus) names what the liar does. Both put the lie and the killing at the root.
cards.s_text: THEN Elohim (God) ordered Satan to show himself to Adam plainly, in his own hideous form.

cards.note: Revelation 12:9 — *And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world: he was cast out into the earth, and his angels were cast out with him.* The hideous form Adam is made to see is the unmasking of the old serpent whose whole trade is deceiving the world.

Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The line Seth is wooed to join (2 Adam & Eve 5:6) is the wicked one's seed-line, set apart from the righteous from the start.
