cards.t_text: Thus says Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); No stranger, uncircumcised in heart, nor uncircumcised in flesh, shall enter into my sanctuary, of any stranger that is among the children of Yashar'el (Israel).

cards.note: Numbers 18:4 — *And they shall be joined unto thee, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you.* When they read the law to Ptolemy (3 Macc 1:12), this is the word that barred him — the stranger comes not nigh.
cards.s_text: Then they read the law to him; but he persisted in obtruding himself, exclaiming, that he ought to be allowed: and saying, Be it that they were deprived of this honour, I ought not to be.
cards.t_text: And they shall be joined unto you, and keep the charge of the tabernacle of the congregation, for all the service of the tabernacle: and a stranger shall not come nigh unto you.

cards.note: Numbers 18:3 — *And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor ye also, die.* If even the ministering Levites die for nearing the holy vessels, a Greek king has no claim at all.
cards.s_text: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
cards.t_text: And they shall keep your charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle: only they shall not come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, that neither they, nor you also, die.

cards.note: *And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.* (3 Maccabees 1:11). *Therefore thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and ye shall serve: I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.* (Numbers 18:7). Ptolemy saw the temple, admired it, and decided he would walk into the sanctuary itself. The priests told him the rule: no one of the nation, not even the priests, only the high priest, and he only once a year. The king called that an honour he was being denied; the Torah calls it a death sentence for anyone else who comes near. Yahuah (God) gave the priesthood to Aaron and his sons as a gift, within the vail as well as at the altar, and said the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death. The high priest's one entry a year on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:2) was not a privilege to be extended; it was the boundary Yahuah (God) set on his own dwelling, and Ptolemy was pressing against the boundary and its penalty.
cards.s_text: And when they told him that this was not permissible, none of the nation, no, nor even the priests in general, but only the supreme high priest of all, and he only once in a year, being allowed to go in, he would by no means give way.
cards.t_text: Therefore you and your sons with you shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail; and you shall serve: I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that comes nigh shall be put to death.

cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The King of heaven who abases the proud — the same hand that shook Ptolemy to and fro like a reed.
cards.s_text: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:29 — *For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.* Cast down powerless and deprived of speech — the identical righteous judgment that paralyzed Ptolemy and silenced his boast.
cards.s_text: Shaking him to and fro as a reed is shaken with the wind, he cast him upon the pavement, powerless, with limbs paralyzed; by a righteous judgment deprived of the faculty of speech.
cards.t_text: For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:26 — *Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.* The same scourging of a proud intruder at the holy place — Heliodorus then, Ptolemy now.
cards.s_text: At that time Elohim (God), who seeth all things, who is beyond all Holy among the holy, heard that prayer, so suitable; and scourged the man greatly uplifted with scorn and insolence.
cards.t_text: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

cards.note: Isaiah 37:16 — *O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: thou hast made heaven and earth.* The unapproachable dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens — the same Father whose throne is above the cherubim, against whom no king may presume.
cards.s_text: Thy dwelling-place, the heaven of heavens, is indeed unapproachable to men.
cards.t_text: O Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts), Elohim (God) of Yashar'el (Israel), that dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth: you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:19 — *Now therefore, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God), I beseech thee, save thou us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that thou art Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), even thou only.* The deliverance Simon seeks is for the Father's Name — that none may boast he trampled his house like an idol's.
cards.s_text: We have trampled upon the holy house, as idolatrous houses are trampled upon.
cards.t_text: Now therefore, O Yahuah (LORD) our Elohim (God), I beseech you, save you us out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God), even you only.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:15 — *And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwellest between the cherubims, thou art the Elohim (God), even thou alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; thou hast made heaven and earth.* Simon prays as Hezekiah prayed — appealing to the sole Creator against the lawless boaster who would trample the holy house.
cards.s_text: Punish us not by means of the uncleanness of their men, nor chastise us by means of their profanity; lest the lawless ones should boast in their rage, and exult in exuberant pride of speech, and say,
cards.t_text: And Hezekiah prayed before Yahuah (LORD), and said, O Yahuah Elohim (LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), which dwell between the cherubims, you are the Elohim (God), even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth; you have made heaven and earth.

cards.note: Daniel 4:34 — *And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation.* The Most High who blots out iniquity and restores — the One whose mercy Simon implores.
cards.s_text: Blot out our iniquities, and do away with our errors, and shew forth thy compassion in this hour.
cards.t_text: And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up my eyes unto heaven, and my understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that lives for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:3 — *And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) one fourth part of the day; and another fourth part they confessed, and worshipped Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God).* Simon's plea is the same covenant posture — sin confessed at the holy place, the Father faithful to hear.
cards.s_text: And thou didst promise, out of love to the house of Yashar'el (Israel), that should we fall away from thee, and become afflicted, and then come to this house and pray, thou wouldest hear our prayer.
cards.t_text: And they stood up in their place, and read in the book of the law of Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God) one fourth part of the day; and another fourth part they confessed, and worshipped Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God).

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:11 — *And thou didst divide the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; and their persecutors thou threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters.* Simon's rolling of the depths over the pursuer with his chariots, and the safe passage for those who trust — the same deliverance, the same Deliverer.
cards.s_text: And thou rolledst the depths of the sea over him, when he made pursuit with chariots, and with a multitude of followers, and gavest a safe passage to those who put their trust in thee, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation.
cards.t_text: And you did divide the sea before them, so that they went through the midst of the sea on the dry land; and their persecutors you threwest into the deeps, as a stone into the mighty waters.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:10 — *And shewedst signs and wonders upon Pharaoh, and on all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for thou knewest that they dealt proudly against them. So didst thou get thee a name, as it is this day.* The same bold Pharaoh, the enslaver who dealt proudly, brought low by the Father's hand.
cards.s_text: Thou didst make known thy power when thou causedst the bold Pharaoh, the enslaver of thy people, to pass through the ordeal of many and diverse inflictions.
cards.t_text: And shewedst signs and wonders upon Pharaoh, and on all his servants, and on all the people of his land: for you knew that they dealt proudly against them. So did you get you a name, as it is this day.

cards.note: Daniel 4:37 — *Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.* The righteous Governor who judges all who act with pride and insolence — the very lesson the humbled king learned.
cards.s_text: It is thou, the Creator of all, Yahuah (Lord) of the universe, who art a righteous Governor, and judgest all who act with pride and insolence.
cards.t_text: Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of heaven, all whose works are truth, and his ways judgment: and those that walk in pride he is able to abase.

cards.note: Nehemiah 9:6 — *Thou, even thou, art Yahuah (LORD) alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and thou preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth thee.* The same confession Simon makes — the one Creator-Father, King of the heavens, before whom the oppressor's strength is nothing.
cards.s_text: O Yahuah (Lord), Yahuah (Lord), King of the heavens, and Ruler of the whole creation, Holy among the holy, sole Governor, Almighty, give ear to us who are oppressed by a wicked and profane one, who exulteth in his confidence and strength.
cards.t_text: You, even you, are Yahuah (LORD) alone; you have made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host, the earth, and all things that are therein, the seas, and all that is therein, and you preservest them all; and the host of heaven worshippeth you.

cards.note: Exodus 1:10 — *Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falleth out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.* Pharaoh's slander that the people are a disloyal danger in war is exactly Ptolemy's charge that they are *hostile to the king's interests* (3 Macc 3:7) and might *turn traitors* (3 Macc 3:24).
cards.s_text: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
cards.t_text: Come on, let us deal wisely with them; lest they multiply, and it come to pass, that, when there falls out any war, they join also unto our enemies, and fight against us, and so get them up out of the land.

cards.note: Exodus 1:9 — *And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:* Ptolemy's dread of the Yahudim is the first Pharaoh's dread — the king of Egypt who again turns on the seed dwelling in his land.
cards.s_text: On discovering this, so incensed was the wicked king, that he no longer confined his rage to the Yahudim (Jews) in Alexandria. Laying his hand more heavily upon those who lived in the country, he gave orders that they should be quickly collected into one place, and most cruelly deprived of their lives.
cards.t_text: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:

cards.note: Daniel 3:28 — *Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).* The deliverance promised over the slandered seed of 3 Macc 3 is the deliverance already shown in the furnace — the Father sends his angel to those who will not bow.
cards.s_text: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
cards.t_text: Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).

cards.note: Daniel 3:12 — *There are certain Yahudim (Jews) whom thou hast set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded thee: they serve not thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.* As the three were charged for serving Elohim alone, so the Egyptian Yahudim are charged because *they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law* (3 Macc 3:4).
cards.s_text: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
cards.t_text: There are certain Yahudim (Jews) whom you have set over the affairs of the province of Babylon, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego; these men, O king, have not regarded you: they serve not your gods, nor worship the golden image which you have set up.

cards.note: Daniel 3:8 — *Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Yahudim (Jews).* The *invidious rumour... uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi race* (3 Macc 3:2) is the same malicious accusation the Chaldeans brought in Babylon.
cards.s_text: While this was going on, an invidious rumour was uttered abroad by men who had banded together to injure the Yahudi (Jewish) race. The purport of their charge was, that the Yahudim (Jews) kept them away from the ordinances of the law.
cards.t_text: Wherefore at that time certain Chaldeans came near, and accused the Yahudim (Jews).

cards.note: The Rest of Esther 13:6 — *Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:* The Greek text of Artaxerxes' decree matches 3 Macc 3:25 phrase for phrase — total destruction of the people *with wives and children*.
cards.s_text: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
cards.t_text: Therefore have we commanded, that all they that are signified in writing to you by Aman, who is ordained over the affairs, and is next to us, shall all, with their wives and children, be utterly destroyed by the sword of their enemies, without all mercy and pity, the fourteenth day of the twelfth month Adar of this present year:

cards.note: Esther 3:13 — *And the letters were sent by posts into all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.* Ptolemy's letter to *destroy* with *wives and children* is the very decree of Esther 3:13 — the same extermination-edict, the same enemy.
cards.s_text: As soon, therefore, as the contents of this letter become known to you, in that same hour we order those Yahudim (Jews) who dwell among you, with wives and children, to be sent to us, vilified and abused, in chains of iron, to undergo a death, cruel and ignominious, suitable to men disaffected.
cards.t_text: And the letters were sent by posts into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Yahudim (Jews), both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even upon the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to take the spoil of them for a prey.

cards.note: Psalm 2:4 — *He that sitteth in the heavens shall laugh: Yahuah (Lord) shall have them in derision.* The king who thinks the people *lift up their heads against kings* (3 Macc 3:19) is himself the one held in derision by the enthroned Father.
cards.s_text: And thus, exhibiting their enmity against us, they alone among the nations lift up their heads against kings and benefactors, as men unwilling to submit to any thing reasonable.
cards.t_text: He that sits in the heavens shall laugh: Adonai (Lord) shall have them in derision.

cards.note: Psalm 2:2 — *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,* The king who writes against Yahuah's people writes, in truth, against Yahuah and his Anointed.
cards.s_text: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,

cards.note: Psalm 2:1 — *Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?* Ptolemy's letter-writing rage against the Yahudim is the empty raging of the heathen against the covenant.
cards.s_text: Now the king, elated with his prosperous fortune, and not regarding the superior power of Elohim (God), but thinking to persevere in his present purpose, wrote the following letter to the prejudice of the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Why do the heathen rage, and the people imagine a vain thing?

cards.note: The Rest of Esther 13:4 — *Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.* The Greek decree of Artaxerxes frames the same accusation as 3 Macc 3:7 — a people whose laws set them apart is named an enemy of the realm.
cards.s_text: who said much of the exclusiveness of the Yahudim (Jews) with regard to their worship and meats; they alleged that they were men unsociable, hostile to the king's interests, refusing to associate with him or his troops. By this way of speaking, they brought much odium upon them.
cards.t_text: Declared to us, that in all nations throughout the world there was scattered a certain malicious people, that had laws contrary to all nations, and continually despised the commandments of kings, so as the uniting of our kingdoms, honourably intended by us cannot go forward.

cards.note: Esther 3:8 — *And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of thy kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king's laws: therefore it is not for the king's profit to suffer them.* Haman's slander is word-for-word the charge laid against the Yahudim of Egypt — Torah-fidelity read as disloyalty.
cards.s_text: yet, as they worshipped Elohim (God), and observed his law, they made certain distinctions, and avoided certain things. Hence some persons held them in odium;
cards.t_text: And Haman said unto king Ahasuerus, There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the people in all the provinces of your kingdom; and their laws are diverse from all people; neither keep they the king’s laws: therefore it is not for the king’s profit to suffer them.

cards.note: Psalm 44:23 — *Awake, why sleepest thou, O Yahuah (Lord)? arise, cast us not off for ever.* The apparent silence before heaven's interference in 3 Macc 4:21 matches the psalmist's plea against the Deliverer's seeming sleep.
cards.s_text: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
cards.t_text: Awake, why sleepest you, O Adonai (Lord)? arise, cast us not off for ever.

cards.note: Psalm 44:26 — *Arise for our help, and redeem us for thy mercies' sake.* The unconquerable Providence that assists from heaven in 3 Macc 4:21 answers the cry to be redeemed for mercy's sake, not for merit.
cards.s_text: Now this was the active interference of the unconquerable Providence which assisted the Yahudim (Jews) from heaven.
cards.t_text: Arise for our help, and redeem us for your mercies’ sake.

cards.note: Psalm 44:22 — *Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.* The registration of the whole nation for destruction in 3 Macc 4:17 is the covenant people counted as slaughter-sheep — yet, as here, not abandoned.
cards.s_text: At the end of the above-mentioned interval of time, the registrars brought word to the king that the multitude of the Yahudim (Jews) was too great for registration,
cards.t_text: Yea, for your sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter.

cards.note: Exodus 1:9 — *And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:* the king who herds the multitude to the hippodrome in 3 Macc 4:11 shares the first Pharaoh's dread of the multiplying people.
cards.s_text: They were conveyed accordingly in this vessel, and at the end of it arrived at Schedia. The king had ordered them to be cast into the vast hippodrome, which was built in front of the city. This place was well adapted by its situation to expose them to the gaze of all comers into the city, and of those who went from the city into the country. Thus they could hold no communication with his forces; nay, were deemed unworthy of any civilized accommodation.
cards.t_text: And he said unto his people, Behold, the people of the children of Yashar'el (Israel) are more and mightier than we:

cards.note: Exodus 1:13 — *And the Egyptians made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to serve with rigour:* the merciless treatment of 3 Macc 4:9 echoes Egypt's first rigour against the covenant seed.
cards.s_text: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
cards.t_text: And the Egyptians made the children of Yashar'el (Israel) to serve with rigour:

cards.note: Exodus 1:14 — *And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.* The chains and fetters of 3 Macc 4:9 are the bitter Egyptian bondage returning upon the same people.
cards.s_text: They were dragged along by unyielding chains, like wild beasts: of these, some had their necks thrust into the benches of the rowers; while the feet of others were enclosed in hard fetters.
cards.t_text: And they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field: all their service, wherein they made them serve, was with rigour.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:6 — *And he hath violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden: he hath destroyed his places of the assembly: Yahuah (LORD) hath caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and hath despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.* Feasting and jollity turned to wailing in 3 Macc 4:8 as the solemn joy of Zion was likewise forgotten.
cards.s_text: The husbands of these, in the prime of their youthful vigour, instead of crowns wore halters round their necks; instead of feasting and youthful jollity, spent the rest of their nuptial days in wailings, and saw only the grave at hand.
cards.t_text: And he has violently taken away his tabernacle, as if it were of a garden: he has destroyed his places of the assembly: Yahuah (LORD) has caused the solemn feasts and sabbaths to be forgotten in Zion, and has despised in the indignation of his anger the king and the priest.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:21 — *The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, and not pitied.* The young brides and bridegrooms hurried to misery in 3 Macc 4:6-8 match Zion's fallen virgins and young men.
cards.s_text: Girls who had entered the bridal chamber quite lately, to enjoy the partnership of marriage, exchanged pleasure for misery; and with dust scattered upon their myrrh-anointed heads, were hurried along unveiled, and, in the midst of outlandish insults, set up with one accord a lamentable cry in lieu of the marriage hymn.
cards.t_text: The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; you have slain them in the day of your anger; you have killed, and not pitied.

cards.note: Lamentations 2:10 — *The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.* The streets filled with wailing in 3 Macc 4:3 echo the dust-strewn mourning of Zion's daughter.
cards.s_text: What home, or city, or place at all inhabited, or what streets were there, which their condition did not fill with wailing and lamentation?
cards.t_text: The elders of the daughter of Zion sit upon the ground, and keep silence: they have cast up dust upon their heads; they have girded themselves with sackcloth: the virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

cards.note: Esther 4:1 — *When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;* the loud bitter cry of grief that fills 3 Macc 4:2-3 has its pattern in Mordecai's own.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
cards.t_text: When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;

cards.note: Esther 4:3 — *And in every province, whithersoever the king's commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Yahudim (Jews), and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.* The identical mourning of the covenant people under a royal decree of destruction, ch4:2 in Egypt mirroring Persia.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews) suffered great throes of sorrow, and wept much; while their hearts, all things around being lamentable, were set on fire as they bewailed the sudden destruction which was decreed against them.
cards.t_text: And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Yahudim (Jews), and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:20 — *Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), That which thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.* The hands stretched out in mournful strains are heard by the same God who answered Hezekiah's prayer against the blasphemer.
cards.s_text: The Yahudim (Jews), breathless with momentary suspense, stretched forth their hands, and prayed the Greatest Elohim (God), in mournful strains, again to help them speedily.
cards.t_text: Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, Thus says Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel), That which you have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria I have heard.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:34 — *For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David's sake.* The Father overthrows the evil purpose for his own sake and for David's line, the same covenant ground on which Egypt's remnant casts its plea.
cards.s_text: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
cards.t_text: For I will defend this city, to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.

cards.note: Esther 6:1 — *On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.* The spirit of oblivion that empties this king's memory of his own decree mirrors the sleepless night that began Haman's undoing — providence governing a king's restless or clouded mind.
cards.s_text: The king, receiving him, was astonished at his unwonted exit; and, overwhelmed with a spirit of oblivion about everything, enquired the object of this earnest preparation.
cards.t_text: On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.

cards.note: Esther 6:1 — *On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.* As one king is kept from sleep to save the Yahudim, this king is sent into sleep to the same providential end — the small turning that overthrows the gallows and the hippodrome alike.
cards.s_text: He, however, who has sent his good creature sleep from all time, by night or by day thus gratifying whom he wills, diffused a portion thereof [now] upon the king.
cards.t_text: On that night could not the king sleep, and he commanded to bring the book of records of the chronicles; and they were read before the king.

cards.note: Proverbs 21:31 — *The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD).* Hermon may ready the elephants for the day of slaughter, but the safety of the covenant people rests with Yahuah, not the strength of the beasts.
cards.s_text: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
cards.t_text: The horse is prepared against the day of battle: but safety is of Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 21:30 — *There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD).* The king's repeated counsel to destroy keeps collapsing because no plotting can stand against the Father's purpose to deliver.
cards.s_text: The king, just like another Phalaris, a prey to thoughtlessness, made no account of the changes which his own mind had undergone, issuing in the deliverance of the Yahudim (Jews). He swore a fruitless oath, and determined forthwith to send them to Hades, crushed by the knees and feet of the elephants.
cards.t_text: There is no wisdom nor understanding nor counsel against Yahuah (LORD).

cards.note: Proverbs 21:1 — *The king's heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turneth it whithersoever he will.* The king's unflinching resolve is held fast and turned aside by the hand that channels every royal will.
cards.s_text: By this sweet and profound influence of Yahuah (Lord) he was held fast, and thus his unjust purpose was quite frustrated, and his unflinching resolve greatly falsified.
cards.t_text: The king’s heart is in the hand of Yahuah (LORD), as the rivers of water: he turns it whithersoever he will.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* Hermon's five hundred enraged beasts are no match for the One who alone can rout an army in a night.
cards.s_text: Then he called Hermon, who had charge of the elephants. Full of rage, altogether fixed in his furious design,
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: Exodus 14:28 — *And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.* The friends and army gathered to hate and destroy stand in the place of Pharaoh's vanished host.
cards.s_text: The king, after issuing these orders, went to his feasting, and gathered together all those of his friends and of the army who hated the Yahudim (Jews) the most.
cards.t_text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:27 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.* The host massed for execution will, like Pharaoh's, be turned back upon itself in the morning.
cards.s_text: he commanded him, with a quantity of unmixed wine and handfuls of incense [infused] to drug the elephants early on the following day. These five hundred elephants were, when infuriated by the copious draughts of frankincense, to be led up to the execution of death upon the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

cards.note: Exodus 14:30 — *Thus Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Yashar'el (Israel) saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.* The cry for Yahuah to reveal himself at the gates of Hades looks for the same hand that once saved Israel out of Egypt's own grip.
cards.s_text: sent up an exceeding great cry, entreating Yahuah (Lord) of all power to reveal himself, and have mercy upon those who now lay at the gates of Hades.
cards.t_text: Thus Yahuah (LORD) saved Yashar'el (Israel) that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Yashar'el (Israel) saw the Egyptians dead upon the sea shore.

cards.note: Exodus 14:14 — *Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.* As they invoke the Almighty Yahuah and beseech the Lord of every power, the battle is the Father's, not the captives'.
cards.s_text: They invoked the Almighty Yahuah (Lord), and ceaselessly besought with tears their merciful Elohim (God) and Father, Ruler of all, Yahuah (Lord) of every power,
cards.t_text: Yahuah (LORD) shall fight for you, and you shall hold your peace.

cards.note: Exodus 14:13 — *And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.* Hemmed in by chains and beasts, the bound remnant of Egypt is set in the same posture Moses commanded at the sea — wait and watch for a salvation no hand of theirs can earn.
cards.s_text: The heathen believed the Yahudim (Jews) to be destitute of all protection; for chains fettered them about.
cards.t_text: And Moses said unto the people, Fear you not, stand still, and see the salvation of Yahuah (LORD), which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom you have seen to day, you shall see them again no more for ever.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:26 — *Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.* The two angels of 3 Macc 6:18 echo the two manifest deliverers at the temple — it ain't new.
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Moreover two other young men appeared before him, notable in strength, excellent in beauty, and comely in apparel, who stood by him on either side; and scourged him continually, and gave him many sore stripes.

cards.note: 2 Maccabees 3:24 — *Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah (God) of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.* The same Prince of all power who routed Heliodorus' guard opens heaven over Ptolemy's host (3 Macc 6:18).
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: Now as he was there present himself with his guard about the treasury, Yahuah (God) of spirits, and the Prince of all power, caused a great apparition, so that all that presumed to come in with him were astonished at the power of Yahuah (God), and fainted, and were sore afraid.

cards.note: Psalms 34:7 — *The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.* The two dreadful angels of 3 Macc 6:18 are the standing promise of the angel-armies about the faithful.
cards.s_text: Then the all-glorious, all-powerful, and true Elohim (God), displayed his holy countenance, and opened the gates of heaven, from which two angels, dreadful of form, came down, and were visible to all but the Yahudim (Jews).
cards.t_text: The angel of Yahuah (LORD) encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivers them.

cards.note: Jonah 2:10 — *And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.* 'Recover him to the sight of his own' (3 Macc 6:8) — the deep gives Jonah back at the Deliverer's word.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: And Yahuah (LORD) spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.

cards.note: Jonah 2:6 — *I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet hast thou brought up my life from corruption, O Yahuah (LORD) my Elohim (God).* The Father who 'looked upon him' (3 Macc 6:8) brought his life up from corruption.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: I went down to the bottoms of the mountains; the earth with her bars was about me for ever: yet have you brought up my life from corruption, O Yahuah (LORD) my Elohim (God).

cards.note: Jonah 2:1 — *Then Jonah prayed unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) out of the fish's belly,* The 'pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster' of 3 Macc 6:8 is Jonah's cry from the deep.
cards.s_text: When Jonah was pining away in the belly of the sea-bred monster, thou didst look upon him, O Father, and recover him to the sight of his own.
cards.t_text: Then Jonah prayed unto Yahuah Elohav (the LORD his God) out of the fish’s belly,

cards.note: Daniel 6:22 — *My Elohim (God) hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.* Daniel 'hurled through slander and envy as a prey to lions' (3 Macc 6:7) was brought back unhurt by the sent angel.
cards.s_text: It was thou who, when Daniel was hurled, through slander and envy, as a prey to lions down below, didst bring him back again unhurt to light.
cards.t_text: My Elohim (God) has sent his angel, and has shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before you, O king, have I done no hurt.

cards.note: Daniel 3:28 — *Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who hath sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king's word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).* The three 'rather than serve vain things' (3 Macc 6:6) were delivered by the angel the Father sent.
cards.s_text: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
cards.t_text: Then Nebuchadnezzar spake, and said, Blessed be the Elohim (God) of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, who has sent his angel, and delivered his servants that trusted in him, and have changed the king’s word, and yielded their bodies, that they might not serve nor worship any god, except their own Elohim (God).

cards.note: Daniel 3:25 — *He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of Elohim (God).* The 'dewy coolness' of 3 Macc 6:6 is the presence of the Formed-Son in the furnace with the three.
cards.s_text: When the three friends in the land of Babylon of their own will exposed their lives to the fire rather than serve vain things, thou didst send a dewy coolness through the fiery furnace, and bring the fire upon all their adversaries.
cards.t_text: He answered and said, Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt; and the form of the fourth is like the Son of Elohim (God).

cards.note: Isaiah 37:36 — *Then the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* Isaiah seals the same deliverance Eleazar pleads in 3 Macc 6:5 — the boaster against the holy city undone.
cards.s_text: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
cards.t_text: Then the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: 2 Kings 19:35 — *And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.* The demolishing of Sennacherim (3 Macc 6:5) was wrought by one angel of the Father's hosts.
cards.s_text: When Sennacherim, the grievous king of the Assyrians, glorying in his countless hosts, had subdued the whole land with his spear, and was lifting himself against thy holy city, with boastings grievous to be endured, thou, O Yahuah (Lord), didst demolish him and didst shew forth thy might to many nations.
cards.t_text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of Yahuah (LORD) went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

cards.note: Exodus 14:28 — *And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.* 'His proud army' overwhelmed (3 Macc 6:4) leaves not so much as one — the same Egypt twice undone.
cards.s_text: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
cards.t_text: And the waters returned, and covered the chariots, and the horsemen, and all the host of Pharaoh that came into the sea after them; there remained not so much as one of them.

cards.note: Exodus 14:27 — *And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.* The overthrow Eleazar rehearses in 3 Macc 6:4 is the very deed of the Sea.
cards.s_text: Thou destroyedst Pharaoh, with his host of chariots, when that lord of this same Egypt was uplifted with lawless hardihood and loud-sounding tongue. Shedding the beams of thy mercy upon the race of Yashar'el (Israel), thou didst overwhelm him with his proud army.
cards.t_text: And Moses stretched forth his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to his strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it; and Yahuah (LORD) overthrew the Egyptians in the midst of the sea.

cards.note: Psalms 111:9 — *He sent redemption unto his people: he hath commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.* The wonders wrought for their salvation in 3 Macc 7:22 are the sent redemption of the covenant Redeemer whose name is holy.
cards.s_text: Every man received back his own, according to inventory; those who had obtained their goods, giving them up with the greatest terror. For the greatest Elohim (God) wrought with perfectness wonders for their salvation.
cards.t_text: He sent redemption unto his people: he has commanded his covenant for ever: holy and reverend is his name.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:22 — *I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, thy transgressions, and, as a cloud, thy sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed thee.* The Redeemer of Yashar'el is the one who redeems by blotting out sin and calling His people home, the salvation celebrated in 3 Macc 7:22-23.
cards.s_text: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.
cards.t_text: I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your transgressions, and, as a cloud, your sins: return unto me; for I have redeemed you.

cards.note: Isaiah 44:6 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).* The Redeemer of Yashar'el blessed unto everlasting in 3 Macc 7:23 is the King and Redeemer who is the first and the last.
cards.s_text: Blessed be the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel) unto everlasting. Amen.
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD) the King of Yashar'el (Israel), and his redeemer Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts); I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no Elohim (God).

cards.note: Exodus 12:14 — *And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and ye shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; ye shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.* The first memorial of deliverance out of Egypt stands behind the seven-day feast of deliverance kept at Ptolemais in 3 Macc 7:17.
cards.s_text: Having arrived at Ptolemais, called from the specialty of that district Rose-bearing, where the fleet, in accordance with the general wish, waited for them seven days,
cards.t_text: And this day shall be unto you for a memorial; and you shall keep it a feast to Yahuah (LORD) throughout your generations; you shall keep it a feast by an ordinance for ever.

cards.note: Esther 9:28 — *And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Yahudim (Jews), nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.* The deliverance registered as sacred on a pillar in 3 Macc 7:20 is the same kind of perpetual memorial the Jews ordained for Purim — a freely instituted remembrance, not a commanded feast of the law.
cards.s_text: These they registered as sacred upon a pillar, when they had dedicated the place of their festivity to be one of prayer. They departed unharmed, free, abundant in joy, preserved by the king's command, by land, by sea, and by river, each to his own home.
cards.t_text: And that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Yahudim (Jews), nor the memorial of them perish from their seed.

cards.note: Esther 9:22 — *As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.* The days of joyfulness kept in 3 Macc 7:19 mirror the Purim days of feasting and joy the people themselves appointed.
cards.s_text: They were accordingly brought back in peace, while they gave utterance to becoming thanks; and they determined to keep these days during their sojourn as days of joyfulness.
cards.t_text: As the days wherein the Yahudim (Jews) rested from their enemies, and the month which was turned unto them from sorrow to joy, and from mourning into a good day: that they should make them days of feasting and joy, and of sending portions one to another, and gifts to the poor.

cards.note: Psalms 111:4 — *He hath made his wonderful works to be remembered: Yahuah (LORD) is gracious and full of compassion.* The deliverance is set to song and remembrance precisely because His wonders are made to be remembered, as in 3 Macc 7:16.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: He has made his wonderful works to be remembered: Yahuah (LORD) is gracious and full of compassion.

cards.note: Isaiah 49:7 — *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD), the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel), and his Holy One, to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of Yahuah (LORD) that is faithful, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), and he shall choose thee.* The Redeemer of Yashar'el — the same title sung in 3 Macc 7:16 and sealed in 7:23.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: Thus says Yahuah (LORD), the Redeemer of Yashar'el (Israel), and his Holy One, to him whom man despises, to him whom the nation abhors, to a servant of rulers, Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship, because of Yahuah (LORD) that is faithful, and the Holy One of Yashar'el (Israel), and he shall choose you.

cards.note: Isaiah 49:26 — *And I will feed them that oppress thee with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I Yahuah (LORD) am thy Saviour and thy Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.* The eternal Saviour of Yashar'el whom they hymn in 3 Macc 7:16 is the one who repays the oppressor and redeems His own.
cards.s_text: They themselves having held fast their Elohim (God) unto death, and having enjoyed a full deliverance, departed from the city garlanded with sweet-flowered wreaths of every kind. Uttering exclamations of joy, with songs of praise, and melodious hymns they thanked the Elohim (God) of their fathers, the eternal Saviour of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.t_text: And I will feed them that oppress you with their own flesh; and they shall be drunken with their own blood, as with sweet wine: and all flesh shall know that I Yahuah (LORD) am your Saviour and your Redeemer, the mighty One of Jacob.

cards.note: Esther 9:16 — *But the other Yahudim (Jews) that were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,* The same pattern of striking down the enemies and then having rest that closes the deliverance in 3 Macc 7:15-16.
cards.s_text: slaying thus, in that day, above three hundred men, and esteeming this destruction of the wicked a season of joy.
cards.t_text: But the other Yahudim (Jews) that were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, and stood for their lives, and had rest from their enemies, and slew of their foes seventy and five thousand, but they laid not their hands on the prey,

cards.note: Esther 9:2 — *The Yahudim (Jews) gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.* The same authorized self-defence of the covenant people that 3 Macc 7:10-12 grants against the apostates.
cards.s_text: When they had received this letter, they were not forward to depart immediately. They petitioned the king to be allowed to inflict fitting punishment upon those of their race who had willingly transgressed the holy Elohim (God), and the law of Elohim (God).
cards.t_text: The Yahudim (Jews) gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, to lay hand on such as sought their hurt: and no man could withstand them; for the fear of them fell upon all people.

cards.note: Esther 9:25 — *But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Yahudim (Jews), should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.* The evil designed against the covenant people falls back on its author, as Ptolemy warns it would in 3 Macc 7:9.
cards.s_text: For know ye, that should we conceive any evil design against, or in any manner aggrieve them, we shall ever have as our opposite, not man, but the highest Elohim (God), the ruler of all might. From Him there will be no escape, as the avenger of such deeds. Fare ye well.
cards.t_text: But when Esther came before the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked device, which he devised against the Yahudim (Jews), should return upon his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

cards.note: Esther 9:1 — *Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)* The day appointed for destruction is turned to the contrary, exactly as the king's letter reverses his own decree in 3 Macc 7.
cards.s_text: King Ptolemy Philopator to the commanders throughout Egypt, and to all who are set over affairs, joy and strength.
cards.t_text: Now in the twelfth month, that is, the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the same, when the king’s commandment and his decree drew near to be put in execution, in the day that the enemies of the Yahudim (Jews) hoped to have power over them, (though it was turned to the contrary, that the Yahudim (Jews) had rule over them that hated them;)

cards.note: *'And' then shall ye see Enoch, Noah, and Shem, and Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, rising on the right hand in gladness. Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven... Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness... And then shall He judge all the Gentiles...* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:6–9). John sees *the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God)... and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works* (Revelation 20:12). Benjamin's *all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame* is that standing of small and great: the rising first, then the judging.
cards.s_text: And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.
cards.t_text: Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].

cards.note: *'And' then shall ye see Enoch, Noah, and Shem, and Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, rising on the right hand in gladness. Then shall we also rise, each one over our tribe, worshipping the King of heaven... Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness... And then shall He judge all the Gentiles...* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 140:6–9). Benjamin sets the rising in order: the fathers first, then the sons each over his tribe, and last *all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame,* and then the judging. Revelation names that last hour: *the time of the dead, that they should be judged* (Revelation 11:18). The fathers and the tribes rise before; the rising of all men, to glory or to shame, comes at the time of the dead, when the one judgment is set.
cards.s_text: And the nations were angry, and your wrath is come, and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that you should give reward unto your servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear your name, small and great; and should destroy them which destroy the earth.
cards.t_text: Then also all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame. And Yahuah (Lord) shall judge Yashar'el (Israel) first, for their unrighteousness; [for when He appeared as Elohim (God) in the flesh to deliver them they believed Him not].

cards.note: *And after these things shall Abraham and Isaac and Jacob arise unto life, and I and my brethren shall be chiefs of the tribes 'of Israel': Levi first, I the second, Joseph third, Benjamin fourth, Simeon fifth, Issachar sixth, and so all in order... And ye shall be the people of Yahuah (Lord), and have one tongue; And there shall be there no spirit of deceit of 'Beliar', For he shall be cast into the fire for ever. And they who have died in grief shall arise 'in joy', 'And they who were poor for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall be made rich,' And they who are put to death for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall awake 'to life'.* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 60:1, 3–4). John sees *the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Yahusha (Jesus)... and they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years* (Revelation 20:4). Judah's testament holds the same rising: the fathers *arise unto life,* the sons stand as *chiefs of the tribes* *all in order,* and *they who are put to death for Yahuah's (Lord's) sake shall awake 'to life'.* The first resurrection raises the fathers and the faithful slain into an ordered kingdom of the tribes, and the deceiver has no place among them, as John sees him shut in the pit *that he should deceive the nations no more* (Revelation 20:3), until his end in the fire.
cards.s_text: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Yahusha (Jesus), and for the word of Elohim (God), and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Messiah (Christ) a thousand years.
cards.t_text: And after these things shall Abraham and Isaac and Jacob arise unto life, and I and my brethren shall be chiefs of the tribes 'of Israel': Levi first, I the second, Joseph third, Benjamin fourth, Simeon fifth, Issachar sixth, and so all in order.

cards.note: *And there I saw Enoch and all who were with him, stript of the garments of the flesh, and I saw them in their garments of the upper world, and they were like angels, standing there in great glory.* (Ascension of Isaiah 9:9). Those on high are seen *stript of the garments of the flesh* and clothed *in their garments of the upper world* — the garments of 4:17, where the saints *turn themselves upward in their garments, and their body will be left in the world.* So the catching-up Paul names — *caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet Yahusha (Lord) in the air: and so shall we ever be with Yahusha (Lord)* (1 Thessalonians 4:17) — is a going up out of the garments of the flesh into the garments of the upper world, after the reign.
cards.s_text: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
cards.t_text: And there I saw Enoch and all who were with him, stript of the garments of the flesh, and I saw them in their garments of the upper world, and they were like angels, standing there in great glory.

cards.note: *And afterwards they will turn themselves upward in their garments, and their body will be left in the world.* (Ascension of Isaiah 4:17). Isaiah's *afterwards* keeps the order Paul keeps: *Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet Yahusha (Lord) in the air* (1 Thessalonians 4:17). The going up comes after the reign and the little season, when the voice says *Come up hither* and *they ascended up to heaven in a cloud* (Revelation 11:12). They turn upward in their garments, and the body is left in the world — as it is written, *it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment* (Hebrews 9:27).
cards.s_text: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
cards.t_text: And afterwards they will turn themselves upward in their garments, and their body will be left in the world.

members.member_note: The Hebrew library's extended Adamic narrative opens at the Genesis-garden register — the same Adamic source the toledot of Matt 1:1 descends from.
The seed-promise carried in apocalyptic register — *as the number of the stars and their power, so will I make thy seed.* The seed-line Matt 1:1 traces is the same the Apocalypse of Abraham extends.

The patriarch Yahudah (Judah) himself, in his deathbed testament, narrates the Tamar episode — *Now Er was wicked, and he was in need concerning Tamar.* The Hebrew library's pseudepigraphal voice of Yahudah (Judah) walks the same case Genesis 38 compresses.

The Testament of Yoseph (Joseph) — Testaments XII chapters 72-87 — narrates the patriarchal-Yoseph's deathbed words to his sons. The Matthean Yoseph carries the same role: dreamer, Egypt-carrier, preserver of the covenant line.

Simeon Chapter 5: *Yahuah (Lord) shall raise up from Levi as it were a High-priest, and from Yahudah (Judah) as it were a King, Elohim (God) and man.* The doubled-tribal priestly-and-kingly Messiah explicitly named.

Levi Chapter 9: *In the second jubilee, he that is anointed shall be conceived in the sorrow of beloved ones.* The conception prophecy the Hebrew library walks before Matthew's Yoseph (Joseph) receives the dream.

Benjamin Chapter 9: *there shall arise in the latter days one beloved of Yahuah (Lord), of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) and Levi.* The Beloved of the doubled-tribal lineage named by the youngest tribe's testament.
The Ascension of Isaiah's witness to the conception narrative — Mary and Joseph both of David's line, the virgin-conception named in the seventh-heaven vision.

Ascension of Isaiah 10:8 — *Go forth and descend through all the heavens, and thou wilt descend to the firmament and that world.* The Father sends the Beloved down through the heavens, and Matthew 1:23 names where the descent ends: *Elohim (God) with us.*
The pre-incarnation announcement of the Beloved's descent in human form — *in the last days.* The Hebrew library's framing of the incarnation Matt 1:23 announces.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 18:6 — *behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter.* The heavens open over Levi at his priestly investiture; they open again over Yahusha (Jesus) at the Jordan (Matthew 3:16), the Messiah's own investiture.

Ascension of Isaiah 9:12 — *Crowns and thrones of glory they do not receive, till the Beloved will descend.* Heaven announces beforehand the Beloved's coming down in human form, and at the water the voice from heaven says, *This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased* (Matthew 3:17).

Ascension of Isaiah 11:32 — *And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory.* The Son whom the voice from heaven names at the water (Matthew 3:17) is seen here with his journey down and back up finished, seated beside the Great Glory.

Ascension of Isaiah 4:2 — *Beliar the great ruler, the king of this world, will descend, who hath ruled it since it came into being.* The Ascension of Isaiah names the one who has ruled this world from the beginning, and the devil offers Yahusha (Jesus) what he holds.

Ascension of Isaiah 4:9 — *those who shall have been associated together in order to receive the Beloved, he will turn aside after him.* The ruler who asked the Son for worship turns aside the greater number of those gathered to receive the Beloved.
Ascension of Isaiah 3:13 — *the going forth of the Beloved from the seventh heaven had been made known.* The Beloved whose descent enraged Beliar sends Satan away with the Torah's own word.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:2 — *the spirit of hatred darkened my mind, and stirred up my soul to slay him.* Gad confesses that hatred began as a darkened mind and ended in a plan to kill, which is the very path Yahusha (Jesus) traces back to anger.

Reuben, Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 3:1 — *an eighth spirit of sleep, with which is brought about the trance of nature and the image of death.* Reuben lists the spirits that work in a man through his nature and his senses, the first of them being fornication — *First, the spirit of fornication is seated in the nature and in the senses* (Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 3:3) — and Yahusha (Jesus) puts the sin in the same place when he says that whoever looks on a woman to lust after her *hath committed adultery with her already in his heart* (Matthew 5:28).

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *if a man sin against thee, speak peaceably to him, and in thy soul hold not guile.* Gad tells his sons to answer a brother's wrong with peace and forgiveness, which is the same heart Yahusha (Jesus) asks for toward an enemy.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 64:7 — *Jacob, my father, knew that Elohim (God) aided my singleness.* Issachar's single heart is an open hand toward the poor, and Yahusha (Jesus) says, *if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light* (Matthew 6:22).
2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The harvest of the age, evil and good seeds together, is the harvest Yahusha (Jesus) says is already plenteous.
2 Baruch 70:2 — *the harvest of its evil and good seeds has come.* The prayer Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in Matthew 9:38 asks for workers for this same harvest.

2 Baruch 78:3 — *all we the twelve tribes are bound by one bond, inasmuch as we are born from one father.* The scattered, shepherdless multitudes Yahusha (Jesus) sees in Matthew 9:36 are this one family born from one father.
2 Baruch 78:7 — *with much mercy will gather together again those who were dispersed.* The compassion Yahusha (Jesus) shows the scattered sheep in Matthew 9:36 is this promised mercy at work.

4 Maccabees 10:1 — *apply it to this body of mine; for my soul ye cannot reach, not if ye would.* The third brother tells Antiochus what Yahusha (Jesus) later tells his own, that the soul is beyond the persecutor's reach.

4 Maccabees 15:1 — *loved rather religion, which saveth unto eternal life according to Elohim (God).* The mother chooses eternal life over the saving alive of her sons, the same order of fear Matthew 10:28 gives.

4 Maccabees 17:12 — *virtue, proving them through endurance, set before them the prize of victory in incorruption in everlasting life.* Endurance is proved first and the prize of incorruption follows, as Matthew 10:22 says of the one who endures to the end.

4 Maccabees 17:17 — *they now do both stand beside the throne of Elohim (God) and live the blessed age.* The brothers' endurance is shown as ending beside the throne of Elohim (God), the end Matthew 10:22 promises.

4 Maccabees 10:4 — *Even if thou dost remove my organ of speech, Elohim (God) is a hearer also of the speechless.* The brother whose tongue is to be cut out trusts that Elohim (God) hears without words, as Matthew 10:20 promises the Father's Spirit speaks in his own.

Ascension of Isaiah 4:3 — *Of the Twelve one will be delivered into his hands.* The persecution of the plant and the loss of one of the Twelve were told in advance, and Matthew's list ends on the one who betrayed.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 100:3 — *Love ye one another from the heart.* Gad's call to love from the heart and forgive the repentant brother stands behind the warning that closes Yahusha's (Jesus's) teaching on forgiveness.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 29:5 — *Work righteousness, therefore, my children, upon the earth, That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven.* Levi's call to work righteousness on the earth and have it as a treasure in heaven is the word Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in Matthew 19:21.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 129:2 — *There were twelve harts feeding: and the nine were (first) dispersed over all the earth.* Joseph's vision of twelve harts dispersed over the earth is the scattering that Yahusha (Jesus) assumes when He speaks of judging the twelve tribes.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 139:5 — *I know how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven.* Benjamin foresees the one who will be lowly on earth and glorious in heaven, and Yahusha (Jesus) says the Son of Adam came to serve and give His life.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:1 — *shall a star arise to you from Jacob in peace, And a man shall arise.* The star out of Jacob from Yahudah's (Judah's) seed is the Son of David the blind men call on.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:4 — *This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High), And this Fountain giving life unto all.* The Branch from Yahudah's (Judah's) line is the Son of David the two blind men call out to in Matthew 20:30.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5 — *the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem.* Two blind men keep crying Son of David against the crowd in Matthew 20:31, naming the stem Yahudah (Judah) was told would rise.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:5 — *the sceptre of my kingdom shine forth; And from your root shall arise a stem.* The sceptre promised to Yahudah (Judah) comes as the meek King on a colt in Matthew 21:5.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 59:6 — *a rod of righteousness to the Gentiles, To judge and to save all that call upon Yahuah (Lord).* Yahudah's (Judah's) rod of righteousness for the Gentiles points to the King coming in Matthew 21:5, whose call goes to the scattered seed.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3 — *ye shall deal lawlessly together with Yashar'el (Israel), so He shall not bear with Jerusalem because of your wickedness.* Levi's lawless leaders who hold the door are the ones Yahusha (Jesus) faces in the first woe of Matthew 23:13.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 33:11 — *in the seventh week shall come priests, (who are) idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud, lawless.* Levi's seventh-week priests, lawless and proud, are the kind of leaders Yahusha (Jesus) charges in Matthew 23:15.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 105:1 — *wear two faces like unto them, of goodness and of wickedness.* Asher charges his sons not to wear two faces, the same split between outside and inside that Yahusha (Jesus) calls hypocrisy.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 108:2 — *they that are double-faced are guilty of a twofold sin.* Asher says the double-faced carry a twofold sin, and Yahusha (Jesus) paints the same figure as a whited tomb.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 90:1 — *I saw a vision on the Mount of Olives, on the east of Jerusalem.* Naphtali saw his vision on the same Mount of Olives where the disciples ask about the end in Matthew 24:3.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 93:3 — *To save the race of Yashar'el (Israel), And to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles.* The gospel preached to all nations in Matthew 24:14 is the news that the scattered are being gathered.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:3 — *coming Himself [as man, with men eating and drinking], and breaking the head of the dragon in the water.* Asher says the Most High will come to the earth Himself in the person of man, and Matthew shows that coming with the tribes watching.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 109:7 — *Yahuah (Lord) will gather you together in faith through His tender mercy.* Asher promises that Yahuah (the Lord) will gather the scattered sons for the sake of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and Matthew describes the elect being gathered from the four winds.

4 Maccabees 9:1 — *We are ready to die rather than transgress the commandments of our fathers.* The brothers' readiness to die rather than break the Law foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) submission to the Father's will in the garden.

4 Maccabees 17:15 — *righteousness won the victory, and gave the crown to her athletes.* The brothers' crown for faithfulness unto death foreshadows the Messiah's (Christ's) obedience, thy will be done, that leads to the third day.

4 Maccabees 17:19 — *they having as it were become a ransom for our nation’s sin.* The book's own words about a ransom foreshadow the Messiah's (Christ's) laying down of his life as he walks to the arrest.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:2 — *I am clear from your ungodliness and transgression, which ye shall commit in the end of the ages.* Levi's warning of ungodly leaders at the end of the ages stands behind the smitten shepherd and scattered flock of Matthew 26:31.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 26:3 — *the veil of the temple shall be rent, so as not to cover your shame.* The high priest rends his clothes in Matthew 26:65, and the veil that Levi said would be rent is torn soon after.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8 — *a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men.* Jacob's word that a sinless one will die for ungodly men in the blood of the covenant is the death Yahusha (Jesus) names at the table.

2 Baruch 6:7 — *I saw him descend into the Holy of Holies, and take from thence the veil, and the holy ark.* The angel who descends and takes the veil in 2 Baruch is the hand from above that tears the veil in Matthew.
Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:1 — *the angel opened to me the gates of heaven, and I saw the holy temple.* The gates opened to Levi are the veil torn from the top at the cross.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 21:2 — *I have given thee the blessings of the priesthood until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel).* The until in Levi's blessing is met when the veil is torn in Matthew 27:51 and the one who sojourns has come.
