Zech 14:21 — *in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* — the spirits of deceit trodden under foot and the Canaanite removed in the day of the Lord.

Gen 9:26 — *Blessed be Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Shem; and Canaan shall be his servant.* — "the Mighty One of Yashar'el (Israel) shall glorify Shem" and Canaan perish, Noah's blessing fulfilled.

Zech 14:9 — *And Yahuah (LORD) shall be king over all the earth: in that day shall there be one Yahuah (LORD), and his name one.* — "Yahuah Elohim shall appear on earth" when all the earth rests from war.

Mal 3:1 — *and Yahuah (Lord), whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant... behold, he shall come, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* — the Lord appearing on earth to save, the coming Simeon foresees.

Isa 11:10 — *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.* — the day Simeon shall "arise in joy," the rest of the appearing King.

Zech 14:11 — *And men shall dwell in it, and there shall be no more utter destruction; but Jerusalem shall be safely inhabited.* — "all the earth rest from trouble, and all the world under heaven from war."

Heb 7:25 — *Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto Elohim (God) by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.* — "He shall save all [the Gentiles and] the race of Yashar'el (Israel)," the salvation arising from the two tribes.

Heb 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* — the King out of Judah made a priest, the change Simeon's priest-king foretells.

Ps 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* — the High-priest from Levi who is also the King at the right hand, David's Lord.
Zech 6:13 — *and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* — priest and king joined in one, the salvation from Levi and Judah.
Num 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)* — the King from Judah whom Simeon bids his sons obey.

Exod 13:8 — *And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which Yahuah (LORD) did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.* — the charge to command one's children that Simeon repeats: "that ye also may command your children."

Exod 13:21 — *And Yahuah (LORD) went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light* — light for Israel as the Egyptians sat in the darkness the sorcerers foretold at the bones' departure.

Josh 24:32 — *And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem... and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.* — the bones at last laid in the land, the homecoming the oath promised.

Exod 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* — the very departure of Joseph's bones at the Exodus that the testament foresees.

Gen 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* — the oath behind the guarded bones of Joseph the testament names.

2 Enoch 3:1 — *bore him up on to the first heaven and placed him on the clouds ... and showed me a very great Sea, greater than the earthly sea.* Enoch's ascent to the first heaven and its great sea is the same first heaven and "great sea hanging" Levi enters.
Matthew 3:16 — *the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove.* The heavens that open over Levi the priest open again over the Anointed at the Jordan.
2 Corinthians 12:2 — *such an one caught up to the third heaven.* Paul's rapture through the heavens matches Levi's ascent past the first and second toward the throne above.

Ezekiel 1:1 — *as I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, that the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of Elohim (God).* Ezekiel the priest sees the very thing Levi the priest sees — the heavens opened to a vision of God.

Malachi 3:1 — *Yahuah (Lord), whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant.* The Lord appearing among men through Levi's priesthood is the Lord coming to His temple.

Numbers 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel).* That by Levi and Judah the Lord shall appear and redeem Israel is Balaam's Star-and-Sceptre — the priest-king hope.
Numbers 18:2 — *thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi... that they may be joined unto thee, and minister unto thee.* Levi's calling to minister before the Lord is the office Moses assigns the tribe.

Isaiah 6:4 — *the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.* That all are shaken when the Lord looks forth — heaven, earth, and the abysses — is the trembling of the temple at His voice.
Revelation 4:8 — *they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty.* John's living creatures keep the same ceaseless praise before the throne Levi is shown.

Isaiah 6:3 — *Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): the whole earth is full of his glory.* The thrones and dominions that 'always they offer praise to Elohim (God)' echo the seraphim's unceasing cry.

Isaiah 6:1 — *I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.* The Great Glory dwelling above all in Levi's vision is the throne high and lifted up Isaiah beheld.
Matthew 3:12 — *he will throughly purge his floor... but he will burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire.* The unbelieving who persist in iniquity are judged as the chaff in the coming One's hand.

Isaiah 6:11 — *Until the cities be wasted without inhabitant, and the houses without man, and the land be utterly desolate.* The all-creation-troubled day of visitation matches the prophet's desolating judgment.

Numbers 24:9 — *He couched, he lay down as a lion, and as a great lion: who shall stir him up? Blessed is he that blesseth thee, and cursed is he that curseth thee.* 'They that bless Him shall be blessed, and they that curse Him shall perish' is the blessing spoken over Israel.

Isaiah 9:2 — *The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.* Levi lighting 'The light of knowledge shalt thou light up in Jacob' and shining 'as the sun shalt thou be to all the seed of Yashar'el (Israel)' is the great light upon the people.
Malachi 3:1 — *Yahuah (Lord), whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple.* 'until I come and sojourn in the midst of Yashar'el (Israel)' is the Lord's promised coming to His temple.
Numbers 18:7 — *I have given your priest's office unto you as a service of gift.* The blessings of the priesthood the angel gives Levi are the very office the Lord gave the tribe as a gift.
Genesis 34:31 — *Should he deal with our sister as with an harlot?* The vengeance for Dinah is the brothers' own answer in Genesis.

Genesis 34:25 — *two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* The shield and sword against Shechem is the deed Moses records of Simeon and Levi.

Genesis 34:26 — *And they slew Hamor and Shechem his son with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem's house.* That the brothers smote the city with the edge of the sword is set down in Genesis.

Genesis 34:13 — *And the sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father deceitfully... because he had defiled Dinah their sister.* Levi's counsel about the circumcision of Hamor's sons is the deceitful answer Moses records.

Exodus 29:9 — *and the priest's office shall be theirs for a perpetual statute: and thou shalt consecrate Aaron and his sons.* The seventh filling Levi's hands with incense to serve as priest is the perpetual office Moses consecrates.

Exodus 29:4 — *And Aaron and his sons thou shalt bring unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and shalt wash them with water.* The second washing Levi with pure water is the washing of the priest at his consecration.
Exodus 29:7 — *Then shalt thou take the anointing oil, and pour it upon his head, and anoint him.* The first man anointing Levi with holy oil is Aaron's anointing in the Torah.

Exodus 28:4 — *a breastplate, and an ephod, and a robe, and a broidered coat, a mitre, and a girdle: and they shall make holy garments.* The robe, breastplate, ephod, and turban put upon Levi are the very holy garments Moses commanded for the priest.

Hebrews 7:12 — *For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.* That Levi's seed is divided 'for a sign of the glory of Yahuah (Lord) who is to come' answers to the changed priesthood Hebrews names.

Hebrews 7:14 — *it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* That a king of Judah establishes a new priesthood is the change of priesthood Hebrews declares.
Psalm 110:4 — *Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The new priesthood established by the king of Judah is the priest-king sworn after Melchizedek's order.

Numbers 18:6 — *I have taken your brethren the Levites... to do the service of the tabernacle.* That Jacob renders the tithe 'through me,' Levi, is the Levites set apart to the service the tithe sustains.
Genesis 28:22 — *of all that thou shalt give me I will surely give the tenth unto thee.* Jacob paying tithes at Bethel through Levi fulfils his own Bethel vow of the tenth.
Leviticus 2:13 — *with all thine offerings thou shalt offer salt.* 'Every sacrifice thou shalt salt with salt' is the covenant of salt commanded in the law.

Leviticus 11:47 — *To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.* Offering 'of every clean beast and bird' keeps the Torah's distinction of clean and unclean.

Deuteronomy 30:1 — *the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations.* The reproach and curse among the Gentiles is the curse Moses set before Israel.

Leviticus 26:33 — *And I will scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you.* That they shall be 'scattered as captives among the Gentiles' is the dispersion Moses foretold for transgression.

Matthew 27:51 — *the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom; and the earth did quake, and the rocks rent.* The veil of the temple Levi foresees rent is the veil torn at the death of the Anointed.

1 Enoch 90:29 — *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* The house the Lord shall choose, named from the book of Enoch, is the new house Enoch saw the Lord gather His own into.
Galatians 6:7 — *for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.* 'Sow good things in your souls... but if ye sow evil things, ye shall reap every trouble' is the law of sowing and reaping.

Matthew 6:20 — *But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt.* 'Work righteousness... That ye may have (it) as a treasure in heaven' is the treasure laid up above.

Deuteronomy 6:5 — *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* 'Fear Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God) with your whole heart' is the Shema's command of whole-hearted love.

Malachi 2:7 — *the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and they should seek the law at his mouth: for he is the messenger of Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* The office the priests forsake when 'puffed up because of your priesthood' is the lips that should keep knowledge.

Malachi 2:8 — *ye have caused many to stumble at the law; ye have corrupted the covenant of Levi, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts).* The priests robbing the offerings and teaching out of covetousness are the corrupters of the covenant of Levi.

Isaiah 42:6 — *and give thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the Gentiles.* That the law was given to lighten every man, lest the Gentiles live in blindness, is the light of the Gentiles Isaiah foresees.
John 1:9 — *That was the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.* 'The light of the law which was given for to lighten every man' is the true Light John names.

Matthew 5:17 — *Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.* That they 'make void the law' and hate the man who reneweth it sets their lawlessness against the One who came to fulfil it.

Matthew 27:25 — *Then answered all the people, and said, His blood be on us, and on our children.* 'Taking innocent blood through wickedness upon your heads' is the blood owned by the people in the Gospel.

Isaiah 53:3 — *He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief.* The renewer of the law whom they 'call a deceiver' and rush to slay is the despised and rejected one of the prophet.

Ezekiel 37:21 — *I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side.* The visiting mercy after the dispersion is the gathering of the two houses Ezekiel foresees.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* 'Until He shall again visit you, and in pity shall receive you' is the Lord turning the captivity and gathering the scattered.

Hebrews 7:11 — *what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), and not be called after the order of Aaron?* The old priesthood failing so the Lord raises a new priest is the very change Hebrews reasons from.

Hebrews 7:24 — *But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.* That 'there shall none succeed him for all generations for ever' is the unchangeable priesthood of the One who continueth ever.

Psalm 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The new priest Yahuah (the Lord) raises up, to whom all his words are revealed and who judges the earth for a multitude of days, is the priest Yahuah (the LORD) swore in after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek) — a priesthood not from Levi's line and not for a season.
Isaiah 9:2 — *The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.* 'Lighting up the light of knowledge as the sun the day' is the great light upon those who walked in darkness.

Malachi 4:2 — *unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings.* That 'he shall shine forth as the sun on the earth, and shall remove all darkness' is the Sun of righteousness arising.
Numbers 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel).* 'His star shall arise in heaven as of a king' is the Star out of Jacob the seer beheld.

Isaiah 11:2 — *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.* 'The spirit of understanding and sanctification shall rest upon him' is the Spirit resting upon the Branch.

Matthew 3:17 — *And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.* 'With the Father's voice as from Abraham to Isaac' is the Father's voice from heaven over the beloved Son.

Matthew 3:16 — *the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove.* 'The heavens shall be opened, and from the temple of glory shall come upon him sanctification' is the opened heaven at the Jordan.

Revelation 22:2 — *was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* The tree of life the saints eat from is the tree in the restored paradise of the Revelation.

Revelation 2:7 — *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* 'He shall give to the saints to eat from the tree of life' is the overcomer's promise in the paradise of God.

Genesis 3:24 — *he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.* 'he shall open the gates of paradise, And shall remove the threatening sword against Adam' undoes the flaming sword that barred Eden.

Revelation 20:2 — *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.* 'Beliar shall be bound by him' is the binding of the adversary the Revelation foresees.

Luke 10:19 — *Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy.* 'He shall give power to His children to tread upon the evil spirits' is the authority over the enemy the Lord grants His own.

Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you... therefore choose life.* 'Yahuah (Lord) is witness, and His angels are witnesses, and ye are witnesses' is Moses' calling of heaven and earth to record the choice of life.

Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.* 'choose, therefore, for yourselves either the light or the darkness, either the law of Yahuah (Lord) or the works of Beliar' is the life-and-death Moses set before Israel.

Genesis 49:8 — *Yahudah (Judah), thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies; thy father's children shall bow down before thee.* The royal blessing the testament remembers is exactly the praise and pre-eminence Jacob spoke.

Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* Jacob's blessing "Thou shalt be a king" is the same scepter Moses sets on Judah's tribe.

Genesis 29:35 — *And she conceived again, and bare a son: and she said, Now will I praise Yahuah (LORD): therefore she called his name Yahudah (Judah); and left bearing.* The testament's "I give thanks to Yahuah... He hath given me a fourth son" simply repeats the praise that named him.
Genesis 38:10 — *And the thing which he did displeased Yahuah (LORD): wherefore he slew him also.* The testament's "he also died through wickedness" names the same judgment Moses records.

Genesis 38:9 — *And Onan knew that the seed should not be his; and it came to pass, when he went in unto his brother's wife, that he spilled it on the ground, lest that he should give seed to his brother.* The testament repeats the very deed for which Onan died.

Genesis 38:7 — *And Er, Yahudah's (Judah's) firstborn, was wicked in the sight of Yahuah (LORD); and Yahuah (LORD) slew him.* The testament's "Er was wicked... an angel of Yahuah smote him" is Moses' own verdict.

Leviticus 18:24 — *Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you.* The Canaanite "wickedness" Judah names is the defilement the Law commands Israel to shun.

Deuteronomy 7:3 — *Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.* The whole tangle springs from the Canaanite alliance the Torah forbids.
Proverbs 23:33 — *Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.* Judah's wine-deceived sight of a strange woman is exactly the wine-snare Proverbs describes.

Proverbs 23:31 — *Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.* The cup that "deceived" Judah when he saw her pouring out wine is the very snare Proverbs forbids looking upon.

Leviticus 18:25 — *And the land is defiled: therefore I do visit the iniquity thereof upon it, and the land itself vomiteth out her inhabitants.* Judah's verdict that "the race of the Canaanites was wicked" echoes the Law's judgment on their iniquity.

Genesis 38:26 — *And Yahudah (Judah) acknowledged them, and said, She hath been more righteous than I; because that I gave her not to Shelah my son. And he knew her again no more.* Judah's "she privily sent my pledges, and put me to shame" is the same confession Moses sets down.

Genesis 38:18 — *And he said, What pledge shall I give thee? And she said, Thy signet, and thy bracelets, and thy staff that is in thine hand. And he gave it her, and came in unto her, and she conceived.* The staff and tokens Judah names as his pledge are exactly the pledge Moses records.

Genesis 38:14 — *And she put her widow's garments off from her, and covered her with a vail, and wrapped herself, and sat in an open place, which is by the way to Timnath; for she saw that Shelah was grown, and she was not given unto him to wife.* The veiled woman by the gate is Moses' own account of Tamar.
Proverbs 31:4 — *It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink.* Judah the king-to-be falls precisely where the proverb warns a king not to go.
Proverbs 23:32 — *At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.* The wine that left Judah unable to recognise Tamar is the very serpent's bite Proverbs warns of.

Deuteronomy 30:2 — *And shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul.* Judah's charge to "keep my sayings to perform all the ordinances of Yahuah" is the Torah's own demand for whole-hearted obedience.
Ephesians 5:18 — *And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.* The apostle's charge against the very excess that ruined Judah confirms it ain't new.

Proverbs 23:33 — *Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.* The wine that "turned aside my eyes" and blinded the heart is the very snare the proverb foresees.
Ephesians 5:18 — *And be not drunk with wine, wherein is excess; but be filled with the Spirit.* Judah's "be not drunk with wine" is the apostle's command word for word.
Proverbs 23:30 — *They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.* The wine that takes away the mind of man is the lingering cup the proverb names.

Proverbs 23:29 — *Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?* Judah's drunkard whose eyes are led into error is the very man Proverbs questions.

Proverbs 31:5 — *Lest they drink, and forget the law, and pervert the judgment of any of the afflicted.* Judah forgetting the commandment and losing his glory is the very ruin the proverb foresees for a drinking king.

Proverbs 31:4 — *It is not for kings, O Lemuel, it is not for kings to drink wine; nor for princes strong drink.* The king stripped of his kingship through fornication is the prince the proverb warns away from wine.

Proverbs 23:32 — *At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.* Judah's counsel to touch wine not at all, lest a man perish before his time, echoes the proverb's serpent at the bottom of the cup.
Proverbs 23:30 — *They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.* The drunkenness that arises when the fear of Elohim departs is the lingering at wine the proverb forbids.

1 Timothy 6:9 — *But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.* Judah led astray for the sake of money is the man caught in this snare.

1 Timothy 6:10 — *For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.* Judah's twin warning against the love of money names the very root the apostle names.

Psalms 89:4 — *Thy seed will I establish for ever, and build up thy throne to all generations. Selah.* The everlasting establishing of the seed and throne is the same covenant standing behind Judah's confidence.

2 Samuel 7:16 — *And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever.* Yahuah's oath establishing David's house, of Judah's tribe, fulfils Judah's word that the kingdom shall be established from him.

Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The kingdom "from me shall the kingdom be established" is the scepter Jacob fixed on Judah.

Leviticus 18:24 — *Defile not ye yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the nations are defiled which I cast out before you.* The fornication that blinds the soul is the defilement the Law warns withdraws Israel from holiness.

1 Timothy 6:10 — *For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.* The money-love that withdraws Judah's sons from the law is the apostle's root that makes men err from the faith.

Matthew 6:24 — *No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* The money that draws the heart from Elohim is the rival master the Messiah names.

Colossians 3:5 — *Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence, and covetousness, which is idolatry.* Judah's word that the love of money leads to idolatry is the apostle's own equation.
Jeremiah 17:9 — *The heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?* The spirit of deceit that writes upon the heart is the deceitful heart only Yahuah can know.

Jeremiah 17:10 — *I Yahuah (LORD) search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings.* The works written on the heart and known to Yahuah are the very heart the prophet says He searches.
Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil.* The two spirits between which the mind must turn are the two ways Moses set before Israel.

Hebrews 7:11 — *If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek), and not be called after the order of Aaron?* Yahuah choosing Levi "to draw near to Him" is the priestly nearness the apostle weighs against the greater priest to come.

Hebrews 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The apostle joins the very tribes Judah joins — the King of Judah's line who holds also a priesthood not of Aaron.

Psalms 110:4 — *Yahuah (LORD) hath sworn, and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melek Tsadiq (Melchizedek).* The priesthood set above the kingdom finds its head in the king-priest sworn for ever after Melchizedek's order.

Zechariah 6:13 — *Even he shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD); and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* The joined kingship of Judah and priesthood of Levi is exactly the counsel of peace between them both.

Matthew 7:15 — *Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves.* The false prophets who persecute the righteous are the wolves the Messiah warns against.
Jeremiah 23:21 — *I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.* The false prophets like tempests are the unsent runners the prophet exposes.

Psalms 89:36 — *His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before me.* Yahuah's oath that He would not destroy the kingdom from Judah's seed for ever is the same sworn endurance of David's throne.
Isaiah 45:21 — *...a just Elohim (God) and a Saviour; there is none beside me.* The "appearing of the Elohim of righteousness" is Isaiah's just God and Saviour beside whom there is none.

Isaiah 45:17 — *But Yashar'el (Israel) shall be saved in Yahuah (LORD) with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.* The coming "salvation of Yashar'el (Israel)" and rest in peace is Isaiah's everlasting salvation.

Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* The kingdom held "Until the salvation of Yashar'el (Israel) shall come" is the scepter held until Shiloh comes.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *That then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* The promise that Yahuah will bring them up from captivity is Moses' own promise of gathering.

Leviticus 26:40 — *If they shall confess their iniquity, and the iniquity of their fathers, with their trespass which they trespassed against me, and that also they have walked contrary unto me.* Judah's "when with perfect heart ye repent" is the confession the Law makes the door of return.

Leviticus 26:33 — *And I will scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you: and your land shall be desolate, and your cities waste.* The sword, the laying waste, and the enslavement among the Gentiles are the very curse Moses set in the Law.

Revelation 22:16 — *I Yahusha (Jesus) have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.* The risen Messiah names Himself the very morning star out of Jacob Judah foretells.

Malachi 4:2 — *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* The man "like the sun of righteousness" is Malachi's Sun arising with healing.

Numbers 24:17 — *...there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* Judah's "shall a star arise to you from Jacob" is Balaam's very oracle of the Star and Sceptre.

Joel 2:28 — *And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions.* Judah's "He shall pour out the spirit of grace upon you" is Joel's outpouring upon all flesh.

John 1:32 — *And John bare record, saying, I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it abode upon him.* The opened heavens and the Spirit poured upon Him are seen fulfilled when the Spirit descends and abides on Him.

Isaiah 11:2 — *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD).* The heavens opened to pour the spirit upon Him is the Spirit resting on the Branch.

Zechariah 6:12 — *...Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD).* Judah's Branch of Elohim is Zechariah's man named The BRANCH.

Jeremiah 23:5 — *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* The Branch Judah names is the righteous Branch raised unto David.

Isaiah 11:1 — *And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots.* "This Branch of Elohim (God) El Elyon (Most High)" is Isaiah's Branch grown from the roots of Jesse.

Isaiah 11:4 — *But with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth: and he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.* The rod that judges and saves all that call upon Yahuah is the Branch's righteous judgment.

Isaiah 11:10 — *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.* The rod of righteousness "to the Gentiles" is Isaiah's root of Jesse to whom the Gentiles seek.
Numbers 24:17 — *...a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)...* The sceptre of Judah's kingdom shining forth is the very Sceptre Balaam saw rise out of Israel.

Matthew 22:32 — *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* Judah's very three fathers arising are the Master's proof of the resurrection.

Isaiah 26:19 — *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.* The rising of the fathers unto life is Isaiah's dead men living and rising.

Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* The patriarchs arising unto life is Daniel's awakening of them that sleep in the dust.

Ezekiel 37:12 — *...Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Yashar'el (Israel).* Israel made one people of Yahuah with one tongue is the whole house brought up out of the graves into the land.

Revelation 20:3 — *And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled.* Beliar cast into the fire so there is no more spirit of deceit is the deceiver shut up that he deceive the nations no more.

Revelation 20:6 — *Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection: on such the second death hath no power, but they shall be priests of Elohim (God) and of Messiah (Christ), and shall reign with him a thousand years.* They put to death for Yahuah's sake awaking to life are blessed in the first resurrection.
1 Corinthians 15:22 — *For as in Adam all die, even so in Messiah (Christ) shall all be made alive.* The dead in grief made to awake to life is the all-made-alive in Messiah.

1 Thessalonians 4:14 — *For if we believe that Yahusha (Jesus) died and rose again, even so them also which sleep in Yahusha (Jesus) will Elohim (God) bring with him.* They who died in grief arising in joy is the apostle's hope that Elohim will bring the sleeping with Him.

Genesis 49:33 — *And when Jacob had made an end of commanding his sons, he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the ghost, and was gathered unto his people.* Judah finishing his charge and falling asleep follows his father Jacob's very pattern of death.

Genesis 49:31 — *There they buried Abraham and Sarah his wife; there they buried Isaac and Rebekah his wife; and there I buried Leah.* Judah carried up to Hebron to his fathers is laid where Moses records the patriarchs were buried.
Matthew 5:8 — *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* The uprightness and singleness of heart Issachar walked in is the purity of heart the Beatitude crowns.

Proverbs 22:9 — *He that hath a bountiful eye shall be blessed; for he giveth of his bread to the poor.* The single, unenvious eye that grudges no neighbour is Proverbs' bountiful eye, blessed for its open hand.

Matthew 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* Issachar's "singleness of eye" is the very single eye the Master makes the lamp of the whole man.

2 Corinthians 9:7 — *Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for Elohim (God) loveth a cheerful giver.* Bestowing on the poor "in the singleness of my heart" is the cheerful, ungrudging giving the apostle commends.
Proverbs 3:9 — *Honour Yahuah (LORD) with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase.* The husbandman who first honours Yahuah with his increase walks Wisdom's path.

Deuteronomy 26:2 — *That thou shalt take of the first of all the fruit of the earth, which thou shalt bring of thy land that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) giveth thee, and shalt put it in a basket, and shalt go unto the place which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall choose to place his name there.* Issachar's offering of all his first-fruits through the priest keeps the Torah's command exactly.

Psalms 32:2 — *Blessed is the man unto whom Yahuah (LORD) imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.* The man who waits only for the will of God, unenvying and undeceiving, is the man in whose spirit is no guile.
Matthew 6:21 — *For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.* The single man who covets no gold and longs for no dainties has laid up his treasure where the Master directs the heart.

Matthew 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* The man who beholds all things in uprightness and shuns the evil eye is the man of the single eye, full of light.

Matthew 22:40 — *On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.* Issachar's "Keep, therefore, my children, the law of Elohim (God)" reduced to love of God and neighbour is the very hinge the Master names.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* "Love your neighbour" and "have compassion on the poor and weak" is Torah's royal command set beside the love of God.

Deuteronomy 6:5 — *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* "Love Yahuah" is the first great word of the Shema, set first by Issachar as by Moses.

Proverbs 3:10 — *So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.* The promise that with first-fruits Yahuah will bless the husbandman echoes Wisdom's reward for honouring Him with the increase.

Exodus 23:19 — *The first of the firstfruits of thy land thou shalt bring into the house of Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God).* Issachar's "offering gifts to Yahuah with thanksgiving" from the first-fruits keeps the Torah's command.

Hebrews 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The Anointed who springs from Judah yet bears a priesthood gathers into himself the two tribes' joined hope — the Messiah of the Levi-Judah line.

Zechariah 6:13 — *and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* The priesthood given to Levi and the kingdom given to Judah are joined in the prophet's priest-king, the counsel of peace between the two offices.

Genesis 49:10 — *The sceptre shall not depart from Yahudah (Judah), nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.* "to Yahudah (Judah) the kingdom" is Jacob's own dying word over Judah's sceptre.

Ezekiel 37:21 — *Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.* The promised return to the land is the prophet's regathering of the scattered house.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *That then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* The merciful deliverance that brings them back into their land is Moses' promise of the gathering after return.

Deuteronomy 28:64 — *And Yahuah (LORD) shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.* "They shall be dispersed among the Gentiles, and shall serve their enemies" is the very curse Moses set before the disobedient.

Exodus 20:17 — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.* "I coveted not any desirable thing that was my neighbour's" keeps the tenth word of the Decalogue.
John 1:47 — *Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!* The guileless heart Issachar confesses is the very mark the Master praised in the true Israelite.

Psalms 32:2 — *Blessed is the man unto whom Yahuah (LORD) imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile.* "Guile arose not in my heart; a lie passed not through my lips" is the very blessedness the psalmist names — the spirit without guile.

1 John 4:21 — *And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth Elohim (God) love his brother also.* Issachar's twin love of Yahuah and of every man is the very command the apostle binds together.
Leviticus 19:18 — *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* Loving "every man with all my heart" and sharing bread with the poor is the royal law of love to the neighbour.

Deuteronomy 6:5 — *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* "I loved Yahuah... with all my heart" is the Shema's first command lived to the end of his days.

Genesis 37:24 — *And they took him, and cast him into a pit: and the pit was empty, there was no water in it.* Zebulun weeping in secret over Joseph stands beside the bare Genesis record of the pit into which the brothers cast him.

Genesis 37:21 — *And Reuben heard it, and he delivered him out of their hands; and said, Let us not kill him.* Zebulun's pleading that they not be guilty of slaying Joseph echoes Reuben's cry to spare him in the same hour.

Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* That Yahuah forbade water to rise in the pit so Joseph might be preserved is the same providence turning the brothers' evil to deliverance.
Proverbs 6:17 — *A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood.* The very sin Joseph begs them not to commit is named among the things that are an abomination to Yahuah.

Genesis 37:22 — *And Reuben said unto them, Shed no blood, but cast him into this pit that is in the wilderness, and lay no hand upon him; that he might rid him out of their hands.* Joseph's cry "lay not upon me your hands to shed innocent blood" answers exactly to Reuben's "shed no blood... lay no hand upon him."

Genesis 37:26 — *And Yahudah (Judah) said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother, and conceal his blood?* The brothers taking the price of Joseph is the trafficking in their brother's blood that Judah first proposed.

Deuteronomy 25:9 — *Then shall his brother's wife come unto him in the presence of the elders, and loose his shoe from off his foot, and spit in his face, and shall answer and say, So shall it be done unto that man that will not build up his brother's house.* This is the very "writing of the law of Moses" Zebulun names: the loosed sandal and the spitting that shame him who will not own his brother.

Genesis 37:30 — *And he returned unto his brethren, and said, The child is not; and I, whither shall I go?* Reuben rending his clothes and crying "How shall I look in the face of Jacob my father?" is the same anguish Genesis sets in his mouth.

Genesis 37:31 — *And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood.* Dan's counsel to slay a kid and dip the coat is the very deceit Genesis records against Jacob.

Genesis 37:23 — *And it came to pass, when Joseph was come unto his brethren, that they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him.* Zebulun's note that they stripped Joseph's coat in selling him matches Genesis word for deed.
Matthew 5:7 — *Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.* That the merciful man is dealt with mercifully by Yahuah is the very blessing of the Beatitude.

Matthew 7:12 — *Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.* "Even as a man doeth to his neighbour, even so also will Yahuah do to him" is the same golden rule the Master calls the law and the prophets.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* Zebulun's command to keep Yahuah's commands and show mercy to thy neighbour stands on this Torah word.

Micah 6:8 — *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* To have compassion in the heart toward all is the love of mercy the prophet sets at the heart of what Yahuah requires.

Proverbs 19:17 — *He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto Yahuah (LORD); and that which he hath given will he pay him again.* Zebulun's pity, for which Yahuah blessed and preserved him, is Wisdom's mercy that lends to Yahuah himself.

Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:4 — *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* Zebulun turning away neither stranger nor sick nor aged keeps the very counsel of the fathers' wisdom.

Deuteronomy 15:8 — *But thou shalt open thine hand wide unto him, and shalt surely lend him sufficient for his need, in that which he wanteth.* Sharing with every man as he had need is the wide-open hand Torah commands toward the poor brother.

Matthew 25:35 — *For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in.* Zebulun feeding the stranger and the sick from his catch is the very mercy the King counts as done to himself.

Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:12 — *Shut up alms in your storehouses: and it shall deliver you from all affliction.* Zebulun's manifold return for sharing is the alms-storehouse that the fathers say profits more than gold.
Proverbs 11:25 — *The liberal soul shall be made fat: and he that watereth shall be watered also himself.* That the one who shares receives manifold more is exactly Wisdom's liberal soul made fat.

Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 29:8 — *Yet have you patience with a man in poor estate, and delay not to shew him mercy.* Where Zebulun had nothing to give yet kept compassion in bowels of mercy, he keeps the fathers' word to show mercy even in want.
Leviticus 19:18 — *but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* Showing compassion and mercy without hesitation to all men is the love of neighbour Torah lays as the rule.

Matthew 25:36 — *Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.* Zebulun clothing the naked man in winter is the very deed the King receives as done to himself.
Luke 6:36 — *Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.* That in the degree a man has compassion Yahuah has compassion on him is the Father's mercy made the measure of the son's.

Matthew 5:7 — *Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.* "Have, therefore, yourselves also, my children, compassion... that Yahuah (Lord) also may have compassion and mercy upon you" is the Beatitude almost word for word.

Ephesians 4:32 — *And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as Elohim (God) for Messiah's (Christ's) sake hath forgiven you.* Zebulun's charge to be without malice and set down no evil against a brother is the apostle's kindness and mutual forgiveness.

Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Joseph bearing no malice in Egypt is the very forgiveness Genesis records over his brothers.

Ezekiel 37:17 — *And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.* That everything Yahuah made has but one head is mirrored in the two sticks of Judah and Joseph made one in Yahuah's hand.

Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel); and one king shall be king to them all: and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.* Zebulun's "Ye shall be divided in Yashar'el (Israel), And ye shall follow two kings" is the very division of the two kingdoms Ezekiel says shall at last be made one.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *That then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* Yahuah being merciful and compassionate to the repentant captives is Moses' promise to turn the captivity and gather them.

Deuteronomy 30:2 — *And shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart, and with all thy soul.* "Ye shall remember Yahuah and repent, and He shall have mercy" is the return with all the heart Moses foretold.

Ephesians 4:8 — *Wherefore he saith, When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.* Yahuah Himself arising and bringing them back from captivity to their own land is the captivity-led-captive the apostle proclaims in the Messiah.

Isaiah 60:1 — *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee.* That ye shall see Him in Jerusalem when the light arises is the glory of Yahuah risen upon Zion as her sons are gathered.

Isaiah 9:2 — *The people that walked in darkness have seen a great light: they that dwell in the land of the shadow of death, upon them hath the light shined.* The light of righteousness arising upon Israel is the great light Isaiah says shall shine on the people in darkness — the land of Zebulun named in the verses before.

Malachi 4:2 — *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* "Yahuah Himself, the light of righteousness" rising upon them is the Sun of righteousness Malachi says shall arise with healing.

Genesis 49:29 — *I am to be gathered unto my people: bury me with my fathers in the cave that is in the field of Ephron the Hittite.* Zebulun carried up and buried in Hebron with his fathers keeps the same burial among the patriarchs Jacob charged.

Isaiah 26:19 — *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead.* That he shall rise and rejoice in the midst of his tribe is the awaking and singing of the dust Isaiah promised.

Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* Zebulun's confidence that he shall rise again in the midst of his sons rests on the awaking from the dust Daniel foretold.
Jas 1:20 — *For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.* James, like Dan, sets anger over against the truth that pleases God.
Eph 4:26 — *Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath.* Paul names the very evil Dan warns of, the wrath that teaches a man wickedness.

Eph 4:25 — *Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour: for we are members one of another.* The same pairing of truth against lying that Dan calls good and well pleasing to God.
Eph 4:27 — *Neither give place to the devil.* The very surrender Dan repented of when Beliar's spirit handed him the sword.
Prov 14:30 — *A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.* The envy that made Dan crush at Joseph as a leopard at a kid.

John 8:44 — *Ye are of your father the devil... He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth... for he is a liar, and the father of it.* The murderer-and-liar behind the spirit of Beliar that armed Dan against Joseph.

Eph 4:31 — *Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice.* The catalogue of the very spirit Dan begs his sons to keep themselves from.
Prov 14:30 — *but envy the rottenness of the bones.* The hatred of heart and envy of a brother that anger ends in, by Dan's own reckoning.
Prov 14:29 — *He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding: but he that is hasty of spirit exalteth folly.* The blindness of anger that Dan says cannot see a man's face with truth.
Jas 1:19 — *let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.* The longsuffering Dan commands against the spirit of anger.
John 8:44 — *When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.* Beliar's character, who rules the soul that lying and wrath have left to him.
Eph 4:25 — *Wherefore putting away lying, speak every man truth with his neighbour.* The lying that, wedded to wrath, makes the twofold mischief Dan warns against.
Eph 4:27 — *Neither give place to the devil.* The very giving-over Dan describes when the disturbed soul yields and Beliar rules over it.

Eph 4:8 — *When he ascended up on high, he led captivity captive, and gave gifts unto men.* The captivity the Lord's salvation takes from Beliar, in Dan's words turning disobedient hearts back to the Lord.

Heb 7:14 — *For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.* The very fusion Dan foretells — the King out of Judah made also the priest, after the order of Melchizedek.
Num 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)*. Balaam's Sceptre, the king from Judah whom Dan joins with Levi as the salvation of the Lord.

Zech 6:13 — *and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* The joined priesthood and kingship — Levi and Judah — from which Dan says salvation arises.

Rev 20:6 — *but they shall be priests of Elohim (God) and of Messiah (Christ), and shall reign with him a thousand years.* The saints whose captivity is taken from Beliar, reigning in the peace Dan promises them.

Rev 20:2 — *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years.* The binding of Beliar that Dan calls the war the Lord's salvation makes against him.
Isa 65:18 — *for, behold, I create Jerusalem a rejoicing, and her people a joy.* The rejoicing of the righteous in the New Jerusalem that Dan foresees.
Gen 2:9 — *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden.* The Eden in which Dan's saints shall rest, the garden the New Jerusalem brings back.
Rev 22:2 — *was there the tree of life... and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* Eden's tree restored within the city — the rest Dan promises the saints.
Rev 21:2 — *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven*. The very New Jerusalem in which Dan says the righteous shall rejoice.
Ezek 37:27 — *My tabernacle also shall be with them: yea, I will be their Elohim (God), and they shall be my people.* The Lord in the midst of His restored city, exactly as Dan promises Jerusalem.

Ezek 37:22 — *and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.* The end of captivity and division Dan foresees when the Lord dwells in the midst of Jerusalem.
Deut 30:3 — *will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations.* The very return-and-mercy Dan promises when Israel turns back to the Lord.
Heb 7:25 — *seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.* The intercession of the priest-king, exactly the office Dan ascribes to the one who pleads Israel's peace.

1 Tim 2:5 — *For there is one Elohim (God), and one mediator between Elohim (God) and men, the man HaMashiach Yahusha (Christ Jesus);* The single mediator Dan tells his sons to draw near to — the appointed Anointed, not a co-equal, but the man who stands between God and Israel.

Deut 30:4 — *from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee:* The Lord's name in every place of Israel and among the Gentiles — the gathering of the scattered Dan foresees.

Ezek 37:23 — *but I will save them out of all their dwellingplaces, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them: so shall they be my people.* The transforming into a nation that does His will, which Dan promises the repentant.

Deut 30:2 — *And shalt return unto Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), and shalt obey his voice according to all that I command thee this day, thou and thy children, with all thine heart*. The day of Israel's repentance on which Dan says the enemy's kingdom ends.

Genesis 35:24 — *The sons of Rachel; Joseph, and Benjamin:* — Rachel's prayer for "a brother of thine from mine own womb," whence "Joseph was like unto me in all things," reaches for the sons Rachel herself bore.
Genesis 30:7 — *And Bilhah Rachel’s maid conceived again, and bare Jacob a second son.* — "I was born from Bilhah... and she conceived and bare me" is the birth of that second son of Bilhah.

Genesis 30:8 — *And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed: and she called his name Naphtali.* — Naphtali's word that Bilhah "conceived and bare me upon Rachel's knees, therefore she called my name Naphtali" is the very naming Moses set down.

Genesis 1:27 — *So Elohim (God) created man in his own image, in the image of Elohim (God) created he him; male and female created he them.* — "He created every man after His own image" is the word of the sixth day repeated.

Psalm 139:2 — *Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.* — "there is no inclination or thought which Yahuah knoweth not" is the LORD who understands the thought afar off.

Psalm 139:14 — *I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.* — that the body is made "by weight, and measure, and rule" after the likeness of the spirit is the wonder of being fearfully and wonderfully made.

Jeremiah 18:6 — *O house of Yashar'el (Israel), cannot I do with you as this potter? saith Yahuah (LORD). Behold, as the clay is in the potter’s hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Yashar'el (Israel).* — the potter who "knoweth the use of each vessel" is the LORD who holds Israel as clay in His hand.

Isaiah 64:8 — *But now, O Yahuah (LORD), thou art our father; we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand.* — "as the potter knoweth the vessel... so also doth Yahuah make the body" is the very figure of the LORD as potter and man as clay.

John 1:5 — *And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not.* — "neither while ye are in darkness can ye do the works of light" is the same parting of light and darkness, of the works of light from the works of Beliar.

Genesis 1:4 — *And Elohim (God) saw the light, that it was good: and Elohim (God) divided the light from the darkness.* — "as there is a division between light and darkness... so also is there a division between man and man" reaches for the first dividing on the first day.

Genesis 1:31 — *And Elohim (God) saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.* — "Elohim (God) made all things good in their order" echoes the verdict over the whole creation, that it was very good.

Romans 1:20 — *For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:* — "recognising in the firmament, in the earth, and in the sea... Yahuah who made all things" is Paul's witness of the Maker read off the created order.

Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.* — "change not the law of Elohim (God)" rests on the law that is perfect, the same psalm that begins with the ordered heavens.

Psalm 19:1 — *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* — that the unchanging luminaries rebuke the changing of God's law is the same testimony the heavens themselves declare.

Genesis 1:14 — *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* — "sun and moon and stars change not their order" is the appointed ordering of the lights on the fourth day.

Romans 1:23 — *And changed the glory of the uncorruptible Elohim (God) into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.* — "the Gentiles... obeyed stocks and stones" is Paul's word that they changed the glory of God into an image.

Jude 1:7 — *Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire.* — Naphtali joins Sodom and the Watchers exactly as Jude does, an example of the order of nature changed and judged.

Jude 1:6 — *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* — the Watchers "whom Yahuah cursed" are the angels Jude says kept not their first estate.

1 Enoch 10:8 — *And the whole earth has been corrupted through the works that were taught by Azâzêl: to him ascribe all sin.* — "on whose account He made the earth without inhabitant and fruitless" is the corruption of the whole earth that Enoch lays to the Watchers (self-link).

1 Enoch 7:1 — *And all the others together with them took unto themselves wives, and each chose for himself one, and they began to go in unto them and to defile themselves with them, and they taught them charms and enchantments...* — the Watchers "whom Yahuah cursed at the flood" are the very ones whose defiling and corrupting Enoch records (self-link).

Genesis 6:4 — *There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of Elohim (God) came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them, the same became mighty men which were of old, men of renown.* — "the Watchers also changed the order of their nature" reaches for the sons of God who came in unto the daughters of men before the flood.

Genesis 19:24 — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* — "that ye become not as Sodom, which changed the order of nature" recalls the city the LORD overthrew with fire.

Isaiah 11:11 — *And it shall come to pass in that day, that Yahuah (Lord) shall set his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people, which shall be left...* — "after ye have become minished and made few, ye shall return" is the remnant the LORD recovers the second time.

Ezekiel 37:21 — *Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* — "Yahuah shall scatter them upon the face of all the earth, until the compassion of Yahuah shall come" looks for the gathering of the scattered house Ezekiel foretells.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *That then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* — "ye shall return and acknowledge Yahuah Elohaychem (the Lord your God); and He shall bring you back into your own land, according to His abundant mercy" is the turning of the captivity and the gathering Moses promised.

Deuteronomy 30:1 — *And it shall come to pass, when all these things are come upon thee, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before thee, and thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath driven thee,* — "Yahuah shall bring captivity upon you... ye shall be bowed down with every affliction" is the curse Moses set before Israel among the nations.

*And after that in the sixth week all who live in it shall be blinded, And the hearts of all of them shall godlessly forsake wisdom. And in it a man shall ascend; And at its close the house of dominion shall be burnt with fire, And the whole race of the chosen root shall be dispersed.* (1 Enoch 93:8). 1 Enoch 91 —  — "I have read in the writing of Enoch that ye yourselves also shall depart from Yahuah" reaches for the very book of Enoch that foretells the generation of apostasy (self-link).

Zechariah 6:13 — *and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* — Levi as the sun and Judah as the moon, raised together, is the counsel of peace between priest and king.

Numbers 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* — that Levi seizes the sun and Judah the moon, both lifted up, is the priest-king hope summed in the Star of Jacob and the Sceptre of Israel.

Genesis 37:9 — *Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me.* — Naphtali's vision "that the sun and the moon were standing still" takes up the very luminaries of Joseph's dream among the brethren.

Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel)... and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:* — the captivity of all twelve tribes looks to the day Ezekiel foretells, when the divided house is made one nation again.

Deuteronomy 30:1 — *...thou shalt call them to mind among all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath driven thee,* — that the nations "shall possess in captivity the twelve tribes of Yashar'el" is the driving among the nations Moses set before them.

Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land upon the mountains of Yashar'el (Israel)... and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all:* — that amid the scattering "Levi and Yahudah were together" foreshadows the priest and king of the one reunited house.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *...will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* — that "the ship reached the land, as it were in peace" and the father came and all rejoiced is the gathering home after the scattering.

Deuteronomy 30:4 — *If any of thine be driven out unto the outmost parts of heaven, from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee:* — "we were all scattered unto the ends of the earth" is the driving to the outmost parts from which the LORD promised to gather Israel.

Zechariah 6:13 — *and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* — to "be united to Levi and to Yahudah" is the counsel of peace between priest and king made one in the anointed.

Numbers 24:17 — *there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel)...* — "through them shall salvation arise unto Yashar'el, and in them shall Jacob be blessed" is the Star and Sceptre that arise out of Jacob and Israel.

Matthew 1:23 — *Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.* — that God should appear and dwell among men to save Israel is Immanuel, God with us, born to save his people from their sins.

John 1:14 — *And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.* — "Elohim (God) shall appear, dwelling among men on earth" is fulfilled when the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us — the only begotten whom the Father sent, the Formed one walking among men.

Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* — "to save the race of Yashar'el" is the assembling of the outcasts of Israel and the dispersed of Judah, the two-house gathering.

Isaiah 11:10 — *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.* — that He gathers "the righteous from amongst the Gentiles" is the root of Jesse to whom the nations seek.

Zechariah 2:11 — *And many nations shall be joined to Yahuah (LORD) in that day, and shall be my people: and I will dwell in the midst of thee...* — "to gather together the righteous from amongst the Gentiles" is the many nations joined to the LORD when He dwells among His people.

Zechariah 2:10 — *Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion: for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith Yahuah (LORD).* — "shall Elohim (God) appear [dwelling among men] on earth" is the LORD's own promise to come and dwell in the midst of Zion.

Psalm 19:11 — *Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward.* — "that Yahuah may love you" through keeping His commandments in due order is the great reward of keeping them.

Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.* — "Be ye therefore wise in Elohim (God)... understanding the order of His commandments" rests on the law that is perfect and makes the simple wise.

Genesis 37:4 — *And when his brethren saw that their father loved him more than all his brethren, they hated him, and could not speak peaceably unto him.* The grudge Gad confesses is the brethren's hatred Moses names.

Genesis 37:2 — *These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives: and Joseph brought unto his father their evil report.* The very scene Gad describes — Joseph with the sons of Bilhah, carrying their report to their father.

1 John 2:11 — *But he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth, because that darkness hath blinded his eyes.* That Gad would neither hear nor see Joseph is the blinded eyes John describes.
1 John 2:9 — *He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.* Gad's spirit of hatred toward his brother is exactly the darkness John exposes.

1 John 3:15 — *Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.* Gad's wish to kill the brother he hated from the heart is the very murder John says hatred already is.
Genesis 37:8 — *And they hated him yet the more for his dreams, and for his words.* The dreams that inflamed Gad's hatred are the same dreams Moses says the brethren hated.

Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* That God delivered Joseph from their hands lest they work great lawlessness is the very providence Joseph names to his brethren.

Genesis 37:27 — *Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites, and let not our hand be upon him; for he is our brother and our flesh. And his brethren were content.* The selling Gad confesses is Judah's counsel Moses records.

Proverbs 10:12 — *Hatred stirreth up strifes: but love covereth all sins.* That the hater dispraiseth truth and envieth the prosperous is the strife-stirring hatred Solomon sets against covering love.

Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.* The spirit of hatred Gad warns against is the heart-hatred Moses forbids by name.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* The commandment concerning loving one's neighbour that hatred refuses to hear is this very word of Moses.

Leviticus 19:18 — *...but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* That love would quicken even the dead, working with the law of God, points to this love-of-neighbour at the heart of Torah.

1 John 3:14 — *We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.* Gad's spirit of love unto salvation and spirit of hatred unto death is John's passage from death to life by love.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people...* That by the same thing a man transgresseth he is punished follows on Gad's grudge against Joseph, the very grudge Moses forbids.

Proverbs 14:30 — *A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones.* Gad's liver, set in envy against Joseph and then mercilessly diseased, is Solomon's envy that rots the bones.

1 John 3:11 — *For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.* That his children should drive forth hatred and cleave to the love of God is the message John says was from the beginning.

Ephesians 4:31 — *Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice:* Hatred that kindleth wrath and stirreth war, which Gad bids his sons drive forth, is the very brood Paul commands put away.

1 John 3:11 — *For this is the message that ye heard from the beginning, that we should love one another.* Gad's charge to love one another in deed and word is the very message John says is from the beginning.

Leviticus 19:17 — *Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart...* That Gad spake peaceably to Joseph before his father while hatred secretly darkened his soul is the very heart-hatred Moses forbids.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* To love one another from the heart and put away hatred is the very love-of-neighbour Moses commands.

Luke 17:4 — *And if he trespass against thee seven times in a day, and seven times in a day turn again to thee, saying, I repent; thou shalt forgive him.* That the one who repents so as not to wrong thee again is to be received is the repeated forgiveness Yahusha enjoins.

Luke 17:3 — *Take heed to yourselves: If thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him; and if he repent, forgive him.* Gad's exact sequence — rebuke, then if he repents, forgive — is the Lord's word in Luke.

Matthew 18:22 — *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.* That if he repent thou shalt forgive him is the boundless forgiveness the Messiah commands.

Matthew 18:15 — *Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother.* Gad's rule to speak peaceably and rebuke the brother who sins is the Lord's own counsel.

Ecclesiasticus 28:7 — *Remember the commandments, and bear no malice to your neighbour.* No malice rooted in the commandments; the Testaments say *even so forgive him from the heart, and leave to Elohim (God) the avenging*.

Sirach 28:2 — *Forgive your neighbour the hurt that he has done to you, so shall your sins also be forgiven when you prayest.* Gad's counsel to forgive the brother who sins is Ben Sira's own word on forgiving thy neighbour.

Romans 12:19 — *Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith Yahuah (Lord).* To leave to God the avenging is exactly Paul's charge to leave vengeance to the Lord.

Matthew 18:35 — *So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.* Gad's 'forgive him from the heart' is the heart-forgiveness the Messiah requires.

Ephesians 4:32 — *And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as Elohim (God) for Messiah's (Christ’s) sake hath forgiven you.* To forgive even the shameless from the heart is Paul's tenderhearted forgiveness.

Psalms 37:7 — *Rest in Yahuah (LORD), and wait patiently for him: fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way...* To put away jealousy and rest in God is the patient waiting the psalm commands toward the prosperous.

Psalms 37:1 — *Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.* Gad's 'do not be vexed... be not envious' when another prospers is David's own counsel against envy.

Psalms 37:36 — *Yet he passed away, and, lo, he was not: yea, I sought him, but he could not be found.* To wait for the end of the Lord upon the unrepentant rich is the psalm's very picture of the wicked passing away.

Psalms 37:35 — *I have seen the wicked in great power, and spreading himself like a green bay tree.* The man grown rich by evil means whom Gad bids us not envy is the flourishing wicked the psalmist beholds.
