Zechariah 6:13 — *...and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both.* That salvation arises from Judah and Levi together is Zechariah's priest-king on one throne, the peace between kingship and priesthood.

Numbers 24:17 — *...there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Yashar'el (Israel), and shall smite the corners of Moab, and destroy all the children of Sheth.* The salvation Gad says the Lord shall raise up from Judah is Balaam's Star and Sceptre of Israel's royal line.

Matthew 7:14 — *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.* The narrow way unto life is the good inclination in which all the soul's actions are in righteousness.

Matthew 7:13 — *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* the two ways of good and evil drawn as the two gates.

Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* Moses's charge to choose between the two is the choice Asher lays on his children.
Deuteronomy 30:15 — *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* the very two ways Asher says God hath given to the sons of men.

Deuteronomy 30:6 — *And Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will circumcise thine heart, and the heart of thy seed, to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart;* the soul that casts away wickedness and cleaves to righteousness is the heart God circumcises to love and obey.

James 1:15 — *Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.* The evil spirit filling the treasure of the inclination forces every issue into evil, just as conceived lust ends in death.
James 1:14 — *But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.* The evil inclination that drives away the good is the lust that draws a man away.

Leviticus 11:47 — *To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.* This is what God "in the tables of the commandments hath thus declared" — the difference between clean and unclean Asher invokes as his standard.

Deuteronomy 14:7 — *Nevertheless these ye shall not eat of them that chew the cud, or of them that divide the cloven hoof; as the camel, and the hare, and the coney: for they chew the cud, but divide not the hoof; therefore they are unclean unto you.* The same hare, half-marked yet unclean, repeated in the second giving of the law Asher appeals to.

Leviticus 11:6 — *And the hare, because he cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof; he is unclean unto you.* Asher's "half clean, but in very deed are unclean" hare is the very creature Moses names: it answers one mark of cleanness and fails the other, like the double-faced man.

Matthew 6:16 — *Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast.* The man who commits fornication yet fasts and "doeth evil" is the hypocrite whose fast is a face put on, not a single heart.

Leviticus 11:44 — *For I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy;* the holiness of the Lord who commandeth the law that the defrauder "setteth at nought and provoketh."

James 4:8 — *Draw nigh to Elohim (God), and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* The cure for two-facedness is James's call to the double-minded to purify the heart and cleave to God alone.
James 1:8 — *A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.* The double-faced soul that serves its own lusts is James's double-minded man, unstable because he is not single toward God.

Matthew 6:24 — *No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve Elohim (God) and mammon.* To wear two faces is to attempt the two masters the Messiah forbids; one must cleave to goodness only.

Leviticus 11:47 — *To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.* The clean who "abstain from what Elohim (God) also hateth and forbiddeth by His commandments" keep this very difference Moses commanded.

Leviticus 11:3 — *Whatsoever parteth the hoof, and is clovenfooted, and cheweth the cud, among the beasts, that shall ye eat.* The stag and the hind that "seem to be unclean, but they are altogether clean" are the cloven-hoofed cud-chewing beasts Moses declares clean — the very mark the single-faced keep.

Matthew 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* The man of single face is the man of the single eye, full of light and just before God.

Matthew 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* To walk "with singleness of face unto that which is good" is to walk with the single eye, the whole body full of light.

James 1:25 — *But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.* Asher's singleness of face, searching out and keeping the commandments, is the doer who continues in the perfect law.
James 4:8 — *Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.* The double-faced "guilty of a twofold sin" are James's double-minded, called to purify the divided heart.

James 1:22 — *But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.* To "keep the law of Yahuah (Lord)" and look unto the thing really good is to be the doer Asher's single face requires.

James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him.* The soul that meets the angel of peace and is led into eternal life receives the crown of life promised to the faithful.

Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* the peaceful soul led "into eternal life" has chosen the life Moses set before Israel.

Genesis 19:24 — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* Asher's warning, "Become not, my children, as Sodom, which knew not the angels of Yahuah (Lord), and perished for ever," recalls the city that rejected the two angels and was destroyed.

Leviticus 26:33 — *And I will scatter you among the heathen, and will draw out a sword after you: and your land shall be desolate, and your cities waste.* The land made desolate and the people scattered for not giving heed to the law is the sanction of Leviticus 26.

Deuteronomy 28:64 — *And Yahuah (LORD) shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other;* the scattering "unto the four corners of the earth" Asher foresees is the very curse Moses pronounced for disobedience.

Isaiah 11:12 — *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* The gathering from the four corners is Isaiah's second-ingathering of both houses.

Ezekiel 37:21 — *Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* those scattered "as Gad and Dan" are the very houses Ezekiel sees gathered and made one again.

Deuteronomy 30:3 — *That then Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) will turn thy captivity, and have compassion upon thee, and will return and gather thee from all the nations, whither Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath scattered thee.* The Lord gathering His people "in faith through His tender mercy" is the compassion and gathering Moses promised the scattered.

Revelation 12:9 — *And the great dragon was cast out, that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan, which deceiveth the whole world;* the dragon whose head is broken is the old serpent at last cast down.

Isaiah 11:10 — *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek:* that the Most High "shall save Yashar'el (Israel) and all the Gentiles" is the root of Jesse to whom the nations are drawn.

Isaiah 27:1 — *In that day Yahuah (LORD) with his sore and great and strong sword shall punish leviathan the piercing serpent, even leviathan that crooked serpent; and he shall slay the dragon that is in the sea.* Asher's "breaking the head of the dragon in the water" is Isaiah's slaying of the dragon in the sea.

Genesis 39:2 — *And Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.* The refrain of the whole testament — "Yahuah (Lord) loved me... the Elohim (God) of my fathers guarded me" — is Moses' own refrain over Joseph.
Psalm 105:19 — *Until the time that his word came: the word of Yahuah (LORD) tried him.* The trying and deliverance Joseph recounts is exactly how the Psalmist frames his ordeal.
Psalm 105:18 — *Whose feet they hurt with fetters: he was laid in iron.* Joseph's "I was taken into captivity" and "in bonds" is the very binding the Psalm records.
Psalm 105:17 — *He sent a man before them, even Joseph, who was sold for a servant.* The Psalmist names the same selling Joseph here confesses, and reads it as God's own sending.

1 Corinthians 10:13 — *Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape.* That God departs "for a little space... to try the inclination of the soul" yet gives protection in all things is Paul's same doctrine of the faithful God in temptation.

James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him.* Joseph's "in ten temptations He showed me approved, and in all of them I endured" is the very blessing James pronounces.

Genesis 39:21 — *But Yahuah (LORD) was with Joseph, and shewed him mercy, and gave him favour in the sight of the keeper of the prison.* Joseph's "Yahuah granted me to find mercy in the sight of the keeper of the prison" quotes Moses almost word for word.

Genesis 39:9 — *how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?* The reason Joseph here gives — the God of Israel delivered him — is the same reason he gave the woman in Genesis.

Genesis 39:8 — *But he refused, and said unto his master's wife, Behold, my master wotteth not what is with me in the house, and he hath committed all that he hath to my hand.* Joseph's struggle "against a shameless woman, urging me to transgress" is the refusal Moses sets down.

2 Timothy 2:22 — *Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on Yahusha (Lord) out of a pure heart.* Joseph's weeping, praying, and fasting is exactly the fleeing of youthful lust by calling on the Lord that Paul charges Timothy.

Genesis 39:7 — *his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.* Her offer here — "Thou shalt be lord of me... if thou wilt give thyself unto me" — is the same solicitation Moses records.

Genesis 39:10 — *And it came to pass, as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.* The woman's repeated threatening "How often did the Egyptian woman threaten me with death!... and then call me back and threaten me" is Moses' "day by day."

Genesis 39:10 — *as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her.* Joseph giving himself "yet more to fasting and prayer" against her renewed pleas is the persistence of the refusal Moses records.

Proverbs 6:25 — *Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.* That Yahuah "willeth not that those that reverence Him should be in uncleanness" is Wisdom's same charge against the adulteress's snare.

Proverbs 6:24 — *To keep thee from the evil woman, from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman.* Joseph's resistance to her flattering, idol-trading pleas is the very deliverance the lamp of the commandment works.

James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah (Lord) hath promised to them that love him.* Joseph eating the enchanted food in faith, unharmed, is the man tried and approved whom James blesses.

1 Corinthians 10:13 — *Elohim (God) is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.* That "the wickedness of the ungodly hath no power over them that worship Elohim with chastity" is Paul's faithful God who makes the way of escape.

1 Corinthians 10:13 — *Elohim (God) is faithful... but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.* Joseph singing praises "in the abode of darkness" because he was delivered from her desire is the escape borne with thanksgiving.

Genesis 39:20 — *And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound.* The false accusation by the garment and the casting into Pharaoh's prison is the very outcome Moses records.

Genesis 39:12 — *And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.* Joseph's "she laid hold of my garments... I left it behind, and fled away naked" is Moses' scene, told from within.

James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.* Her offer to release him from his bonds for consent, and his not inclining "even in thought," is endurance under trial whose end is the crown.

Genesis 39:10 — *as she spake to Joseph day by day, that he hearkened not unto her, to lie by her, or to be with her.* Her baring of arms and breasts "that I might lie with her" while Yahuah guarded him is the persistent solicitation refused that Moses records.

2 Timothy 2:22 — *Flee also youthful lusts: but follow righteousness, faith, charity, peace, with them that call on Yahusha (Lord) out of a pure heart.* That God loves him "who in a den of darkness combines fasting with chastity" over the man of luxury and licence is Paul's same preference of righteousness over youthful lust.

1 Peter 2:23 — *Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously.* Joseph's patience under slavery, slander and envy — committing his cause to Yahuah who dwells in the chaste — is the Messiah's own pattern of suffering.

Genesis 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* That he would not raise himself against his brethren "with evil intent" is the same spirit that forgave them at the last.

Genesis 50:20 — *ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Saying "I was a home-born slave" rather than expose those who sold him is the same refusal to requite evil that Genesis crowns with forgiveness.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* That "every one who doeth the law of Yahuah shall be loved by Him" and Joseph's shielding of his brethren is the royal commandment itself.

1 Peter 2:23 — *Who, when he was reviled, reviled not again; when he suffered, he threatened not; but committed himself to him that judgeth righteously.* Joseph swallowing his grief and not betraying his brethren is the Messiah's silent endurance under suffering.

Genesis 45:1 — *Then Joseph could not refrain himself before all them that stood by him; and he cried, Cause every man to go out from me.* That Joseph here "desired greatly to weep, but I restrained myself" is the same overflowing heart Moses records breaking forth before his brethren.

Leviticus 19:18 — *Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* "love one another, and with long-suffering hide 'ye one another's faults'" is the royal commandment in plain words.

Genesis 50:21 — *Now therefore fear ye not: I will nourish you, and your little ones. And he comforted them, and spake kindly unto them.* Joseph loving his brethren "more abundantly" after Jacob's death, suffering them not to be afflicted, is exactly Moses' scene of comfort after the father's burial.

Genesis 45:5 — *Now therefore be not grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that ye sold me hither: for Elohim (God) did send me before you to preserve life.* That he "upbraided them not, and comforted them" is the very comfort Joseph spoke when he made himself known.

Proverbs 25:21 — *If thine enemy be hungry, give him bread to eat; and if he be thirsty, give him water to drink.* Wisdom long before commanded the very kindness to an enemy that Joseph here urges and lived.
Romans 12:21 — *Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.* To answer those who seek your harm with well-doing is Paul's same overcoming of evil with good.

Matthew 5:44 — *But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you.* "If any one seeketh to do evil unto you, do well unto him, and pray for him" is the Messiah's command in the same breath.

Ezekiel 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land... and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.* The three harts becoming lambs and gathering with the nine into twelve flocks is the two houses made one nation again.

Daniel 7:14 — *his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* "For his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, which shall not pass away" is Daniel's everlasting dominion of the Son of Adam, word for word.

Revelation 5:6 — *And I beheld, and, lo, in the midst of the throne... stood a Lamb as it had been slain.* The Lion and the Lamb seen as one in Joseph's vision are the Lion and the slain Lamb John beholds in the throne-room.

Revelation 5:5 — *behold, the Lion of the tribe of Juda, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book, and to loose the seven seals thereof.* That from Levi and Judah shall arise the one who saves is John's Lion of the tribe of Judah who prevailed.

Isaiah 53:7 — *he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.* The spotless lamb against whom all the beasts rush is Isaiah's silent suffering lamb.

John 1:29 — *Behold the Lamb of Elohim (God), which taketh away the sin of the world.* The spotless lamb born of the virgin, and named in v11 as the one who saves Israel and the Gentiles, is John's Lamb of God.

Genesis 49:9 — *Yahudah (Judah) is a lion's whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?* The lion at the lamb's hand, born of Judah, is Jacob's own blessing of the lion of Judah.

Matthew 1:23 — *Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, Elohim (God) with us.* Matthew names the very virgin and son this vision saw, fulfilling Isaiah's sign.

Isaiah 7:14 — *Therefore Yahuah (Lord) himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.* The virgin from whom the lamb is born is the sign Isaiah gave the house of David.

Genesis 50:20 — *ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* Joseph's dying confidence that "Elohim will avenge you, and will bring you into that which He promised to your fathers" rests on the same faith that read his whole affliction as God's saving purpose.

Joshua 24:32 — *And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem... and it became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.* That at the Exodus they took up his bones and buried him with his fathers is the burial Joshua records.

Exodus 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him: for he had straitly sworn the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you; and ye shall carry up my bones away hence with you.* Joseph's charge "ye shall carry up my bones with you" is the very oath Moses kept at the Exodus.
Gen 35:24 — *The sons of Rachel; Joseph, and Benjamin.* — the two sons of Rachel set side by side, the brotherhood that drives the whole testament.

Gen 35:18 — *And it came to pass, as her soul was in departing, (for she died) that she called his name Ben-oni: but his father called him Benjamin.* — Rachel's death in birth that Benjamin mourns, "since Rachel my mother died in giving me birth."

Gen 30:24 — *And she called his name Joseph; and said, Yahuah (LORD) shall add to me another son.* — Rachel's own prayer for a second son, which the testament says Jacob also prayed, "that he might see two sons born from her."

Gen 30:22 — *And Elohim (God) remembered Rachel, and Elohim (God) hearkened to her, and opened her womb.* — the hearkened-to prayer Benjamin recalls, that his mother "prayed Yahuah with fasting twelve days, and she conceived."
Gen 37:28 — *and sold Joseph to the Ishmeelites for twenty pieces of silver: and they brought Joseph into Egypt.* — the very sale Joseph names, "they gave me to the Ishmaelites."
Gen 37:23 — *they stript Joseph out of his coat, his coat of many colours that was on him.* — the stripping Joseph recalls, "when they had stripped me of my coat."
Gen 37:31 — *And they took Joseph's coat, and killed a kid of the goats, and dipped the coat in the blood.* — the bloodied coat Benjamin describes, "they dabbled thy coat with blood and sent it."
Matt 5:8 — *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* — the pure mind that "seeth all things rightly," shielded by the fear of God.
Lev 19:18 — *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* — the neighbour-love Benjamin couples to the fear of God as the shield against Beliar.

Deut 30:16 — *to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live.* — the love-and-keep Moses set before Israel, which Benjamin repeats to his sons.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:6 — *besought our father 'that he would pray for his brethren', that 'the Lord' would not impute to them as sin.* Joseph asked his father to pray for the brothers who wronged him, which is the love of enemies Yahusha (Jesus) later commands.

Gen 50:20 — *But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good, to bring to pass, as it is this day, to save much people alive.* — the good-man's word turning his brothers' evil to salvation, the keystone of Joseph's mercy.

Gen 50:17 — *Forgive, I pray thee now, the trespass of thy brethren, and their sin; for they did unto thee evil... And Joseph wept when they spake unto him.* — the forgiveness Benjamin recalls, that Joseph asked the sin not be imputed to them.

Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs 133:8 — *a blameless one shall be delivered up for lawless men, and a sinless shall die for ungodly men.* Jacob foretells a sinless one dying for ungodly men, and Peter names the Messiah (Christ) as the just one who suffered for the unjust.

Isa 49:6 — *I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.* — the salvation reaching to the Gentiles that the prophecy names, "for the salvation of the Gentiles and of Israel."
Lev 19:18 — *thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am Yahuah (LORD).* — the love of the righteous "as his own soul" that crowns the good man's mercy.
Matt 5:7 — *Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.* — the mercy to all, even to sinners, that the good man shows.

Matt 6:22 — *The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.* — the single eye against the "dark eye" Benjamin names as the mark of the good man.
Prov 14:31 — *He that oppresseth the poor reproacheth his Maker: but he that honoureth him hath mercy on the poor.* — the mercy on the poor and compassion on the weak that marks the good man.
Rom 12:15 — *Rejoice with them that do rejoice, and weep with them that weep.* — the un-envying heart that praises the valiant and laughs not at another's good.
Rom 12:21 — *Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.* — the very overcoming Benjamin names, "by doing good he overcometh evil."
Isa 49:7 — *to him whom man despiseth, to him whom the nation abhorreth... Kings shall see and arise.* — the despised one lifted to honour, the Servant-pattern of humbled-then-glorious.

Gen 50:20 — *ye thought evil against me; but Elohim (God) meant it unto good... to save much people alive.* — Joseph humbled by betrayal yet raised to save, the example Benjamin names, "as was Joseph my brother."
1 Pet 3:9 — *Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing.* — the holy man's mercy to his reviler, that he "holdeth his peace."
Matt 5:37 — *But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.* — the single, guileless speech of the uncorrupt mind.
Ps 73:26 — *My flesh and my heart faileth: but Elohim (God) is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.* — the Lord as the good man's portion, that he covets no corruptible thing.
Jas 3:10 — *Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing. My brethren, these things ought not so to be.* — the tongue "of blessing and of cursing" the good mind refuses.
Jas 1:8 — *A double minded man is unstable in all his ways.* — the very doubleness Benjamin condemns, the mind with "two tongues" and "double sight."

1 Jn 3:15 — *Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.* — the judgment on "those who are like unto Cain in envy and hatred of brethren."

1 Jn 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* — the Cain-pattern of envy and brother-hatred the testament warns against.
Gen 4:24 — *If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, truly Lamech seventy and sevenfold.* — the very measure the testament names, "but Lamech with seventy times seven."
Gen 4:15 — *whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold.* — the sevenfold vengeance Benjamin recalls, "Cain also delivered over to seven vengeances."
Matt 5:8 — *Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see Elohim (God).* — the purity of heart on which the Spirit of God rests.

Matt 5:28 — *whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.* — the very looking the pure mind refuses, "looketh not after a woman with a view to fornication."

Jude 1:7 — *Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, and the cities about them in like manner, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh, are set forth for an example.* — the fornication of Sodom set forth as warning, exactly as Benjamin invokes it.

1 Enoch 9:8 — *And they have gone to the daughters of men upon the earth, and have slept with the women, and have defiled themselves, and revealed to them all kinds of sins.* — the wanton deeds with women Benjamin warns his sons they will renew.

1 Enoch 8:2 — *And there arose much godlessness, and they committed fornication, and they were led astray, and became corrupt in all their ways.* — the fornication Enoch foretold, which Benjamin draws from "the words of Enoch the righteous."

Ezek 37:22 — *And I will make them one nation in the land... and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.* — the twelve tribes gathered together as one, the two-house reunion.

Isa 2:2 — *And it shall come to pass in the last days, that the mountain of the LORD'S house shall be established in the top of the mountains... and all nations shall flow unto it.* — the gathering of the tribes and all the Gentiles to the house of God.

Hag 2:9 — *The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former, saith Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts): and in this place will I give peace.* — the latter temple "more glorious than the first" Benjamin foresees.
Matt 27:51 — *And, behold, the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.* — the very rending of the veil Benjamin prophesies, "the veil of the temple shall be rent."

Gal 3:13 — *Messiah (Christ) hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.* — the Anointed lifted up upon a tree, bearing the curse for the salvation Benjamin foresees.
Deut 21:23 — *for he that is hanged is accursed of Elohim (God)* — the Torah's word on the one hanged on a tree, the curse the lifted-up Lord bears.
Joel 2:28 — *I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh.* — the Spirit poured forth "as fire" and passing to the Gentiles.
1 Pet 3:19 — *By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison.* — the One who passed through Hades, the same descent into the lower parts.
Eph 4:10 — *He that descended is the same also that ascended up far above all heavens, that he might fill all things.* — "how lowly He shall be upon earth, and how glorious in heaven."

Eph 4:9 — *Now that he ascended, what is it but that he also descended first into the lower parts of the earth?* — the descent and ascent Benjamin names, "He shall ascend from Hades and shall pass from earth into heaven."
Acts 13:47 — *I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.* — the apostles' citation of the same promise, salvation to the Gentiles.

Isa 49:6 — *I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.* — the salvation revealed "to all Gentiles" that the fathers' charge waits for.

Deut 30:16 — *to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live.* — the very keeping Benjamin leaves "instead of inheritance."
Ezek 37:12 — *Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves.* — the raising of Israel and her fathers from the grave.
Matt 19:28 — *ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* — the twelve set "each one over our tribe," as Benjamin foresees.

Matt 22:32 — *I am the Elohim (God) of Abraham, and the Elohim (God) of Isaac, and the Elohim (God) of Jacob? Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living.* — the fathers who live to God, who Benjamin sees "rising on the right hand in gladness."

Rev 20:12 — *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God)... and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* — all men risen and judged, as Benjamin foresees.

John 5:29 — *And shall come forth; they that have done good, unto the resurrection of life; and they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of damnation.* — the two resurrections, to glory and to shame.

Dan 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* — the very words behind "all men shall rise, some unto glory and some unto shame."
Rom 11:25 — *blindness in part is happened to Yashar'el (Israel), until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.* — the chosen Gentiles brought in to convict and gather Israel.

Acts 13:46 — *It was necessary that the word of Elohim (God) should first have been spoken to you: but seeing ye put it from you... lo, we turn to the Gentiles.* — judgment of Israel first, then the turning to the Gentiles.
Rom 11:11 — *through their fall salvation is come unto the Gentiles, for to provoke them to jealousy.* — Israel convicted and provoked through the believing Gentiles, exactly as Benjamin foresees.

Ezek 37:21 — *Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen... and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land.* — the ingathering that makes the dispersed dwell securely again.

Deut 30:4 — *from thence will Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) gather thee, and from thence will he fetch thee.* — the gathering of "all Yashar'el (Israel) shall be gathered unto Yahuah (Lord)" Benjamin foresees.
Gen 49:27 — *Benjamin shall ravin as a wolf: in the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.* — the very wolf Benjamin says he shall "no longer be called."
Acts 13:47 — *I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles.* — the beloved "enlightening the Gentiles" in their synagogues, as Benjamin foresees.
Rom 11:1 — *For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.* — the apostle naming his own tribe, the beloved arisen in the latter days.
Phil 3:5 — *of the stock of Yashar'el (Israel), of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews.* — Paul, the man of Benjamin's seed, the beloved who enlightened the Gentiles.

Deut 33:12 — *The beloved of Yahuah (LORD) shall dwell in safety by him; and Yahuah (LORD) shall cover him all the day long.* — the "one beloved of Yahuah" of Benjamin's tribe, Moses' own blessing on Benjamin.

Josh 24:32 — *And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Yashar'el (Israel) brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem.* — the fathers' bones at last brought into the land, the oath fulfilled.
Exod 13:19 — *And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him.* — the keeping of the fathers' oath, the bones carried up out of Egypt as Benjamin commands.

Gen 50:25 — *And Joseph took an oath of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), saying, Elohim (God) will surely visit you, and ye shall carry up my bones from hence.* — the same oath Benjamin lays on his sons, "carry up my bones out of Egypt."

Deuteronomy 30:14 — *But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it.* The Law that disciplines the reason is no far-off counsel but the word already set in heart and mouth to do.

Proverbs 16:32 — *He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.* Reason "lord over" rage and over the passions opposed to manliness is Solomon's man who rules his spirit.

Psalm 19:8 — *The statutes of Yahuah (LORD) are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of Yahuah (LORD) is pure, enlightening the eyes.* Wisdom "manifested under the forms of judgement and justice" is the right, heart-rejoicing statute of Yahuah.

Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple.* The Law converting the soul IS the "culture acquired under the Law" that makes the simple wise.

Romans 7:25 — *So then with the mind I myself serve the law of Elohim (God); but with the flesh the law of sin.* Self-control "asserts its authority over the passions" by serving the Law with the mind — Paul's very division.

Romans 7:23 — *But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which is in my members.* The mind's law against the passions of the members is the same contest 4 Maccabees frames as Reason over the passions.
Romans 7:22 — *For I delight in the law of Elohim (God) after the inward man:* the inward delight in the Law is exactly the inner Reason 4 Maccabees sets over the passions.
Romans 7:12 — *Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.* The "culture acquired under the Law" that schools the reason is the very Torah Paul calls holy, just and good.

Proverbs 16:32 — *He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city.* The reason that masters the passions is the spirit-ruler Solomon crowns above the conqueror.

Galatians 5:24 — *And they that are Messiah's (Christ’s) have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts.* The appetites "checked and inhibited by the temperate mind... bridle of Reason" are the affections and lusts Messiah's people crucify.
Galatians 5:23 — *Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.* The temperance through which "Reason becomes supreme over the passions" is named among the very fruit of the Spirit.

Galatians 5:17 — *For the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh: and these are contrary the one to the other: so that ye cannot do the things that ye would.* The "two comprehensive sources, namely, pleasure and pain" warred against by Reason mirror Paul's flesh contrary to the Spirit.

Galatians 5:16 — *This I say then, Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.* Reason as "guide of the virtues" and "master of the passions" is Paul's walk in the Spirit not fulfilling the flesh's lust.

Daniel 1:8 — *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king’s meat, nor with the wine which he drank: therefore he requested of the prince of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.* Daniel's purposed refusal in the king's court is the very pattern of Reason repressing the appetite "under the Law."

Deuteronomy 14:8 — *And the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase.* The swine the brothers refuse is the swine Moses twice forbids — the clean/unclean law stands.
Deuteronomy 14:3 — *Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.* Moses' plain charge underwrites the abstinence from "meats of every description forbidden to us under the Law."

Leviticus 11:44 — *For I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.* The dietary discipline is grounded in holiness unto Yahuah, the Creator-Lawgiver — the very ground the martyrs will plead.

Leviticus 11:8 — *Of their flesh shall ye not eat, and their carcase shall ye not touch; they are unclean to you.* To "abstain through the predominance of Reason" from meats "forbidden to us under the Law" is simply to keep this command.

Leviticus 11:7 — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you.* The "forbidden meats" repressed by Reason are the swine the Lawgiver declared unclean.

Deuteronomy 5:21 — *Neither shalt thou desire thy neighbour's wife, neither shalt thou covet thy neighbour's house, his field, or his manservant, or his maidservant, his ox, or his ass, or any thing that is thy neighbour's.* Moses' second giving of the Tenth Word is the same command 4 Maccabees cites — "when the Law orders us not to covet."

Exodus 20:17 — *Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.* This is the Tenth Word the writer quotes verbatim as the Law that schools Reason to control covetous desire.

Genesis 39:12 — *And she caught him by his garment, saying, Lie with me: and he left his garment in her hand, and fled, and got him out.* Joseph fleeing the temptation is the deed 4 Maccabees praises as Reason mastering the passion.

Genesis 39:9 — *There is none greater in this house than I; neither hath he kept back any thing from me but thee, because thou art his wife: how then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against Elohim (God)?* Joseph's refusal — "sin against Elohim" — is the carnal impulse quenched at the age "when physical desire is strong."

Genesis 39:7 — *And it came to pass after these things, that his master's wife cast her eyes upon Joseph; and she said, Lie with me.* This is the very temptation the "virtuous Joseph" checked by his Reason.

Deuteronomy 24:19 — *When thou cuttest down thine harvest in thy field, and hast forgot a sheaf in the field, thou shalt not go again to fetch it: it shall be for the stranger, for the fatherless, and for the widow: that Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) may bless thee in all the work of thine hands.* Moses' law of the forgotten sheaf is the same harvest-charity the Law presses on the grasping man through Reason.

Leviticus 19:10 — *And thou shalt not glean thy vineyard, neither shalt thou gather every grape of thy vineyard; thou shalt leave them for the poor and stranger: I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God).* The parsimonious man who refrains from "picking the last grapes from his vineyards" is keeping this command for the poor and stranger.

Leviticus 19:9 — *And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not wholly reap the corners of thy field, neither shalt thou gather the gleanings of thy harvest.* To be one who "refrains from gleaning his stubbles" is to obey the law of the corners and the gleanings left for the poor.

Deuteronomy 15:2 — *And this is the manner of the release: Every creditor that lendeth ought unto his neighbour shall release it; he shall not exact it of his neighbour, or of his brother; because it is called the LORD'S release.* The miser "overruled by the Law" to lend without interest and cancel the debt is keeping the Lord's release.
Deuteronomy 15:1 — *At the end of every seven years thou shalt make a release.* The "seventh-year periods" at which a man "cancels the debt" is this very statute of release.

Genesis 34:25 — *And it came to pass on the third day, when they were sore, that two of the sons of Jacob, Simeon and Levi, Dinah's brethren, took each man his sword, and came upon the city boldly, and slew all the males.* The "unreasoning slaughter of the tribe of the Shechemites" is this deed Jacob's curse condemns.

Genesis 49:7 — *Cursed be their anger, for it was fierce; and their wrath, for it was cruel: I will divide them in Jacob, and scatter them in Yashar'el (Israel).* This is the very curse the writer quotes — "Accursed be their anger!" — proof that unreasoning rage is condemned by the Law.
Genesis 49:5 — *Simeon and Levi are brethren; instruments of cruelty are in their habitations.* This is the censure 4 Maccabees recalls as Jacob blaming the houses of Simeon and Levi.

Numbers 16:12 — *And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab: which said, We will not come up.* Their open defiance is precisely the provocation Moses met by governing his anger, not by surrendering to it.

Numbers 16:2 — *And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown.* This rising against Moses is the occasion at which he "governed his anger by his Reason" rather than giving free course to wrath.

Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.* The Law given "to the mind" so a man may reign over a temperate and just kingdom is the choice of life Moses sets before Israel.

Genesis 2:8 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) planted a garden eastward in Eden; and there he put the man whom he had formed.* The Creator who "set the mind on a throne... to be his sacred guide" placed the man he formed under his charge in Eden.

Genesis 2:7 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.* "The day when Elohim created man" and "implanted in him his passions" is the very forming Moses records.

1 Chronicles 11:19 — *shall I drink the blood of these men that have put their lives in jeopardy?... Therefore he would not drink it* — the same reasoning that the temperate mind opposed to the burning desire.
1 Chronicles 11:18 — *David would not drink of it, but poured it out to Yahuah (LORD)* — the Chronicler's parallel witness to the offering poured out rather than drunk.

2 Samuel 23:15 — *And David longed, and said, Oh that one would give me drink of the water of the well of Beth-lehem, which is by the gate!* — the intense thirst and irrational craving the king could not slake.

2 Samuel 23:17 — *is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it* — David reckoning the water as blood, the danger to his soul that bridled his desire.

2 Samuel 23:16 — *the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Beth-lehem... and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto Yahuah (LORD)* — the very deed the writer cites of the two warriors and the poured-out draught.
Psalm 19:11 — *Moreover by them is thy servant warned: and in keeping of them there is great reward* — the Torah-disciplined mind that wrestles victoriously against the swaying of malevolence.

Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple* — the Law is the culture in which Reason becomes master over the passions of the body.
Proverbs 16:32 — *He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city* — Reason as the antagonist that masters anger and desire.

2 Maccabees 3:33 — *Now as the high priest was making an atonement, the same young men in the same clothing appeared and stood beside Heliodorus, saying, Give Onias the high priest great thanks, insomuch as for his sake Yahuah (God) has granted you life.* Onias the high priest interceding so the spoiler is granted his life is the same mercy the sibling book records at the same altar.

2 Maccabees 3:29 — *For he by the hand of Yahuah (God) was cast down, and lay speechless without all hope of life.* Apollonius fallen half-dead with hands stretched to heaven matches the king's agent cast down speechless by the hand of Elohim.

2 Maccabees 3:25 — *For there appeared to them an horse with a terrible rider upon him, and adorned with a very fair covering, and he ran fiercely, and struck at Heliodorus with his forefeet, and it seemed that he that sat upon the horse had complete harness of gold.* The heavenly horsemen flashing from heaven who terrify the raiders are the same apparition the sibling book describes striking the king's man down.

2 Maccabees 3:15 — *But the priests, prostrating themselves before the altar in their priests' vestments, called to heaven upon him that made a law concerning things given to be kept, that they should safely be preserved for such as had committed them to be kept.* As in 4 Maccabees the priests, women, and children besought Elohim, here the priests prostrate and cry to heaven over the same violated trust.

2 Maccabees 3:7 — *Now when Apollonius came to the king, and had shewed him of the money of which he was told, the king chose out Heliodorus his treasurer, and sent him with a commandment to bring him the foresaid money.* The same Apollonius carries word to the king and the royal agent is dispatched to seize the deposits.

2 Maccabees 3:6 — *And told him that the treasury in Jerusalem was full of infinite sums of money, so that the multitude of their riches, which did not pertain to the account of the sacrifices, was innumerable, and that it was possible to bring all into the king's hand.* The sibling book records the identical boast of the temple treasury that sets the raid in motion.

Daniel 11:33 — *And they that understand among the people shall instruct many: yet they shall fall by the sword, and by flame, by captivity, and by spoil, many days.* The martyrdoms this whole book will recount are the falling by sword and flame Daniel foretold of the wise under this king.

Daniel 11:32 — *And such as do wickedly against the covenant shall he corrupt by flatteries: but the people that do know their Elohim (God) shall be strong, and do exploits.* The death-decree against living after the Law and the people's constancy under it are Daniel's covenant-breakers corrupted while the faithful stay strong.

Daniel 11:31 — *And arms shall stand on his part, and they shall pollute the sanctuary of strength, and shall take away the daily sacrifice, and they shall place the abomination that maketh desolate.* The king who abolishes the service of the temple is Daniel's profaner of the sanctuary who takes away the daily sacrifice.

Daniel 11:22 — *And with the arms of a flood shall they be overflown from before him, and shall be broken; yea, also the prince of the covenant.* Antiochus deposing Onias the high priest answers Daniel's breaking of the prince of the covenant.

Daniel 11:21 — *And in his estate shall stand up a vile person, to whom they shall not give the honour of the kingdom: but he shall come in peaceably, and obtain the kingdom by flatteries.* The overweening Antiochus who succeeds Seleucus is the vile person Daniel foresaw seizing the kingdom by flattery.

2 Maccabees 5:11 — *Now when this that was done came to the king's ear, he thought that Judea had revolted: whereupon removing out of Egypt in a furious mind, he took the city by force of arms.* The plundering of the city before the decrees is the same furious return from Egypt and storming of Jerusalem the other sibling book records.

1 Maccabees 1:62 — *Howbeit many in Yashar'el (Israel) were fully resolved and confirmed in themselves not to eat any unclean thing.* The men tortured to eat unclean meats answer the many resolved not to eat any unclean thing — the dietary law of Leviticus standing under threat of death.

1 Maccabees 1:60 — *At which time according to the commandment they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.* The women flung from the rocks for circumcising their sons are the same mothers slain for the covenant in the sibling chronicle.

1 Maccabees 1:50 — *And whoever would not do according to the commandment of the king, he said, he should die.* The death-penalty decree against living after the Law of the fathers is the king's edict the sibling book records.

1 Maccabees 1:20 — *And after that Antiochus had struck Egypt, he returned again in the hundred forty and third year, and went up against Yashar'el (Israel) and Jerusalem with a great multitude.* The same return from Egypt and march on Jerusalem that 4 Maccabees compresses into Antiochus marching back against the city.

James 2:10 — *For whosoever shall keep the whole law, and yet offend in one point, he is guilty of all* — the apostle's echo of Eleazar's rule that transgression in small things or great is equally heinous.

Psalm 19:7 — *The law of Yahuah (LORD) is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of Yahuah (LORD) is sure, making wise the simple* — the perfect Law that may not be despised in small things or great.
Deuteronomy 30:20 — *that thou mayest love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God)... for he is thy life, and the length of thy days* — the Law held as life itself, the necessity Eleazar owns above all.
Deuteronomy 30:14 — *But the word is very nigh unto thee, in thy mouth, and in thy heart, that thou mayest do it* — the doable, owned Law that Eleazar deems it right never to transgress.

Deuteronomy 30:11 — *For this commandment which I command thee this day, it is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off* — the Law made the Law of the people, the obedience Eleazar will not put off.

Romans 7:12 — *Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good* — Paul's verdict on the very Law that teaches self-control, justice, and righteousness, against the charge that it is contrary to reason.

Proverbs 16:32 — *He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city* — the self-control and mastery over the passions which Eleazar attributes to the Law's training.
Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me* — the first word of the Law, the worship of the only Elohim that Eleazar says the Law teaches.

Deuteronomy 10:12 — *what doth Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) require of thee, but to fear Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in all his ways, and to love him, and to serve Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thy heart* — the Law's own teaching of reverent worship of the only Elohim.

2 Maccabees 6:20 — *As it behoved them to come, that are resolute to stand out against such things, as are not lawful for love of life to be tasted* — what is not lawful is not to be tasted even to save life, the martyr's exact resolve (self-link).

2 Maccabees 6:19 — *he, choosing rather to die gloriously, than to live stained with such an abomination, spit it forth, and came of his own accord to the torment* — Eleazar refusing the unlawful meat unto death, the same event told twice (self-link).

2 Maccabees 6:18 — *Eleazar, one of the principal scribes, an aged man, and of a well favoured countenance, was constrained to open his mouth, and to eat swine's flesh* — the same Eleazar, the same swine, the sibling martyrology (self-link).

Daniel 1:8 — *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat... that he might not defile himself* — the same resolve under a pagan court, refusing the king's defiling table.

Deuteronomy 14:8 — *And the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase* — the same swine-prohibition repeated, the contrary meat the Lawgiver forbids.
Deuteronomy 14:3 — *Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing* — Moses' summary of the dietary law, the abomination Eleazar will not touch.

Leviticus 11:45 — *For I am Yahuah (LORD) that bringeth you up out of the land of Egypt, to be your Elohim (God): ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy* — the Maker who redeemed the people and gave the law convenient for their souls.

Leviticus 11:44 — *I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing* — the holiness for which the dietary law is given, that none defile himself.
Leviticus 11:8 — *Of their flesh shall ye not eat, and their carcase shall ye not touch; they are unclean to you* — the standing prohibition that makes swine's flesh unclean meat to the martyr.

Leviticus 11:7 — *And the swine, though he divide the hoof, and be clovenfooted, yet he cheweth not the cud; he is unclean to you* — the Creator-Lawgiver's own statute forbidding the very flesh Eleazar refuses.

Exodus 20:5 — *Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) am a jealous Elohim (God)* — the jealous Elohim whose worship leaves no room for the idol's defiling table.

Exodus 20:4 — *Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath* — the prohibition of idols behind which stands the ban on things offered to them.
Exodus 20:3 — *Thou shalt have no other gods before me* — the first word of the Law that forbids the idol-meat Antiochus would force upon the Hebrews.

Romans 9:8 — *the children of the flesh, these are not the children of Elohim (God): but the children of the promise are counted for the seed* — sonship to Abraham reckoned by promise, the faith Eleazar would not counterfeit.

Romans 9:7 — *Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called* — the seed of promise, the line Eleazar bids die nobly for righteousness' sake.
Galatians 3:7 — *Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham* — the sons of Abraham defined by the same faith that made Eleazar choose death over impiety.

Genesis 17:8 — *I will give unto thee, and to thy seed after thee, the land... for an everlasting possession; and I will be their Elohim (God)* — the inheritance of Abraham's seed, the patrimony the martyr will not betray.

Genesis 17:7 — *And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a Elohim (God) unto thee, and to thy seed after thee* — the everlasting covenant that makes Eleazar a son of Abraham unwilling to forfeit it.

2 Maccabees 7:37 — *I, as my brothers, offer up my body and life for the laws of our fathers* — the sibling martyrology, the same Eleazar and brothers refusing the swine for the laws of their fathers (self-link).

Daniel 1:8 — *But Daniel purposed in his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the king's meat... that he might not defile himself* — the same resolve under a pagan court, refusing the king's defiling table.

Deuteronomy 14:8 — *the swine, because it divideth the hoof, yet cheweth not the cud, it is unclean unto you: ye shall not eat of their flesh, nor touch their dead carcase* — Moses' repetition of the same prohibition the martyr keeps unto death.

Leviticus 11:44 — *I am Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God): ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy* — the holiness that forbids defilement, the truth Eleazar guarded in lawful guise unto old age.
Leviticus 11:8 — *Of their flesh shall ye not eat, and their carcase shall ye not touch; they are unclean to you* — the standing command Eleazar will not break even to escape the fire.

Elohim (God) is not the Elohim (God) of the dead, but of the living* — the very logic the mother voices: the patriarchs live unto Elohim, the Messiah proving the resurrection from the same three names.

Romans 12:1 — *that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto Elohim (God), which is your reasonable service* — the debt the mother names, *ye owe it to Elohim to endure,* the body offered up for his sake.

Daniel 12:3 — *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* — the very figure of the *seven starlike sons* set in heaven, the wise shining like stars in the resurrection.

Matthew 13:43 — *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear* — the righteous shining in the Father's kingdom, the same starlike glory of the martyred sons.

Philippians 2:15 — *That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of Elohim, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world* — the sons of Elohim shining as lights amid a perverse nation, as the mother lit the path of her sons unto righteousness.

1 Corinthians 15:53 — *For this corruptible must put on incorruption, and this mortal must put on immortality* — the *incorruption in everlasting life* set before the martyrs as their prize of victory.

1 Corinthians 15:54 — *So when this corruptible shall have put on incorruption... then shall be brought to pass the saying that is written, Death is swallowed up in victory* — the victory in incorruption the endurance of the martyrs won.

Daniel 12:2 — *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* — the awaking to *everlasting life,* the resurrection hope behind the martyrs' prize.
2 Timothy 4:7 — *I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith* — the same athlete's contest finished in faithfulness, the race the martyrs ran unto death.

2 Timothy 4:8 — *Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which Yahusha (Lord), the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.* — the crown of righteousness given by the Judge, as righteousness *gave the crown to her athletes.*

James 1:12 — *Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which Yahuah hath promised to them that love him* — the crown of life for the tried and enduring, exactly the martyrs' reward through endurance.
Revelation 2:10 — *be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life* — faithfulness unto death crowned with life, the very wreath given to the athletes of the true Law.

1 Corinthians 9:24 — *Know ye not that they which run in a race run all, but one receiveth the prize? So run, that ye may obtain* — the athletic figure Paul shares, the race the martyrs ran to obtain the prize.

1 Corinthians 9:25 — *And every man that striveth for the mastery is temperate in all things. Now they do it to obtain a corruptible crown; but we an incorruptible* — the incorruptible crown of the true athletes, against the perishing wreath of the games.

Revelation 7:9 — *a great multitude, which no man could number... stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palms in their hands* — the throng standing before the throne, where the martyrs now *stand beside the throne of Elohim.*

Revelation 7:14 — *These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb* — those brought through great tribulation to the throne, the company of the enduring martyrs.

Revelation 7:15 — *Therefore are they before the throne of Elohim, and serve him day and night in his temple: and he that sitteth on the throne shall dwell among them* — the redeemed *before the throne of Elohim,* the very honour the martyrs receive.

Revelation 20:4 — *I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness... and they lived and reigned with Messiah a thousand years* — the souls of the slain witnesses who *live the blessed age,* reigning before the throne.
Daniel 7:9 — *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit... his throne was like the fiery flame* — the throne of glory beside which the sanctified now stand.

Daniel 7:10 — *thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened* — the heavenly host standing before the throne, the court the martyrs are gathered into.

Deuteronomy 33:3 — *Yea, he loved the people; all his saints are in thy hand: and they sat down at thy feet; every one shall receive of thy words* — Moses' word the writer cites, the sanctified ones *under thy hands.*

Isaiah 53:5 — *But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed* — the Suffering Servant whose wounded blood truly delivers, which the martyrs' death only pointed toward.

Isaiah 53:10 — *when thou shalt make his soul an offering for sin, he shall see his seed, he shall prolong his days* — the soul given as an offering for sin, the propitiation the martyrs' death dimly figures but cannot accomplish.

Isaiah 53:11 — *by his knowledge shall my righteous servant justify many; for he shall bear their iniquities* — the righteous Servant bearing the iniquities of the many, the true ransom the type points toward.

Isaiah 53:12 — *he hath poured out his soul unto death... and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors* — the One who pours out his soul and bears the nation's sin, the one whom the martyrs' blood foreshadows.

Daniel 9:24 — *to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness* — the reconciliation appointed, which no martyr's blood but only the Anointed brings to pass.

Romans 3:25 — *Whom Elohim hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins* — the true propitiation that fulfils the type; the martyrs' *propitiation of their death* foreshadows, the Messiah's effects.

Hebrews 9:14 — *the blood of Messiah, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without spot to Elohim, purge your conscience from dead works* — the blood that truly cleanses the people, which the martyrs' blood only pointed toward.

Hebrews 11:35 — *others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection* — the NT's own allusion to this very martyrdom, the tortured who looked beyond death to the better resurrection.

Genesis 2:21 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam, and he slept: and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh instead thereof* — the rib the mother says she kept guard over, the very building-block of woman.

Genesis 2:22 — *And the rib, which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had taken from man, made he a woman, and brought her unto the man* — the rib *builded into Eve,* the womanhood the mother guarded in purity.

Genesis 2:23 — *This is now bone of my bones, and flesh of my flesh: she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man* — the first marriage the mother honours, having lived with her husband all the days of her youth.

Genesis 3:1 — *Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) had made* — the *false, beguiling Serpent* whose subtilty the mother says never sullied her maidenhood.
Genesis 3:4 — *And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die* — the deceiver's lie that beguiled the first Eve, which this daughter of Eve refused.

Genesis 3:6 — *and when the woman saw that the tree was good for food... she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband* — the fall the mother did not repeat; the Serpent could not *sully the purity of my maidenhood.*

Genesis 4:8 — *and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him* — *Abel who was slain by Cain,* the first righteous martyr the father set before his sons.

Genesis 22:9 — *and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood* — *Isaac who was offered as a burnt-offering,* the Akedah that is the martyrs' own charter.

Genesis 22:13 — *and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son* — the burnt-offering provided in Isaac's stead, the binding the father read to his children.

Genesis 39:20 — *And Joseph's master took him, and put him into the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were bound: and he was there in the prison* — *Joseph in the prison,* the righteous one wrongly chained yet kept by Yahuah.

Numbers 25:11 — *Phinehas... hath turned my wrath away from the children of Yashar'el (Israel), while he was zealous for my sake among them* — *Phineas, the zealous priest,* whose zeal for the Law the father held up to his sons.

Numbers 25:13 — *and he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his Elohim (God)* — the everlasting covenant given for zeal, the reward of the priest the father named.
Daniel 3:25 — *Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt* — the song of *Ananias, Azarias, and Mishael in the fire,* the three children unhurt in the furnace.

Daniel 3:27 — *upon whose bodies the fire had no power, nor was an hair of their head singed... nor the smell of fire had passed on them* — the deliverance the father taught, the fire that could not touch the faithful three.

Song of the Three Holy Children 1:66 — *O Ananias, Azarias, and Misael, bless you Yahuah (God)... for he has delivered us... out of the midst of the fire* — the very song the father *taught you,* sung by the three in the furnace (self-link).

Daniel 6:22 — *My Elohim (God) hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me* — *Daniel in the den of lions,* whom the father *glorified... and blessed,* preserved among the beasts.

Daniel 6:23 — *So Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no manner of hurt was found upon him, because he believed in his Elohim (God)* — Daniel delivered unhurt, the faith the father set before the seven sons.

Isaiah 43:2 — *when thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned; neither shall the flame kindle upon thee* — the saying of Isaiah the father quoted, the promise the three children and the martyrs leaned upon.
Psalm 34:19 — *Many are the afflictions of the righteous: but Yahuah (LORD) delivereth him out of them all* — the words of David the father sang, the just man afflicted yet always delivered.

Proverbs 3:18 — *She is a tree of life to them that lay hold upon her: and happy is every one that retaineth her* — the proverb of Solomon the father quoted, wisdom-and-Law the tree of life for them that do His will.

Ezekiel 37:3 — *Son of Adam, can these bones live? And I answered, O Yahuah (Lord) GOD, thou knowest* — *Shall these dry bones live?* the resurrection-question the father confirmed, the hope of the whole house of Yashar'el.

Deuteronomy 32:39 — *I kill, and I make alive; I wound, and I heal: neither is there any that can deliver out of my hand* — the song of Moses the father remembered, *I will slay and I will make alive,* the Author of death and resurrection.

Deuteronomy 30:19 — *I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* — the life Moses set before Yashar'el, *this is your life,* chosen by the sons in dying for the Law.
Deuteronomy 30:20 — *for he is thy life, and the length of thy days* — *this is your life and the blessedness of your days,* the very phrase the father drew from Moses' song.

Hebrews 11:35 — *and others were tortured, not accepting deliverance; that they might obtain a better resurrection* — the NT's own allusion to this very martyrdom; the sons gathered to their fathers awaited the better resurrection.
Hebrews 11:39 — *and these all, having obtained a good report through faith, received not the promise* — the cloud of witnesses, the sons of Abraham gathered to the place of their ancestors in hope.

Hebrews 11:40 — *Elohim (God) having provided some better thing for us, that they without us should not be made perfect* — the better thing reserved, the immortal souls the martyrs received from Elohim awaiting consummation.

Luke 16:22 — *and it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom* — *gathered together unto the place of their ancestors,* the faithful received to Abraham among the fathers.

Daniel 12:2 — *and many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life* — the resurrection of the just, the *pure and immortal souls* the sons of Abraham received from Elohim.

Daniel 12:3 — *and they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* — the starlike glory of the victorious mother and her sons, set among the everlasting righteous.

Daniel 12:1 — *and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book* — the day of deliverance and judgement, when the wretch is pursued but the faithful are gathered.

Jubilees 4:1 — *And in the third week in the second jubilee she gave birth to Cain, and in the fourth she gave birth to Abel, and in the fifth she gave birth to her daughter ’Âwân.* The book of the fathers keeps the same two births, Cain then Abel, that Adam & Eve sets at its head.

Genesis 4:2 — *And she again bare his brother Abel. And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.* The two sons Eve bears in Adam and Eve 1:1, Cain and Abel, are the same pair Moses names in their birth order.

Genesis 4:1 — *And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from Yahuah (LORD).* The opening of Adam & Eve, the man knowing his wife after the expulsion, is the very verse with which Moses begins the generations of Adam.

Matthew 23:35 — *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.* The Messiah dates the shed blood of the righteous from this first murder of Abel.

1 John 3:12 — *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.* The hand of Cain in Adam and Eve 3:1 is the very fratricide John sets as the warning against hatred.

Hebrews 11:4 — *By faith Abel offered unto Elohim (God) a more excellent sacrifice than Cain, by which he obtained witness that he was righteous, Elohim (God) testifying of his gifts: and by it he being dead yet speaketh.* The murdered Abel of Adam and Eve 3:1 is the righteous one whose blood still speaks.

Genesis 4:10 — *And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother's blood crieth unto me from the ground.* The blood Eve sees poured out in her dream is the blood that cries from the ground in Moses' account.

Genesis 4:8 — *And Cain talked with Abel his brother: and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.* Abel found murdered by his brother's hand in Adam and Eve 3:1 is the slaying Moses records in the field.

Luke 3:38 — *Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* The son given in Abel's place stands in the Messiah's own genealogy, the line from Adam preserved through Seth.

Genesis 4:26 — *And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of Yahuah (LORD).* Adam's resolve to give glory and sacrifice to Elohim through the new son is the very calling on the Name that returns with Seth's line.

Genesis 5:3 — *And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.* The Seth born to Adam in Adam and Eve 4:1 is the son begotten in Adam's own likeness who heads the book of the generations.

Genesis 4:25 — *And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For Elohim (God), said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel, whom Cain slew.* Adam's word in Adam and Eve 4:1, a son in place of Abel whom Cain slew, is Moses' account verbatim of the appointed seed.

Hebrews 9:27 — *And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.* The sickness that falls on Adam before he dies is the once-appointed death that came upon him and passed to all his seed.

Genesis 5:5 — *And all the days that Adam lived were nine hundred and thirty years: and he died.* The nine hundred and thirty years and the sickness unto death in Adam and Eve 5:1 are the exact span Moses sets down for the first man.

Genesis 3:3 — *But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, Elohim (God) hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.* The charge Adam recalls is the same one Eve repeated to the serpent before she ate.

Genesis 2:17 — *But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.* The one tree forbidden and the death through it in Adam and Eve 7:1 are the single command and its sentence Moses set down.

Genesis 2:16 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat.* Adam's words, that he was given power to eat of every tree, are Moses' grant of the whole garden but for one.

Psalms 139:12 — *Yea, the darkness hideth not from thee; but the night shineth as the day: the darkness and the light are both alike to thee.* The house cannot hide from its builder, says Adam and Eve 8:1; no darkness hides the creature from the Maker, says the psalm.

Psalms 139:7 — *Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?* Adam's hiding face and the maker's question, can the house hide from its builder, are answered by the psalmist: there is no fleeing the presence of the One who formed us.

Genesis 3:9 — *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?* The terrible call "Adam, where art thou" in Adam and Eve 8:1 is the very word Moses records first after the Fall.

Genesis 3:8 — *And they heard the voice of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) amongst the trees of the garden.* Yahuah coming into paradise and the man hiding in Adam and Eve 8:1 is Moses' scene of the voice in the garden.

Romans 5:12 — *Wherefore, as by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin; and so death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned.* The sorrow and death come upon Adam by Eve's own account are the sin and death the apostle traces to the one man, passing upon all.

Genesis 3:19 — *In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.* The trouble that beset Adam ends in the return to dust Moses pronounced over the first man.

Genesis 3:17 — *And unto Adam he said, Because thou hast hearkened unto the voice of thy wife, and hast eaten of the tree, of which I commanded thee, saying, Thou shalt not eat of it: cursed is the ground for thy sake; in sorrow shalt thou eat of it all the days of thy life.* Adam's distress and toils in Adam and Eve 9:1 are the sorrow Moses laid on the man for hearkening to his wife.

Genesis 3:16 — *Unto the woman he said, I will greatly multiply thy sorrow and thy conception; in sorrow thou shalt bring forth children; and thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.* Eve's word that the trouble is on her account reaches for the sorrow Moses appointed the woman at the Fall.
